In this way, it should be understood by one who sees distinctions.

Evaṃ nānānayehi dhammavibhattiṃ dassetvā idāni bhūmivibhattiṃ padaṭṭhānavibhattiñca vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “dassanabhūmī”tiādimāha. Tattha dassanabhūmīti paṭhamamaggo. Yasmā pana paṭhamamaggakkhaṇe ariyasāvako sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamanto nāma hoti, tato paraṃ okkanto[V 0.0240], tasmā “dassanabhūmi niyāmāvakkantiyā padaṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Kiñcāpi heṭṭhimo heṭṭhimo maggo upariuparimaggādhigamassa kāraṇaṃ hoti, sakkāyadiṭṭhiādīni appahāya kāmarāgabyāpādādippahānassa asakkuṇeyyattā. Tathāpi ariyamaggo attano phalassa visesakāraṇaṃ āsannakāraṇañcāti dassetuṃ “bhāvanābhūmi [M 0.0114] uttarikānaṃ phalānaṃ pattiyā padaṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Sukhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā ñāṇuttarassa tathāvidhapaccayasamāyoge ca hotīti sā vipassanāya padaṭṭhānanti vuttā. Itarā pana tissopi paṭipadā samathaṃ āvahanti eva. Tāsu sabbamudutāya dassitāya sesāpi dassitā evāti āha – “dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā samathassa padaṭṭhāna”nti.

Having thus shown the classification of phenomena in various ways, now, in order to classify and show the classification of stages and the classification of proximate causes, he said, 'The stage of vision,' etc. Therein, 'the stage of vision' is the first path. And because at the moment of the first path, the noble disciple is one who is entering the fixed course of rightness, and after that has entered, therefore it is said: 'The stage of vision is the proximate cause for entry into the fixed course.' Although each lower path is a cause for the attainment of each higher path—because without having abandoned identity-view and so forth, it is impossible to abandon sensual desire, ill-will, and the like—nevertheless, to show that the noble path is a special cause and a proximate cause for its own fruit, it is said: 'The stage of development is the proximate cause for the attainment of the subsequent fruits.' The pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge occurs for one with superior knowledge and when there is a conjunction of such conditions; therefore, it is said to be the proximate cause for insight. The other three practices, however, certainly bring about serenity. Among them, when the most inferior of all is shown, the rest are also considered shown. Therefore, he said: 'The painful practice with slow direct knowledge is the proximate cause for serenity.'

Dānamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthūti dānameva dānamayaṃ, pujjaphalanibbattanaṭṭhena puññaṃ, tadeva kattabbato kiriyā, payogasampattiyādīnaṃ adhiṭṭhānabhāvato vatthu cāti dānamayapuññakiriyavatthu. Paratoghosassāti dhammassavanassa. Sādhāraṇanti na bījaṃ viya aṅkurassa, dassanabhūmiādayo viya vā niyāmāvakkantiādīnaṃ āveṇikaṃ, atha kho sādhāraṇaṃ, tadaññakāraṇehipi paratoghosassa pavattanatoti adhippāyo. Tattha keci dāyakassa dānānumodanaṃ āciṇṇanti dānaṃ paratoghosassa kāraṇanti vadanti. Dāyako pana dakkhiṇāvisuddhiṃ ākaṅkhanto dānasīlādiguṇavisesānaṃ savane yuttappayutto hotīti dānaṃ dhammassavanassa kāraṇaṃ vuttaṃ.

'The basis of meritorious action consisting of giving' (dānamayapuññakiriyavatthu) means: giving itself is 'consisting of giving' (dānamaya); it is 'merit' (puñña) because it produces a worthy fruit; that itself, because it is to be done, is 'action' (kiriyā); and because it is the foundation for the accomplishment of the undertaking and so forth, it is a 'basis' (vatthu). Thus it is 'the basis of meritorious action consisting of giving.' 'Of the voice from another' means of hearing the Dhamma. 'Common' means it is not a specific cause like a seed for a sprout, or like the stage of vision and so forth for the entry into the fixed course and so forth; rather, it is a common cause. The meaning is that the voice from another also occurs due to causes other than that. Therein, some say that because giving appreciation for the gift to the donor is customary, giving is a cause for the voice from another. However, the donor, desiring the purity of the offering, is diligently engaged in hearing of the special qualities of giving, virtue, and so forth; therefore, giving is said to be a cause of hearing the Dhamma.

Sīlasampanno vippaṭisārābhāvena samāhito dhammacintāsamattho hotīti sīlaṃ cintāmayañāṇassa kāraṇanti āha “sīlamaya”ntiādi. Bhāvanāmayanti samathasaṅkhātaṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ. Bhāvanāmayiyāti uparijhānasaṅkhātāya vipassanāsaṅkhātāya ca bhāvanāmayiyā. Purimaṃ purimañhi pacchimassa pacchimassa padaṭṭhānaṃ. Idāni yasmā dānaṃ sīlaṃ lokiyabhāvanā ca na kevalaṃ yathāvuttaparatoghosādīnaṃyeva, atha kho yathākkamaṃ pariyattibāhusaccakammaṭṭhānānuyogamaggasammādiṭṭhīnampi paccayā honti, tasmā tampi nayaṃ dassetuṃ puna “dānamaya”ntiādinā desanaṃ vaḍḍhesi. Tathā patirūpadesavāsādayo kāyavivekacittavivekādīnaṃ kāraṇaṃ hotīti imaṃ nayaṃ dassetuṃ “patirūpadesavāso”tiādimāha. Tattha kusalavīmaṃsāyāti paṭisaṅkhānupassanāya. Akusalapariccāgoti iminā pahānapariññā vuttāti. Samādhindriyassāti maggasamādhindriyassa. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

One endowed with virtue, due to the absence of remorse, becomes concentrated and is capable of thinking about the Dhamma; therefore, virtue is a cause for knowledge consisting of thought. Thus he said, 'Consisting of virtue,' etc. 'Consisting of development' (bhāvanāmaya) means development called serenity. 'For wisdom consisting of development' (bhāvanāmayiyā) refers to that called the higher absorptions and that called insight. For each preceding one is the proximate cause for each succeeding one. Now, because giving, virtue, and worldly development are not only conditions for the aforementioned hearing from another and so forth, but are also, respectively, conditions for learning and great learning, for application to a meditation subject, and for path right view, therefore, to show this method as well, he expanded the teaching again with 'Consisting of giving,' etc. Similarly, because living in a suitable place and so forth is a cause for bodily seclusion, mental seclusion, and so forth, to show this method he said, 'Living in a suitable place,' etc. Therein, 'for wholesome investigation' means for the contemplation of reflection. By this statement 'abandonment of the unwholesome,' full understanding by abandoning is stated. 'Of the faculty of concentration' means of the path faculty of concentration. The rest is easy to understand.

Vibhattihāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the Method of Classification is concluded.

9. Parivattanahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Analysis of the Turning Mode

35. Tattha [V 0.0241][M 0.0115] katamo parivattano hāroti parivattanahāravibhaṅgo. Tattha yasmā saṃvaṇṇiyamāne sutte yathāniddiṭṭhānaṃ kusalākusaladhammānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūte akusalakusaladhamme pahātabbabhāvādivasena niddhāraṇaṃ paṭipakkhato parivattanaṃ, tasmā “sammādiṭṭhissa purisapuggalassa micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā bhavatī”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha sammā pasatthā, sundarā diṭṭhi etassāti sammādiṭṭhi, tassa. Sā panassa sammādiṭṭhitā pubbabhāgasammādiṭṭhiyā vā lokuttarasammādiṭṭhiyā vā veditabbā. Micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā bhavatīti purimanaye vipassanāsammādiṭṭhiyā pahīnā hoti, vikkhambhitāti attho. Pacchimanaye paṭhamamaggasammādiṭṭhiyā pahīnā samucchinnāti attho.

35. Herein, what is the turning mode? It is the analysis of the turning mode. Herein, because in the Sutta that is being elucidated, the determination—by way of being that which should be abandoned, and so forth—of the unwholesome and wholesome states that are the opposites of the wholesome and unwholesome states as indicated, is a turning by way of the opposite, therefore it is begun with: “For a person with right view, wrong view is overcome.” Herein, `sammādiṭṭhi` is a person for whom there is a rightly praised, beautiful view; `tassa` refers to that person. And for him, that state of having right view should be understood as either preliminary right view or supramundane right view. “Wrong view is overcome” means, in the former method, it is abandoned by insight right view, that is, it is suppressed. In the latter method, it is abandoned by the right view of the first path, that is, it is eradicated.

Ye cassa micchādiṭṭhipaccayāti micchābhinivesahetu ye ariyānaṃ adassanakāmatādayo lobhādayo pāṇātipātādayo ca aneke lāmakaṭṭhena pāpakā akosallasambhūtaṭṭhena akusalā dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ. Imassa āraddhavipassakassa ariyassa ca. Dhammāti samathavipassanādhammā, sattattiṃsabodhipakkhiyadhammā vā anuppannā vā sambhavanti uppannā, bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Sammāsaṅkappassātiādīnampi imināva nayena attho veditabbo. Ayaṃ pana viseso – sammāvimuttiādīnaṃ micchāvimutti avimuttāva samānā “vimuttā maya”nti evaṃsaññino avimuttiyaṃ vā vimuttisaññino. Tatrāyaṃ vacanattho – micchā pāpikā vimutti vimokkho etassāti micchāvimutti. Aṭṭhaṅgā ca micchāvimutti yathāvuttenākārena micchābhinivesavasena ca pavattā antadvayalakkhaṇā. Sammāvimutti pana phaladhammā, micchādiṭṭhike samāsevato micchāvimokkho vā micchāvimutti. Micchāvimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ pana micchāvimokkhe micchādiṭṭhiyā ca sāranti gahaṇavasena pavatto akusalacittuppādo antamaso pāpaṃ katvā “sukataṃ mayā”ti paccavekkhato uppannamoho ca. Sammāvimuttiñāṇadassanassāti ettha sekkhānaṃ paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ sammāvimuttiñāṇadassananti adhippetaṃ. Tañhi uttaribhāvanāpāripūriyā saṃvattati.

And with regard to `ye cassa micchādiṭṭhipaccayā`: whatever many states—such as the desire not to see the noble ones, greed, and the killing of living beings—which are evil (`pāpakā`) because of their base nature and unwholesome (`akusalā`) because they arise from unskillfulness, might arise for this person who has undertaken insight and for this noble one, due to the cause of wrong adherence. As for `dhammā`: the states of serenity and insight, or the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment. Those that have not yet arisen, arise; those that have arisen go to the fulfillment of development. The meaning of `sammāsaṅkappassa`, and so forth, should also be understood in this same way. This, however, is the distinction regarding `sammāvimutti`, and so forth: `micchāvimutti` (wrong liberation) is for those who, while being unliberated, have the perception, “We are liberated,” or who, in non-liberation, have the perception of liberation. Herein, this is the word-meaning: `micchāvimutti` is so-called because for this person (`etassa`), the liberation (`vimutti`) or release (`vimokkho`) is wrong (`micchā`) and evil (`pāpikā`). And wrong liberation has eight components, occurs in the manner described and by way of wrong adherence, and is characterized by the two extremes. Right liberation (`sammāvimutti`), however, are the fruition-states. Or, for one who associates with those of wrong view, wrong release is wrong liberation. As for the knowledge and vision of wrong liberation (`micchāvimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ`), it is the arising of an unwholesome state of mind that occurs by way of grasping wrong release and wrong view as the essence; and it is the delusion that arises for one who, at the very least, after doing evil, reflects, “It was well done by me.” Here, in the phrase `sammāvimuttiñāṇadassanassa`, the reviewing knowledge of trainees (`sekkhā`) is intended as the knowledge and vision of right liberation. For that leads to the fulfillment of further development.

36. Evaṃ [V 0.0242] sammādiṭṭhiādimukhena micchādiṭṭhiādiṃ dassetvā puna pāṇātipātaadinnādānakāmesumicchācārādito veramaṇiyādīhi pāṇātipātādīnaṃ parivattanaṃ dassetuṃ “yassā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha kālavādissāti [M 0.0116] lakkhaṇavacanaṃ. Kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasañhitanti so samphappalāpassa pahānāya paṭipanno hotīti vuttaṃ.

36. Thus, having shown wrong view and so forth by means of right view and so forth, to then show the turning from killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and so forth, by means of abstinence and so forth, the passage beginning with `yassa` is commenced. Herein, `kālavādī` is a word indicating a characteristic. It is said: by speaking at the right time (`kālena`), with reason (`sāpadesaṃ`), with limits (`pariyantavatiṃ`), and connected with the goal (`atthasañhitaṃ`), he is practicing for the abandonment of frivolous talk.

Puna “ye ca kho kecī”tiādinā sammādiṭṭhiādimukheneva micchādiṭṭhiādīhi eva parivattanaṃ pakārantarena dasseti. Tattha sandiṭṭhikāti paccakkhā. Sahadhammikāti sakāraṇā. Gārayhāti garahitabbayuttā. Vādānuvādāti vādā ceva anuvādā ca. “Vādānupātā”tipi pāṭho, vādānupavattiyoti attho. Pujjāti pūjanīyā. Pāsaṃsāti pasaṃsitabbā.

Again, by the passage beginning with `ye ca kho keci`, the turning from wrong view and so forth by means of right view and so forth is shown in another way. Herein, `sandiṭṭhikā` (visible) means directly experienced (`paccakkhā`). `Sahadhammikā` (with the teaching) means with a cause (`sakāraṇā`). `Gārayhā` (blameworthy) means worthy of censure (`garahitabbayuttā`). `Vādānuvādā` means both censures (`vādā`) and accusations (`anuvādā`). There is also the reading `vādānupātā`, which means occurrences in accordance with blame (`vādānupavattiyo`). `Pujjā` (venerable) means worthy of worship (`pūjanīyā`). `Pāsaṃsā` (praiseworthy) means worthy of praise (`pasaṃsitabbā`).

Puna “ye ca kho kecī”tiādinā majjhimāya paṭipattiyā antadvayaparivattanaṃ dasseti. Tattha bhuñjitabbātiādīni cattāri padāni vatthukāmavasena yojetabbāni. Bhāvayitabbā bahulīkātabbāti padadvayaṃ kilesakāmavasena. Tesaṃ adhammoti bhāvetabbo nāma dhammo siyā, kāmā ca tesaṃ bhāvetabbā icchitā, kāmehi ca veramaṇī kāmānaṃ paṭipakkho, iti sā tesaṃ adhammo āpajjatīti adhippāyo.

Again, by the passage beginning with `ye ca kho keci`, the turning from the two extremes by means of the middle practice is shown. Herein, the four terms beginning with `bhuñjitabbā` (to be enjoyed) should be connected by way of sensual pleasures as objects (`vatthukāma`). The two terms `bhāvayitabbā` (to be developed) and `bahulīkātabbā` (to be cultivated) should be connected by way of sensual pleasures as defilements (`kilesakāma`). As for `tesaṃ adhammo` (their non-Dhamma): there might be a Dhamma to be developed, but for them, sensual pleasures are what is desired to be developed. And abstinence from sensual pleasures is the opposite of sensual pleasures. Therefore, that abstinence amounts to non-Dhamma for them—this is the intention.

Niyyāniko dhammoti saha vipassanāya ariyamaggo. Dukkhoti pāpaṃ nijjarāpessāmāti pavattitaṃ sarīratāpanaṃ vadati. Sukhoti anavajjapaccayaparibhogasukhaṃ. Etesupi vāresu vuttanayeneva adhammabhāvāpatti vattabbā. Idāni asubhasaññādimukhena subhasaññādiparivattanaṃ dassetuṃ “yathā vā panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Āraddhavipassakassa kilesāsucipaggharaṇavasena tebhūmakasaṅkhārā asubhato upaṭṭhahantīti katvā vuttaṃ “sabbasaṅkhāresu asubhānupassino viharato”ti. “Yaṃ yaṃ vā panā”tiādinā paṭipakkhassa lakkhaṇaṃ vibhāveti. Tattha ajjhāpannoti adhiāpanno, abhiupagato pariññātoti attho.

`Niyyāniko dhammo` (the liberating Dhamma) is the noble path together with insight. `Dukkha` refers to the tormenting of the body undertaken with the thought, “We will make our evil wear away.” `Sukha` is the happiness from using blameless requisites. In these instances as well, the falling into the state of non-Dhamma should be stated in the way already explained. Now, to show the turning from the perception of beauty, and so forth, by means of the perception of foulness, and so forth, the passage beginning with `yathā vā pana` is stated. Because for one who has undertaken insight, the formations of the three realms appear as foul by way of the oozing of the impurity of defilements, it is said: “dwelling contemplating foulness in all formations.” By the passage beginning with `yaṃ yaṃ vā pana`, it clarifies the characteristic of the opposite. Herein, `ajjhāpanno` means `adhiāpanno` (entered upon), `abhiupagato` (approached), `pariññāto` (fully understood); this is the meaning.

Parivattanahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Turning Mode is concluded.

10. Vevacanahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Analysis of the Mode of Synonyms

37. Tattha [V 0.0243][M 0.0117] katamo vevacano hāroti vevacanahāravibhaṅgo. Tattha yathā vevacananiddeso hoti, taṃ dassetuṃ “ekaṃ bhagavā dhammaṃ aññamaññehi vevacanehi niddisatī”ti vuttaṃ. Vevacanehīti pariyāyasaddehīti attho. Padattho pubbe vutto eva. Kasmā pana bhagavā ekaṃ dhammaṃ anekapariyāyehi niddisatīti? Vuccate – desanākāle āyatiñca kassaci kathañci tadatthapaṭibodho siyāti pariyāyavacanaṃ, tasmiṃ khaṇe vikkhittacittānaṃ aññavihitānaṃ aññena pariyāyena tadatthāvabodhanatthaṃ pariyāyavacanaṃ. Teneva padena puna vacane tadaññesaṃ tattha adhigatatā siyāti mandabuddhīnaṃ punappunaṃ tadatthasallakkhaṇe asammosanatthaṃ pariyāyavacanaṃ. Anekepi atthā samānabyañjanā hontīti yā atthantaraparikappanā siyā, tassā parivajjanatthampi pariyāyavacanaṃ anaññassa vacane anekāhi tāhi tāhi saññāhi tesaṃ tesaṃ atthānaṃ ñāpanatthampi pariyāyavacanaṃ seyyathāpi nighaṇṭusatthe. Dhammakathikānaṃ tantiatthupanibandhanaparāvabodhanānaṃ sukhasiddhiyāpi pariyāyavacanaṃ. Attano dhammaniruttipaṭisambhidāppattiyā vibhāvanatthaṃ, veneyyānaṃ tattha bījāvāpanatthaṃ vā pariyāyavacanaṃ bhagavā niddisati.

37. Herein, which is the mode of synonyms? It is the analysis of the mode of synonyms. Herein, to show how the indication of synonyms occurs, it is said: “The Blessed One indicates one dhamma with various synonyms.” ‘With synonyms’ means with synonymous terms. The meaning of the words has already been stated before. But why does the Blessed One indicate one dhamma with many synonyms? It is said: A synonymous term is indicated so that at the time of teaching and also in the future, someone might, in some way, understand its meaning. At that moment, for those with distracted minds or occupied with other things, a synonymous term is indicated so they may understand its meaning through another synonym. And since repeating the same term would only serve to deepen the understanding of others, a synonymous term is indicated for those of weak intellect to prevent forgetfulness when repeatedly discerning its meaning. Also, since many meanings can have the same phrasing, a synonymous term is indicated to avoid any speculation of a different meaning that might arise. When speaking of a single thing, a synonymous term is indicated to make its various meanings known through various designations, just as in a glossary. A synonymous term is also indicated for the easy accomplishment of Dhamma teachers' retention of the meaning of the text and their profound understanding. The Blessed One indicates a synonymous term either to reveal his own attainment of the analytical knowledges of Dhamma and language, or to plant the seed thereof in those to be trained.

Kiṃ bahunā yassā dhammadhātuyā suppaṭividdhattā sammāsambuddhā yathā sabbasmiṃ atthe appaṭihatañāṇācārā, tathā sabbasmiṃ saddavohāreti ekampi atthaṃ anekehi pariyāyehi bodheti, na tattha dandhāyitattaṃ vitthāyitattaṃ atthassa. Nāpi dhammadesanāhāni, āveṇikovāyaṃ buddhadhammoti pariyāyadesanaṃ dassento “āsā”tiādimāha. Tattha atthaṃ dassento “āsā nāma vuccati yā bhavissassa atthassā”tiādimāha. Tattha bhavissassa atthassāti anāgatassa icchitabbassa atthassa. “Avassaṃ āgamissatī”tiādinā tassā pavattiyākāraṃ dasseti. Anāgatatthavisayā taṇhā āsā. Anāgatapaccuppannatthavisayā taṇhā pihāti ayametāsaṃ viseso.

What need is there for much speech? Because of the thorough penetration of the Dhamma-element of omniscience, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, just as he has unimpeded knowledge and conduct in all meanings, so too does he have them in all verbal expression; therefore, he makes known even one meaning with many synonyms. Therein, there is no slowness or diffuseness of meaning. Nor is there any deficiency in the Dhamma teaching. This is a unique quality of a Buddha. Thus, showing the teaching with synonyms, he said, ‘āsā,’ and so on. Therein, showing the meaning, he said, ‘āsā is the name for that which is for a future benefit,’ and so on. Therein, ‘for a future benefit’ means for a benefit that is future and to be desired. By ‘It will certainly come,’ and so on, he shows the mode of its occurrence. Craving that has a future benefit as its object is āsā. Craving that has future and present benefits as its object is pihā. This is the distinction between them.

Atthanipphattipaṭipālanāti yāya icchitassa atthassa nipphattiṃ paṭipāleti āgameti, yāya vā nipphannaṃ atthaṃ paṭipāleti rakkhati. Ayaṃ abhinandanā [M 0.0118] nāma, yathāladdhassa atthassa kelāyanā nāmāti attho. Taṃ atthanipphattiṃ sattasaṅkhāravasena vibhajitvā dassento “piyaṃ vā ñāti”ntiādimāha[V 0.0244]. Tattha dhammanti rūpādiārammaṇadhammaṃ, atiiṭṭhārammaṇaṃ abhinandati, aniṭṭhārammaṇehipi taṃ dassetuṃ “appaṭikkūlato vā abhinandatī”ti vuttaṃ. Paṭikkūlepi hi vipallāsavasena sattaṃ, saṅkhāraṃ vā appaṭikkūlato abhinandati.

‘Awaiting the fulfillment of a benefit’ means: that by which one awaits and expects the fulfillment of a desired benefit, or that by which one protects and guards a benefit already fulfilled. This is called ‘rejoicing’; the meaning is that it is called ‘cherishing’ a benefit as it has been obtained. Showing that fulfillment of a benefit by dividing it according to beings and formations, he said, ‘a dear one or a relative,’ and so on. Therein, ‘dhamma’ means one rejoices in the dhamma which is an object such as form, etc., an extremely desirable object. And to show this regarding undesirable objects too, it is said, ‘or one rejoices in it as not repulsive.’ For even in what is repulsive, through the power of perversion, one rejoices in a being or a formation as not repulsive.

Yāsu anekadhātūsu pavattiyā taṇhā “anekadhātūsu sarā”ti vuttā, tā dhātuyo vibhāgena dassetuṃ “cakkhudhātū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kiñcāpi dhātuvibhaṅgādīsu (vibha. 172 ādayo) kāmadhātuādayo aññāpi anekadhātuyo āgatā, tāsampi ettheva samavarodhoti dassanatthaṃ aṭṭhārasevettha dassitā. Keci rūpādhimuttātiādi tāsu dhātūsu taṇhāya pavattidassanaṃ. Tattha yasmā pañca ajjhattikā dhātuyo satta ca viññāṇadhātuyo dhammadhātu ca dhammārammaṇeneva saṅgahitā, tasmā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo uddisitvā chaḷeva taṇhāya pavattiṭṭhānāni vibhattānīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Taṇhāpakkhā nekkhammassitāpi domanassupavicārā tassa anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato uppajjati “pihapaccayā domanassa”nti vacanato, ko pana vādo gehassitesu domanassupavicāresūti imāni catuvīsati padāni “taṇhāpakkho”ti vuttaṃ. Gehassitā pana upekkhā aññāṇupekkhatāya yathābhinivesassa paccayo hotīti “yā cha upekkhā gehassitā, ayaṃ diṭṭhipakkho”ti vuttaṃ.

Because of its occurrence in many elements, craving is called ‘a flow in many elements.’ To show those elements by way of analysis, ‘the eye element,’ and so on, is said. Although in the Analysis of Elements and other texts, other various elements such as the sense-sphere element are mentioned, to show that they too are included right here, only the eighteen have been shown here. ‘Some are intent on form,’ and so on, shows the occurrence of craving in those elements. Therein, because the five internal elements, the seven consciousness elements, and the dhamma-element are included by the dhamma-object alone, it should be understood that having indicated the eighteen elements, only six bases for the occurrence of craving have been distinguished. Even the mental proliferations of displeasure based on renunciation belong to the side of craving, since for one who arouses longing for the unsurpassed liberations, displeasure arises, according to the saying, ‘displeasure arises from longing as a condition.’ What then to say of the mental proliferations of displeasure based on the household life? For this reason, these twenty-four terms are said to be ‘the side of craving.’ But equanimity based on the household life, because it is equanimity due to ignorance, is a condition for adherence to whatever wrong view. Therefore it is said, ‘The six kinds of equanimity based on the household life, this is the side of views.’

38. Idāni tesaṃ upavicārānaṃ taṇhāpariyāyaṃ dassento “sāyeva patthanākārena dhammanandī”tiādimāha. Puna cittaṃ paññā bhagavā dhammo saṅgho sīlaṃ cāgoti imesaṃ pariyāyavacananiddhāraṇena vevacanahāraṃ vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “cittaṃ mano viññāṇa”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha “aññampi evaṃ jātiya”nti iminā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo sallakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā cintā upaparikkhā bhūrī medhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amohoti (mahāni. 149) evamādīnampi paññāya pariyāyasaddānaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo.

38. Now, showing the synonyms of craving for those mental proliferations, he said, ‘That very delight in dhammas in the form of longing,’ and so on. Again, to show the mode of synonyms by analyzing it through the determination of the synonymous terms for these—mind, wisdom, the Blessed One, the Dhamma, the Sangha, virtue, and generosity—‘mind, intellect, consciousness,’ and so on, was begun. Therein, by this phrase ‘and others of a similar kind,’ the inclusion of synonymous terms for wisdom such as these should be understood: wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of dhammas, marking, close marking, repeated close marking, sagacity, skill, ingenuity, perspicacity, reflection, scrutiny, extensive wisdom, sagacity, guidance, insight, clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the weapon of wisdom, the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, and non-delusion.

Pañcindriyāni [M 0.0119] lokuttarānīti khaye ñāṇantiādīni pañcindriyāni lokuttarāni, lokuttarapaññāya vevacanānīti attho. Sabbā paññāti itarehi vevacanehi vuttā sabbā paññā lokiyalokuttaramissikāti attho. “Api cā”tiādinā imināpi pariyāyena vevacanaṃ vattabbanti dasseti. Ādhipateyyaṭṭhenāti adhimokkhalakkhaṇe ādhipateyyaṭṭhena. Yathā ca buddhānussatiyaṃ [V 0.0245] vuttanti yathā buddhānussatiniddese (visuddhi. 1.123) “itipi so bhagavā”tiādinā pāḷiyā so bhagavā itipi arahaṃ…pe… itipi bhagavāti anekehi vevacanehi bhagavā anussaritabboti vuttaṃ. Imināva nayena balanipphattigato vesārajjappatto yāva dhammobhāsapajjotakaroti, etehi pariyāyehi buddhassa bhagavato vevacanaṃ buddhānussatiyaṃ vattabbanti padaṃ āharitvā sambandho veditabbo. Etānipi katipayāni eva bhagavato vevacanāni. Asaṅkhyeyyā hi buddhaguṇā guṇanemittakāni ca bhagavato nāmāni. Vuttañhetaṃ dhammasenāpatinā –

The five faculties are supramundane: the five faculties, such as the knowledge of destruction, etc., are supramundane; this means they are synonyms for supramundane wisdom. All wisdom: this means that all wisdom stated by other synonyms is mixed with the mundane and the supramundane. 'Moreover,' and so on—this shows that a synonym should be stated by this alternative method as well. By way of predominance: by way of predominance in the characteristic of resolution. And just as it was said in the recollection of the Buddha—as in the exposition of the recollection of the Buddha, by the Pāḷi passage 'Indeed, that Blessed One,' and so on, it was said that the Blessed One should be recollected by many synonyms: 'that Blessed One is indeed the Arahant... up to... indeed the Blessed One.' By this very method, the connection should be understood by supplying the phrase 'the synonyms of the Buddha, the Blessed One, are to be stated in the recollection of the Buddha' to these alternative terms: 'attained the perfection of strength,' 'attained fearlessness,' up to 'the maker of the Dhamma's light and radiance.' These too are just a few synonyms of the Blessed One. For immeasurable indeed are the Buddha's virtues, and the names of the Blessed One are based on his virtues. This was said by the General of the Dhamma—

“Asaṅkhyeyyāni nāmāni, saguṇena mahesino;

Guṇena nāmamuddheyyaṃ, api nāma sahassato”ti. (udā. aṭṭha. 53);

Innumerable are the names of the Great Sage, which are due to his virtues; by a single virtue, I could extract a name, even from a thousand.

Dhammānussatiyaṃ “asaṅkhata”ntiādīsu na kenaci paccayena saṅkhatanti asaṅkhataṃ. Natthi etassa anto vināsoti anantaṃ. Āsavānaṃ anārammaṇato anāsavaṃ. Aviparītasabhāvattā saccaṃ. Saṃsārassa paratīrabhāvato pāraṃ. Nipuṇañāṇavisayattā sukhumasabhāvattā ca nipuṇa. Anupacitañāṇasambhārehi daṭṭhuṃ na sakkāti sududdasaṃ. Uppādajarāhi anabbhāhatattā ajajjaraṃ. Thirabhāvena dhuvaṃ. Jarāmaraṇehi apalujjanato apalokitaṃ. Maṃsacakkhunā dibbacakkhunā ca apassitabbattā anidassanaṃ. Rāgādipapañcābhāvena nippapañcaṃ. Kilesābhisaṅkhārānaṃ vūpasamahetutāya santaṃ.

In the recollection of the Dhamma, concerning 'unconditioned' and so on: it is 'unconditioned' (asaṅkhata) because it is not conditioned by any cause. It is 'endless' (ananta) because for it there is no end or destruction. It is 'taintless' (anāsava) because it is not an object for the taints. It is 'truth' (sacca) because its nature is not perverted. It is the 'far shore' (pāra) because it is the further shore of saṃsāra. It is 'subtle' (nipuṇa) because it is the domain of refined wisdom and because of its subtle nature. It is 'very hard to see' (sududdasa) because it cannot be seen by those who have not accumulated the requisites of wisdom. It is 'unaging' (ajajjara) because it is not afflicted by origination and aging. It is 'stable' (dhuva) because of its steadfast nature. It is 'indestructible' (apalokita) because it does not break up with aging and death. It is 'invisible' (anidassana) because it cannot be seen by the physical eye or the divine eye. It is 'free from proliferation' (nippapañca) because there is no proliferation of lust and so on. It is 'peaceful' (santa) because it is the cause for the subsiding of defilements and formations.

Amatahetutāya bhaṅgābhāvato ca amataṃ. Uttamaṭṭhena atappakaṭṭhena ca paṇītaṃ. Asivānaṃ kammakilesavipākavaṭṭānaṃ abhāvena sivaṃ. Catūhi yogehi anupaddavabhāvena khemaṃ. Taṇhā khīyati etthāti taṇhakkhayo. Katapuññehipi kadācideva passitabbattā acchariyaṃ. Abhūtapubbattā abbhutaṃ[M 0.0120]. Anantarāyattā anītikaṃ. Anantarāyabhāvahetuto anītikadhammaṃ (saṃ. ni. aṭṭha. 3.5.377-409).

It is 'deathless' (amata) because it is the cause of the deathless and because of the absence of dissolution. It is 'excellent' (paṇīta) because it is supreme and sublime. It is 'auspicious' (siva) because of the absence of the inauspicious cycles of kamma, defilements, and their results. It is 'secure' (khema) because it is without affliction from the four yokes. It is the 'destruction of craving' (taṇhakkhaya) because 'craving is destroyed in it.' It is 'wonderful' (acchariya) because it is to be seen only occasionally even by those who have made merit. It is 'marvellous' (abbhuta) because it has not been before. It is 'free from affliction' (anītika) because it is without danger. It is the 'state free from affliction' (anītikadhamma) because it is the cause of the state of being without danger.

Anibbattisabhāvattā ajātaṃ. Tato eva abhūtaṃ. Ubhayenāpi uppādarahitanti vuttaṃ hoti. Kenaci anupaddutattā anupaddavaṃ. Na kenaci paccayena katanti akataṃ. Natthi ettha sokoti asokaṃ. Sokahetuvigamena visokaṃ. Kenaci anupasajjitabbattā anupasaggaṃ. Anupasaggabhāvahetuto anupasaggadhammaṃ.

It is 'unborn' (ajāta) because its nature is non-arising. For that very reason, it is 'unbecome' (abhūta). By both, it is said to be devoid of arising. It is 'free from calamity' (anupaddava) because it is not afflicted by anything. It is 'unmade' (akata) because it is not made by any condition. It is 'sorrowless' (asoka) because 'there is no sorrow here.' It is 'free from sorrow' (visoka) because the cause of sorrow has departed. It is 'unassailable' (anupasagga) because it is not to be assailed by anyone. It is the 'unassailable state' (anupasaggadhamma) because it is the cause of the state of being unassailable.

Gambhīrañāṇagocarato [V 0.0246] gambhīraṃ. Sammāpaṭipattiṃ vinā passituṃ pattuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā duppassaṃ. Sabbalokaṃ uttaritvā ṭhitanti uttaraṃ. Natthi etassa uttaranti anuttaraṃ. Samassa sadisassa abhāvena asamaṃ. Paṭibhāgābhāvena appaṭisamaṃ. Uttamaṭṭhena jeṭṭhaṃ, pāsaṃsatamattā vā jeṭṭhaṃ. Saṃsāradukkhaṭṭitehi letabbato leṇaṃ. Tato rakkhaṇato tāṇaṃ. Raṇābhāvena araṇaṃ. Aṅgaṇābhāvena anaṅgaṇaṃ. Niddosatāya akācaṃ. Rāgādimalāpagamena vimalaṃ. Catūhi oghehi anajjhottharaṇīyato dīpo. Saṃsāravūpasamasukhatāya sukhaṃ. Pamāṇakaradhammābhāvato appamāṇaṃ, gaṇetuṃ etassa na sakkāti ca appamāṇaṃ. Saṃsārasamudde anosīdanaṭṭhānatāya patiṭṭhā. Rāgādikiñcanābhāvena pariggahābhāvena ca akiñcananti evamattho daṭṭhabbo.

It is 'profound' (gambhīra) because it is the domain of deep wisdom. It is 'difficult to see' (duppassa) because, without right practice, it is unable to be seen or attained. It is 'supreme' (uttara) because it stands having transcended the entire world. It is 'unsurpassed' (anuttara) because there is nothing superior to it. It is 'unequaled' (asama) because of the absence of an equal or a similar. It is 'matchless' (appaṭisama) because of the absence of a counterpart. It is 'foremost' (jeṭṭha) in the sense of being supreme, or 'foremost' because it is most praiseworthy. It is a 'refuge' (leṇa) because it is to be resorted to for shelter by those established in the suffering of saṃsāra. It is 'protection' (tāṇa) because it protects from that. It is 'free from conflict' (araṇa) because of the absence of conflict. It is 'free from defilement' (anaṅgaṇa) because of the absence of defilement. It is 'flawless' (akāca) because of its faultlessness. It is 'immaculate' (vimala) because of the removal of stains such as lust. It is an 'island' (dīpa) because it is not to be overwhelmed by the four floods. It is 'bliss' (sukha) because of the happiness from the calming of saṃsāra. It is 'immeasurable' (appamāṇa) because of the absence of measuring dhammas, and also 'immeasurable' because its measure cannot be calculated. It is a 'foundation' (patiṭṭhā) because it is a place of not sinking in the ocean of saṃsāra. It is 'possessionless' (akiñcana) because of the absence of hindrances such as lust and because of the absence of grasping. Thus the meaning should be understood.

Saṅghānussatiyaṃ sattānaṃ sāroti sīlasārādisāraguṇayogato sattesu sārabhūto. Sattānaṃ maṇḍoti gorasesu sappimaṇḍo viya sattesu maṇḍabhūto. Sāraguṇavaseneva sattesu uddharitabbato sattānaṃ uddhāro. Niccalaguṇatāya sattānaṃ esikā. Guṇasobhāsurabhibhāvena sattānaṃ pasūnaṃ surabhi kusumanti attho.

In the recollection of the Saṅgha: 'the essence of beings' (sattānaṃ sāro) means that because of their connection with essential qualities such as virtue, they are the essence among beings. 'The cream of beings' (sattānaṃ maṇḍo) means that just as the cream of ghee is the finest among milk products, so they are the cream among beings. 'The select of beings' (sattānaṃ uddhāro) means they are to be selected from among beings by the power of their essential qualities. 'The pillar of beings' (sattānaṃ esikā) means they are so because of their unwavering qualities. 'The fragrant flower of beings' (sattānaṃ pasūnaṃ surabhi kusumaṃ) means they are so by the splendor and fragrance of their virtues—this is the meaning.

Guṇesu uttamaṅgaṃ paññā tassā upasobhāhetutāya sīlaṃ uttamaṅgopasobhanaṃ vuttaṃ. Sīlesu paripūrakārino anijjhantā nāma guṇā natthīti “nidhānañca sīlaṃ sabbadobhaggasamatikkamanaṭṭhenā”ti vuttaṃ. Ayañca attho ākaṅkheyyasuttena (ma. ni. 1.64 ādayo) dīpetabbo. Aparampi vuttaṃ – “ijjhati, bhikkhave, sīlavato cetopaṇidhi visuddhattā”ti (dī. ni. 3.337; saṃ. ni. 4.352; a. ni. 8.35). Sippanti dhanusippaṃ. Dhaññanti dhanāyitabbaṃ. Dhammavolokanatāyāti samathavipassanādidhammassa volokanabhāvena[M 0.0121]. Volokanaṭṭhenāti sattabhūmakādipāsāde viya sīle ṭhatvā abhiññācakkhunā lokassa voloketuṃ sakkāti vuttaṃ. Sabbabhūmānuparivatti ca sīlaṃ catubhūmakakusalassāpi tadanuvattanato. Sesaṃ uttānamevāti.

Among virtues, wisdom is the highest limb (uttamaṅga); because it enhances it, virtue is called 'the enhancer of the highest limb' (uttamaṅgopasobhana). For one who fulfills the virtues, there are no qualities that do not succeed; therefore it is said, 'And virtue is a treasure, in the sense of surpassing all misfortunes.' This meaning should also be illustrated by the Ākaṅkheyya Sutta. Furthermore, it is said: 'For the virtuous, bhikkhus, the aspiration of the mind succeeds because of its purity.' 'Skill' (sippa) means the skill of archery. 'Grain' (dhañña) means what is to be desired as wealth. 'By way of looking upon the Dhamma' (dhammavolokanatāya) means because it is a basis for looking upon the Dhamma of serenity, insight, and so on. 'In the sense of surveying' (volokanaṭṭhena), it is said that just as one can survey from a seven-storied palace and so on, so too, standing on virtue, one can survey the world with the eye of higher knowledge. And virtue revolves after all planes (sabbabhūmānuparivatti), for even the wholesome states of the four planes follow after it. The rest is clear.

Vevacanahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Analysis of the Method of Synonyms is finished.

11. Paññattihāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā

11. The Commentary on the Analysis of the Method of Designations

39. Tattha [V 0.0247] katamo paññattihāroti paññattihāravibhaṅgo. Tattha kā panāyaṃ paññattīti? Āha “yā pakatikathāya desanā”ti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yā desanāhārādayo viya assādādipadatthavisesaniddhāraṇaṃ akatvā bhagavato sābhāvikadhammakathāya desanā. Yā tassā paññāpanā, ayaṃ paññattihāro. Yasmā pana sā bhagavato tathā tathā veneyyasantāne yathādhippetamatthaṃ nikkhipatīti nikkhepo. Tassa cāyaṃ hāro dukkhādisaṅkhāte bhāge pakārehi ñāpeti, asaṅkarato vā ṭhapeti, tasmā “nikkhepapaññattī”ti vutto. Iti pakatikathāya desanāti saṅkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vitthārena vibhajituṃ “kā ca pakatikathāya desanā”ti pucchitvā “cattāri saccānī”tiādimāha.

39. Herein, 'What is the method of designation?' refers to the Analysis of the Method of Designation. Therein, what is this designation? He said: 'That which is the teaching by way of natural speech.' This is what is meant: that teaching which, unlike the method of teaching and so on, does not determine the specific meanings of terms such as 'enjoyment,' is the Blessed One's teaching by way of a natural discourse on the Dhamma. Whatever is the making known of that, this is the method of designation. And since that teaching of the Blessed One places the intended meaning in the mental continuum of the trainable ones in various ways, it is 'placement' (nikkhepa). And this method makes known the parts designated as suffering, etc., by means of types, or it establishes them without confusion; therefore, it is called 'designation by placement' (nikkhepapaññatti). Thus, to analyze in detail the meaning stated briefly as 'the teaching by way of natural speech,' having asked, 'And what is the teaching by way of natural speech?', he said, 'The four truths,' and so on.

Tattha idaṃ dukkhanti ayaṃ paññattīti kakkhaḷaphusanādisabhāve rūpārūpadhamme atītādivasena anekabhedabhinne abhinditvā pīḷanasaṅkhatasantāpavipariṇāmaṭṭhatāsāmaññena yā kucchitabhāvādimukhena ekajjhaṃ gahaṇassa kāraṇabhūtā paññatti, kā pana sāti? Nāmapaññattinibandhanā tajjāpaññatti. “Viññattivikārasahito saddo evā”ti apare. Iminā nayena tattha tattha paññattiattho veditabbo. “Pañcannaṃ khandhāna”ntiādinā tassā paññattiyā upādānaṃ dasseti. Dasannaṃ indriyānanti aṭṭha rūpindriyāni manindriyaṃ vedanindriyanti evaṃ dasannaṃ. Anubhavanasāmaññena hi vedanā ekamindriyaṃ katā, tathā saddhādayo ca maggapakkhiyāti.

Therein, 'This is suffering'—this is a designation. Regarding material and immaterial phenomena which have the nature of harshness, contact, etc., and are divided into many kinds by way of the past, etc.—without distinguishing them, the designation which, with the contemptible state as its primary aspect, becomes the cause for grasping them together through the commonality of being oppressive, conditioned, tormenting, and perishable—what is that? It is the resultant designation connected with name-designation. 'It is just sound together with intimation and alteration,' say others. By this method, the meaning of designation should be understood in each and every case. By 'Of the five aggregates,' etc., he shows the basis of that designation. 'Of the ten faculties' means: the eight material faculties, the mind faculty, and the feeling faculty—thus ten. Indeed, by the commonality of experiencing, feeling is made one faculty. Likewise, faith and so on are made factors of the path.

Kabaḷaṃ karīyatīti kabaḷīkāroti vatthuvasena ayaṃ niddeso. Yāya ojāya sattā yāpenti, tassāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Sā hi ojaṭṭhamakassa [M 0.0122] rūpassa āharaṇato āhāro. Atthīti maggena asamucchinnatāya vijjati. Rāgoti rañjanaṭṭhena rāgo. Nandanaṭṭhena nandī. Taṇhāyanaṭṭhena taṇhā. Sabbānetāni lobhasseva nāmāni. Patiṭṭhitaṃ tattha viññāṇaṃ viruḷhanti kammaṃ javāpetvā paṭisandhiākaḍḍhanasamatthatāya patiṭṭhitañceva viññāṇaṃ viruḷhañca. Yatthāti tebhūmakavaṭṭe bhummaṃ, sabbattha vā purimapurimapade etaṃ bhummaṃ. Atthi tattha saṅkhārānaṃ vuddhīti ye imasmiṃ vipākavaṭṭe ṭhitassa āyatiṃ vaḍḍhanahetukā saṅkhārā, te sandhāya vuttaṃ – “yattha atthi āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattī”ti yasmiṃ ṭhāne āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti atthi. Atthi tattha āyatiṃ [V 0.0248] jātijarāmaraṇanti yattha paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ, tattha khandhānaṃ abhinibbattilakkhaṇā jāti, paripākalakkhaṇā jarā, bhedanalakkhaṇaṃ maraṇañca atthi. Ayaṃ pabhāvapaññatti dukkhassa ca samudayassa cāti ayaṃ yathāvuttā desanā dukkhasaccassa samudayasaccassa ca samuṭṭhānapaññatti, vipākavaṭṭassa saṅkhārānañca taṇhāpaccayaniddesatoti adhippāyo.

'A morsel is made,' thus it is 'morsel-making' (kabaḷīkāra). This explanation is by way of the substance. By which nutriment beings are sustained, this is a designation for that nutriment. Indeed, that nutriment, because it brings materiality that has nutriment as its eighth factor, is called nutriment (āhāra). 'It exists' means: because it has not been completely cut off by the path, it exists. Lust (rāga) is so called in the sense of coloring. Delight (nandī) is so called in the sense of delighting. Craving (taṇhā) is so called in the sense of craving. All these are just names for greed. 'Consciousness is established there and grows' means: having impelled kamma, through its ability to draw forth rebirth-linking, consciousness is both established and grown. 'Where' means: it is the locative case in the three-realm cycle of existence. Or, this locative case applies to each preceding term everywhere. 'There is a growth of formations there' is said in reference to those formations which are the cause of future growth for one established in this cycle of result. 'Where there is future rebirth-production' means: in whatever place future rebirth-production exists. 'There is future birth, aging, and death there' means: where the taking of rebirth-linking occurs, there exists birth, which has the characteristic of the production of the aggregates; aging, which has the characteristic of their maturation; and death, which has the characteristic of their dissolution. Regarding 'This is the designation of origination for suffering and its origin': this teaching, as stated, is the designation of the cause of arising for the truth of suffering and the truth of origin, because it points to craving as the condition for the cycle of result and formations—this is the intended meaning.

Natthi rāgoti aggamaggabhāvanāya samucchinnattā natthi ce rāgo. Appatiṭṭhitaṃ tattha viññāṇaṃ aviruḷhanti kammaṃ javāpetvā paṭisandhiākaḍḍhanasamatthatāyābhāvena appatiṭṭhitañceva aviruḷhañcāti vuttapaṭipakkhanayena attho veditabbo.

'There is no lust' means: if lust does not exist because it has been completely cut off by the cultivation of the highest path. 'Consciousness is not established there and does not grow' means: due to the absence of the ability to impel kamma and draw forth rebirth-linking, consciousness is neither established nor grown. The meaning should be understood by the method opposite to what was said before.

“Ayaṃ pariññāpaññattī”tiādinā ekābhisamayavaseneva maggasammādiṭṭhi catūsu ariyasaccesu pavattatīti dasseti. Ayaṃ bhāvanāpaññattīti ayaṃ dvārārammaṇehi chadvārappavattanadhammānaṃ aniccānupassanā maggassa bhāvanāpaññatti. Nirodhapaññatti nirodhassāti rodhasaṅkhātāya taṇhāya maggena anavasesanirodhapaññatti. Uppādapaññattīti uppannassa paññāpanā. Okāsapaññattīti ṭhānassa paññāpanā. Āhaṭanāpaññattīti nīharaṇapaññatti. Āsāṭikānanti gunnaṃ vaṇesu nīlamakkhikāhi ṭhapitaaṇḍakā āsāṭikā nāma. Ettha yassa uppannā, tassa sattassa anayabyasanahetutāya āsāṭikā viyāti āsāṭikā, kilesā, tesaṃ āsāṭikānaṃ. Abhinighātapaññattīti samugghātapaññatti.

By 'This is the designation of full understanding,' etc., he shows that the right view of the path operates in the four noble truths by the power of a single penetration. 'This is the designation of development' means: this contemplation of impermanence regarding phenomena occurring at the six doors with their objects is the designation of the development of the path. 'The designation of cessation for cessation' means: the designation of the complete cessation by the path of craving, which is called 'rodha'. 'The designation of arising' is the making known of what has arisen. 'The designation of location' is the making known of a place. 'The designation of removal' is the designation of taking out. 'Of the āsāṭikā' means: the eggs laid by blue flies in the wounds of cattle are called āsāṭikā. For whatever being they arise, they are like those eggs because they are a cause of misfortune and ruin for that being; therefore, the defilements are called āsāṭikā. 'The designation of striking down' is the designation of complete uprooting.

41. Evaṃ vaṭṭavivaṭṭamukhena sammasanaupādānakkhandhamukheneva saccesu paññattivibhāgaṃ dassetvā idāni teparivaṭṭavasena dassetuṃ “idaṃ ‘dukkha’nti me, bhikkhave”tiādi [M 0.0123] āraddhaṃ. Tattha dassanaṭṭhena cakkhu. Yathāsabhāvato jānanaṭṭhena ñāṇaṃ. Paṭivijjhanaṭṭhena paññā. Viditakaraṇaṭṭhena vijjā. Obhāsanaṭṭhena āloko. Sabbaṃ paññāvevacanameva. Ayaṃ vevacanapaññatti. Sacchikiriyāpaññattīti paccakkhakaraṇapaññatti.

41. Thus, having shown the analysis of designation in the truths by way of the cycle and the end of the cycle, and by way of the aggregates of clinging as objects of comprehension, now, to show it by way of the three revolutions, it was begun with 'This is suffering, O monks,' etc. Therein, 'eye' is so called in the sense of seeing. 'Knowledge' is so called in the sense of knowing according to its true nature. 'Wisdom' is so called in the sense of penetrating. 'True knowledge' is so called in the sense of making clear. 'Light' is so called in the sense of illuminating. All are just synonyms for wisdom. This is the designation of synonyms. 'The designation of realization' is the designation of direct experience.

Tulamatulañcāti gāthāya pacurajanānaṃ paccakkhabhāvato tulitaṃ paricchinnanti tulaṃ, kāmāvacaraṃ. Na tulanti atulaṃ, tulaṃ vā sadisamassa aññaṃ lokiyakammaṃ natthīti atulaṃ, mahaggatakammaṃ. Kāmāvacararūpāvacarakammaṃ vā tulaṃ, arūpāvacaraṃ atulaṃ, appavipākaṃ vā tulaṃ. Bahuvipākaṃ atulaṃ. Sambhavati etenāti sambhavaṃ, sambhavahetubhūtaṃ. Bhavasaṅkhāraṃ punabbhavasaṅkharaṇakaṃ. Avassajīti vissajjesi. Munīti buddhamuni. Ajjhattaratoti niyakajjhattarato[V 0.0249]. Samāhitoti upacārappanāsamādhivasena samāhito. Abhindi kavacamivāti kavacaṃ viya bhindi. Attasambhavanti attani sañjātaṃ kilesaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – savipākaṭṭhena sambhavaṃ bhavābhisaṅkharaṇaṭṭhena bhavasaṅkhāranti ca laddhanāmaṃ tulātulasaṅkhātaṃ lokiyakammañca ossaji, saṅgāmasīse mahāyodho kavacaṃ viya attasambhavaṃ kilesañca ajjhattarato samāhito hutvā abhindīti.

In the verse beginning `Tulamatulañca`: because it is directly perceived by many people, it is measured and defined, therefore `tulaṃ` (the measured) is kamma of the sense-sphere. Because it is not measured, it is `atulaṃ` (the unmeasured); or, because there is no other worldly kamma similar to it, `atulaṃ` is sublime kamma. Alternatively, kamma of the sense-sphere and form-sphere is `tulaṃ`, while kamma of the formless-sphere is `atulaṃ`. Or, kamma with little result is `tulaṃ`, while kamma with much result is `atulaṃ`. `Sambhavaṃ` (origination) is so called because one comes into being through it; it is the cause of existence. `Bhavasaṅkhāraṃ` (existence-formation) is that which conditions a new existence. `Avassaji` means he abandoned. `Muni` means the Buddha-sage. `Ajjhattarato` means delighting in one's own internal states. `Samāhito` means concentrated by way of access and absorption concentration. `Abhindi kavacamiva` means he broke it like armor. `Attasambhavaṃ` means the defilement arisen in oneself. This is what is said: He abandoned worldly kamma—called `tula` and `atula`, and named `sambhava` for its nature of having results and `bhavasaṅkhāra` for its nature of conditioning new existence—and, like a great warrior on the battlefield shatters armor, being one who delights internally and is concentrated, he broke the defilement arisen in himself.

Atha vā tulanti tulayanto tīrento. Atulañca sambhavanti nibbānañceva sambhavañca. Bhavasaṅkhāranti bhavagāmikammaṃ. Avassaji munīti “pañcakkhandhā aniccā, tesaṃ nirodho nibbānaṃ nicca”ntiādinā (paṭi. ma. 3.38 atthato samānaṃ) nayena tulayanto buddhamuni bhave ādīnavaṃ nibbāne ānisaṃsañca disvā taṃ khandhānaṃ mūlabhūtaṃ bhavasaṅkhāraṃ kammakkhayakarena ariyamaggena avassaji. Kathaṃ? Ajjhattarato. So hi vipassanāvasena ajjhattarato samathavasena samāhito kavacamiva attabhāvaṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhitaṃ attani sambhavattā “attasambhava”nti laddhanāmaṃ sabbaṃ kilesajātaṃ abhindi, kilesābhāve kammaṃ appaṭisandhikattā avassaṭṭhaṃ nāma hoti, kilesābhāvena kammaṃ jahīti attho (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.169; udā. aṭṭha. 51).

Or alternatively, `tulaṃ` means weighing, investigating. `Atulañca sambhavaṃ` means both Nibbāna and existence. `Bhavasaṅkhāraṃ` means kamma that leads to existence. Regarding `avassaji muni`: weighing by the method beginning with, “The five aggregates are impermanent; their cessation, Nibbāna, is permanent,” the Buddha-sage, having seen the danger in existence and the benefit in Nibbāna, abandoned that existence-formation—the root of the aggregates—by means of the noble path which brings about the destruction of kamma. How did he abandon it? By delighting inwardly. Indeed, he, by way of insight, delights inwardly and, by way of serenity, is concentrated. He broke the entire mass of defilements—which stands enveloping the individual existence like armor and which, because it arises in oneself, has obtained the name `attasambhava` (self-arisen). And in the absence of defilements, kamma is called ‘abandoned’ because it does not cause rebirth-linking. “Through the absence of defilements, he abandoned kamma”—this is the meaning.

Saṅkhatāsaṅkhatadhātuvinimuttassa abhiññeyyassa abhāvato vuttaṃ “tula…pe… dhammāna”nti. Tena dhammapaṭisambhidā vuttā hotīti āha – “nikkhepapaññatti dhammapaṭisambhidāyā”ti. Bhavasaṅkhāre samudayapakkhiyaṃ sandhāyāha “pariccāgapaññattī”ti. Dukkhasaccapakkhiyavasena “pariññāpaññattī”ti. Samādhānavisiṭṭhassa [M 0.0124] ajjhattaratabhāvassa vasena “bhāvanāpaññatti kāyagatāya satiyā”ti vuttaṃ. Ajjhattaratatāvisiṭṭhassa pana samādhānassa vasena “ṭhitipaññatti cittekaggatāyā”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Abhinibbidāpaññatti cittassāti āyusaṅkhārossajjanavasena cittassa abhinīharaṇapaññatti. Upādānapaññattīti gahaṇapaññatti. Sabbaññutāyāti sammāsambuddhabhāvassa. Etena asammāsambuddhassa āyusaṅkhārossajjanaṃ natthīti dasseti. Kilesābhāvena bhagavā kammaṃ jahatīti dassento “padālanāpaññatti avijjaṇḍakosāna”nti āha.

Because there is no knowable thing that is free from the conditioned and unconditioned elements, it is said, “tula…pe… dhammānaṃ.” By that, the discrimination of phenomena is said to be spoken of; thus, he said, “The designation of classification is for the discrimination of phenomena.” Referring to that which is on the side of the truth of origin among the existence-formations, he said, “the designation of relinquishment.” By way of that which is on the side of the truth of suffering, it is “the designation of full understanding.” By way of the state of delighting internally which is distinguished by concentration, it is said, “The designation of development is for mindfulness directed to the body.” But it should be understood that by way of the concentration which is distinguished by the state of delighting internally, it is said, “The designation of stability is for one-pointedness of mind.” “The designation of disenchantment is of the mind” means the designation of directing the mind towards Parinibbāna by way of relinquishing the life-formation. “The designation of grasping” is the designation of seizing. `Sabbaññutāya` refers to the state of a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. By this, he shows that for one who is not a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, there is no relinquishing of the life-formation. Showing that “the Blessed One abandons kamma through the absence of defilements,” he said, “The designation of breaking open is of the eggshell of ignorance.”

Yo dukkhamaddakkhi yatonidānanti yo āraddhavipassako sabbaṃ tebhūmakaṃ dukkhaṃ adakkhi passi, tañca yatonidānaṃ yaṃ hetukaṃ, tampissa kāraṇabhāvena taṇhaṃ passi. Kāmesu so jantu kathaṃ [V 0.0250] nameyyāti so evaṃ paṭipanno puriso savatthukāmesu kilesakāmesu yena pakārena nameyya abhinameyya, so pakāro natthi. Kasmā? Kāmā hi loke saṅgoti ñatvā. Yasmā imasmiṃ loke kāmasadisaṃ bandhanaṃ natthi. Vuttañcetaṃ bhagavatā “na taṃ daḷhaṃ bandhanamāhu dhīrā”tiādi (dha. pa. 345; saṃ. ni. 1.121; netti. 106; peṭako 15), tasmā saṅkhāre āsajjanaṭṭhena saṅgoti viditvā. Tesaṃ satīmā vinayāya sikkheti kāyagatāsatiyogena satimā tesaṃ kāmānaṃ vūpasamāya tīsupi sikkhāsu appamatto sikkheyyāti attho.

Regarding “He who saw suffering and its origin”: Whatever person who has undertaken insight meditation saw all the suffering of the three planes; and that suffering has a certain cause, and he also saw that craving as its cause. Regarding “How could that being incline towards sensual pleasures?”: There is no way in which that person who has practiced thus would incline or bend towards sensual pleasures connected with objects and sensual pleasures that are defilements. Why? Because of knowing, “Sensual pleasures are an attachment in the world.” For in this world there is no bond like sensual pleasure. And this was said by the Blessed One: “The wise do not call that a strong bond,” and so on. Regarding “For their removal, the mindful one trains”: the meaning is that, having known that formations are an attachment due to their nature of clinging, one should train diligently in all three trainings for the calming of those sensual pleasures, being mindful through the practice of mindfulness directed to the body.

Vevacanapaññattīti khandhādīnaṃ vevacanapaññatti. Adakkhīti pana padena sambandhattā vuttaṃ – “dukkhassa pariññāpaññatti cā”ti. Paccatthikato dassanapaññattīti anatthajananato paccatthikato dassanapaññatti. Pāvakakappāti jalitaaggikkhandhasadisā. Papātauragopamāti papātūpamāuragopamā ca.

“The designation of synonyms” is the designation of synonyms for the aggregates and so on. But because of the connection with the word `adakkhi`, it is said, “and the designation of the full understanding of suffering.” “The designation of seeing as an adversary” is the designation of seeing as an adversary because it generates what is not beneficial. `Pāvakakappa` means similar to a mass of blazing fire. `Papātauragopamā` means both the simile of a precipice and the simile of a snake.

Mohasambandhano lokoti ayaṃ loko avijjāhetukehi saṃyojanehi bandho. Bhabbarūpova dissatīti vipannajjhāsayopi māyāya sāṭheyyena ca paṭicchāditasabhāvo bhabbajātikaṃ viya attānaṃ dasseti. Upadhibandhano bālo, tamasā parivāritoti tassa pana bālassa tathā dassane sammohatamasā parivāritattā kāmaguṇesu anādīnavadassitāya kilesābhisaṅkhārehi bandhattā. Tathā bhūto cāyaṃ [M 0.0125] bālo paṇḍitānaṃ assirī viya khāyati alakkhiko eva hutvā upaṭṭhāti. Tayidaṃ sabbaṃ bālassa sato rāgādikiñcanato. Paṇḍitassa pana paññācakkhunā passato natthi kiñcananti ayaṃ saṅkhepattho. Mohasīsena vipallāsā gahitāti āha – “desanāpaññatti vipallāsāna”nti. Viparītapaññattīti viparītākārena upaṭṭhahamānassa paññāpanā.

The world is bound by delusion: this world of beings is bound by the fetters that have ignorance as their cause. It appears as if capable: though one's disposition is corrupt, through deceit and trickery, one conceals one's true nature and presents oneself as if of a nature capable of liberation. The fool is bound by attachments, enveloped in darkness: for that fool, in so presenting himself, being enveloped by the darkness of delusion and not seeing the danger in sensual pleasures, is bound by the formations of defilements. Being thus, this fool appears to the wise as if without splendor; he presents himself as one lacking distinction. All this is so for the fool due to the impediment of lust and so on. But for the wise, who see with the eye of wisdom, there is no impediment. This is the brief meaning. The distortions are taken with delusion as their head; therefore, it is said: 'the teaching-designation of distortions.' Distorted designation: the designation of that which appears in a distorted manner.

Atthi nibbānanti samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ vācāvatthumattameva. Natthi nibbānanti paramatthato alabbhamānasabhāvattāti vippaṭipannānaṃ micchāvādaṃ bhañjituṃ bhagavatā vuttaṃ – “atthi, bhikkhave, ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhata”nti. Tattha hetuṃ dassetuṃ “no cetaṃ, bhikkhave”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassattho – bhikkhave, yadi asaṅkhatā dhātu na abhavissa, na idha sabbassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṃ siyā. Nibbānañhi ārammaṇaṃ katvā pavattamānā sammādiṭṭhiādayo maggadhammā anavasesakilese samucchindanti, tato tividhassapi vaṭṭassa appavattīti.

To refute the wrong view of those who have practiced wrongly—who hold that '[The statement] "There is Nibbāna" is merely a topic of speech for ascetics and brahmins,' and that 'There is no Nibbāna, because in an ultimate sense its nature is unattainable'—the Blessed One said: 'Monks, there is the unborn, the unbecome, the unmade, the unconditioned.' Therein, to show the reason, the passage beginning 'If it were not so, monks...' was spoken. Its meaning is as follows: Monks, if the unconditioned element did not exist, there would be no escape here from all that is conditioned. For, taking Nibbāna as their object, the arising path-factors—right view and so on—eradicate the defilements without remainder, and from that comes the non-occurrence of the threefold round.

Tatthāyamadhippāyo [V 0.0251] – yathā pariññeyyatāya sauttarānaṃ kāmānaṃ rūpānañca paṭipakkhabhūtaṃ tabbidhurasabhāvaṃ nissaraṇaṃ paññāyati, evaṃ taṃsabhāvānaṃ saṅkhabhadhammānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtena tabbidhuratāsabhāvena nissaraṇena bhavitabbaṃ, yañca taṃ nissaraṇaṃ. Sā asaṅkhatā dhātu. Kiñca bhiyyo? Saṅkhatadhammārammaṇaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ. Api ca anulomañāṇaṃ kilese na samucchedavasena pajahituṃ sakkoti. Sammutisaccārammaṇampi paṭhamajjhānādīsu ñāṇaṃ vikkhambhanamattameva karoti, kilesānaṃ na samucchedaṃ, samucchedappahānakarañca ariyamaggañāṇaṃ, tassa saṅkhatadhammasammutisaccaviparītena ārammaṇena bhavitabbaṃ, sā asaṅkhatā dhātu. Tathā nibbāna-saddo katthaci visaye aviparītattho veditabbo, upacāravuttisabbhāvato, yathā taṃ “sīhasaddo”ti.

Herein, this is the intended meaning: Just as for sense-sphere and form-sphere phenomena, which are to be fully understood and have a superior state beyond them, an escape is discerned that is their opposite, having a nature contrary to them; so too for conditioned phenomena, which are of such a nature, there must be an escape with a nature contrary to them, that is their opposite. And that escape is the unconditioned element. Furthermore, insight knowledge, which has conditioned phenomena as its object, even up to adaptation knowledge, is not able to abandon defilements by way of eradication. The knowledge occurring in the first jhāna and so on, which has conventional truth as its object, performs only suppression of the defilements, not eradication. But the noble path knowledge effects abandonment by eradication, and it must have an object that is the opposite of conditioned phenomena and conventional truth. That object is the unconditioned element. Thus, the word 'Nibbāna', due to the existence of its figurative usage, should be understood in a certain context as having a non-perverted meaning, just like the word 'lion'.

Atha vā “atthi, bhikkhave, ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhata”nti (udā. 73) vacanaṃ aviparītatthaṃ, bhagavatā bhāsitattā. Yañhi bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ, taṃ aviparītatthaṃ. Yathā taṃ “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā, sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā, sabbe dhammā anattā”ti (ma. ni. 1.353, 356; kathā. 753; cūḷani. ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 4; paṭi. ma. 1.31; netti. 5; dha. pa. 277-279), evampi yuttivasena asaṅkhatāya dhātuyā paramatthato sabbhāvo veditabbo. Kiṃ vā etāya yutticintāya? Yasmā bhagavatā [M 0.0126] “atthi, bhikkhave, ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhatanti (udā. 73), appaccayā dhammā asaṅkhatā dhammāti (dha. sa. dukamātikā 7-8) ca, asaṅkhatañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi asaṅkhatagāminiñca paṭipada”ntiādinā (saṃ. ni. 4.366-367, 377) ca anekehi suttapadehi nibbānadhātuyā paramatthato sabbhāvo desitoti. Tattha upanayanapaññattīti paṭipakkhato hetuupanayanassa paññāpanā. Jotanāpaññattīti paṭiññātassa atthassa siddhiyā pakāsanāpaññatti. Sesaṃ sabbaṃ suviññeyyameva.

Alternatively, the statement 'There is, bhikkhus, the unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned' is of non-perverted meaning, as it was spoken by the Blessed One. For whatever was spoken by the Blessed One is of non-perverted meaning, just as it is said, 'All conditioned things are impermanent, all conditioned things are suffering, all phenomena are not-self.' In this way too, by means of reason, the ultimate existence of the unconditioned element should be understood. Or what is the need for this line of reasoning? Because the Blessed One has declared the ultimate existence of the Nibbāna-element in many sutta passages, such as 'There is, bhikkhus, the unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned'; and 'States without conditions are unconditioned states'; and 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unconditioned, and the path leading to the unconditioned.' Therein, 'deductive designation' is the designation of adducing a reason from the opposite. 'Illustrative designation' is the designation that illuminates for the establishment of the acknowledged meaning. The rest is all easily understood.

Paññattihāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Analysis of the Mode of Designation is concluded.

12. Otaraṇahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā

12. The Explanation of the Analysis of the Mode of Descent

42. Tattha katamo otaraṇo hāroti otaraṇahāravibhaṅgo. Tattha asekkhā vimuttīti ayaṃ tedhātuke vītarāgatā asekkhā phalavimutti. Tāniyevāti tāni asekkhāyaṃ vimuttiyaṃ saddhādīni[V 0.0252]. Ayaṃ indriyehi otaraṇāti asekkhāya vimuttiyā niddhāritehi saddhādīhi indriyehi saṃvaṇṇanāya otaraṇā.

42. Herein, what is the mode of descent? It is the analysis of the mode of descent. Therein, as for 'the liberation of one beyond training': this freedom from passion in the three realms is the fruit-liberation of one beyond training. As for 'those very ones': those things beginning with faith in that liberation of one beyond training. As for 'this is the descent by way of the faculties': it is the descent by way of description through the faculties beginning with faith, which are ascertained in the liberation of one beyond training.

Pañcindriyāni vijjāti sammāsaṅkappo viya sammādiṭṭhiyā upakārakattā paññākkhandhe saddhādīni cattāri indriyāni vijjāya upakārakattā saṅgaṇhanavasena vuttāni. Saṅkhārapariyāpannānīti pañcasu khandhesu saṅkhārakkhandhe antogadhāni. Ye saṅkhārā anāsavāti taṃ saṅkhārakkhandhaṃ viseseti, aggaphalassa adhippetattā. Tato eva ca no bhavaṅgā. Dhammadhātusaṅgahitāti aṭṭhārasadhātūsu dhammadhātusaṅgahitā. Yadipi pubbe vītarāgatā asekkhā vimutti dassitā, tassā pana paṭipattidassanatthaṃ “ayaṃ ahamasmīti anānupassī”ti dassanamaggo idha vuttoti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “ayaṃ ahamasmīti anānupassī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sabbaṃ vuttanayameva.

In the context of 'the five faculties are wisdom': just as right intention is said to be included in the aggregate of wisdom because it is helpful to right view, so too the four faculties beginning with faith are said, by way of inclusion, to be helpful to wisdom. As for 'included in formations': they are included in the aggregate of formations among the five aggregates. By 'those formations that are untainted,' it qualifies that aggregate of formations, because the highest fruit is intended. And for that very reason, they are not a cause of existence. As for 'included in the element of phenomena': they are included by the element of phenomena among the eighteen elements. Although the liberation of one beyond training, being freedom from passion, was shown previously, in order to show the practice for it, the path of vision is stated here as 'not contemplating, "This I am."' To show this meaning, 'not contemplating, "This I am,"' and so on, is said. Everything is in the manner already stated.

43. Nissitassa calitanti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena kammaṃ anavaṭṭhānaṃ. Cutūpapātoti aparāparaṃ cavanaṃ upapatanañca. Nissitapade labbhamānaṃ nissayanaṃ uddharanto āha – “nissayo nāmā”ti. Taṇhānissayoti taṇhābhiniveso. So hi taṇhācaritassa patiṭṭhābhāvena tathā vutto. Evaṃ [M 0.0127] diṭṭhinissayopi daṭṭhabbo. Rattassa cetanāti cetanāpadhānattā saṅkhārakkhandhadhammānaṃ cetanāsīsena taṇhaṃ eva vadati. Tenevāha – “ayaṃ taṇhānissayo”ti. Yasmā pana viparītābhiniveso mohassa balavabhāve eva hoti, tasmā “yā mūḷhassa cetanā, ayaṃ diṭṭhinissayo”ti vuttaṃ.

43. As for 'for one who is dependent, there is wavering': it is trembling and unsteadiness by way of craving and views. As for 'passing away and rebirth': it is successive passing away and arising. Wishing to extract the meaning of 'support' found in the word 'dependent,' he said: 'Support is called...' As for 'dependence on craving': it is adherence through craving. Indeed, it is spoken of thus because it is a foundation for one whose conduct is characterized by craving. In the same way, dependence on views should also be understood. By 'the volition of one who is impassioned': because volition is predominant among the phenomena of the aggregate of formations, it speaks of craving itself with volition as the chief. For that very reason, he said: 'This is dependence on craving.' And because perverse adherence occurs only when delusion is strong, it is said: 'The volition of one who is deluded, this is dependence on views.'

Evaṃ cetanāsīsena taṇhādiṭṭhiyo vatvā idāni tattha nippariyāyena cetanaṃyeva gaṇhanto “cetanā pana saṅkhārā”ti āha. Yā rattassa vedanā, ayaṃ sukhā vedanāti sukhāya vedanāya rāgo anusetīti katvā vuttaṃ. Tathā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjā anusetīti āha – “yā sammūḷhassa vedanā, ayaṃ adukkhamasukhā vedanā”ti. Idha vedanāsīsena cetanā vuttā. Taṇhāyāti taṇhaṃ. Diṭṭhiyāti diṭṭhiṃ. Yathā vā sesadhammānaṃ taṇhāya nissayabhāve puggalo taṇhāya nissitoti vuccati. Evaṃ taṇhāya sesadhammānaṃ paccayabhāve puggalo taṇhāya nissitoti vuccatīti āha – “taṇhāya anissito”ti.

Thus, having spoken of craving and views with volition as the chief, now, taking up volition itself directly therein, he said, 'But volition is formations.' As for 'the feeling of one who is impassioned, this is pleasant feeling,' it is said because of holding that 'passion lies latent in pleasant feeling.' Similarly, because 'ignorance lies latent in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,' he said, 'the feeling of one who is utterly deluded, this is neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.' Here, volition is spoken of with feeling as the chief. 'By craving' means 'craving' (accusative). 'By view' means 'view' (accusative). Or, just as when craving is the state of being a support for other phenomena, a person is said to be the support of craving. Similarly, when other phenomena are the state of being a condition for craving, a person is said to be dependent on craving. Therefore, he said, 'not dependent on craving.'

Passaddhīti darathapaṭippassambhanā. Kāyikāti karajakāyasannissitā. Cetasikāti cittasannissitā. Yasmā pana sā darathapaṭippassaddhi kāyacittānaṃ sukhe sati pākaṭā hoti, tasmā [V 0.0253] “yaṃ kāyikaṃ sukha”ntiādinā phalūpacārena vuttāya passaddhiyā natiabhāvassa kāraṇabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “passaddhakāyo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Soti evaṃ vimuttacitto khīṇāsavo. Rūpasaṅkhaye vimuttoti rūpānaṃ saṅkhayasaṅkhāte nibbāne vimutto. Atthītipi na upetīti sassato attā ca loko cātipi taṇhādiṭṭhiupayena na upeti na gaṇhāti. Natthīti asassatoti. Atthi natthīti ekaccaṃ sassataṃ ekaccaṃ asassatanti. Nevatthi no natthīti amarāvikkhepavasena. Gambhīroti uttānabhāvahetūnaṃ kilesānaṃ abhāvena gambhīro. Nibbutoti atthītiādinā upagamanakilesānaṃ vūpasamena parinibbuto sītibhūto.

As for 'tranquility': it is the calming of agitation. As for 'bodily': it is tranquility dependent on the body born of kamma. As for 'mental': it is tranquility dependent on the mind. And because that calming of agitation becomes manifest when there is happiness of body and mind, therefore, with terms beginning 'bodily happiness,' in order to show, by way of a metaphor of the fruit, the state of being a cause for the absence of inclination of the aforesaid tranquility, 'one with a tranquil body,' and so on, is said. As for 'he': it is the Arahant, thus with a liberated mind and exhausted taints. As for 'liberated in the destruction of form': he is liberated in Nibbāna, which is described as the destruction of forms. As for 'he does not even approach "it exists"': he does not approach or grasp by means of the adherence of craving and view that 'the self and the world are eternal.' As for 'it does not exist': it means 'not eternal.' As for 'it exists and does not exist': it means 'some is eternal, some is not eternal.' As for 'it neither exists nor does not exist': it is by way of endless equivocation. As for 'profound': he is profound through the absence of the defilements that are the cause of shallowness. As for 'extinguished': by the calming of the defilements of approaching, beginning with 'it exists,' he is fully extinguished, become cool.

Idhāgatīti paralokato idha āgati. Gatīti idhalokato paralokagamanaṃ. Taṃ pana punabbhavoti āha “peccabhavo”ti. Idha huranti dvārārammaṇadhammā dassitāti “ubhayamantarenā”ti padena dvārappavattadhamme dassento “phassasamuditesu dhammesū”ti āha. Tassattho – phassena [M 0.0128] saddhiṃ phassena kāraṇabhūtena ca samuditesu sambhūtesu viññāṇavedanāsaññācetanāvitakkavicārādidhammesu. Attānaṃ na passatīti tesaṃ dhammānaṃ anattabhāveneva tattha attānaṃ na passati. Virajjati virāgā vimuccatīti padehi lokuttaradhammānaṃ paṭiccasamuppādabhāvaṃ dassento tadatthatāya sīlādīnampi pariyāyena tabbhāvamāha “lokuttaro”tiādinā.

As for 'coming here': it is coming here to this existence from the next world. As for 'going': it is going from this existence to the next world. That, however, is new existence; therefore, he said, 'existence after death.' By the words 'here' (idha) and 'beyond' (huraṃ), the phenomena of the door and the object are shown. Therefore, showing the phenomena that occur at the door with the phrase 'between the two,' he said, 'in phenomena arisen from contact.' The meaning of this is: in phenomena such as consciousness, feeling, perception, volition, initial thought, and sustained thought, which have arisen together with contact and with contact that has become the cause. As for 'he does not see a self': it is only through the not-self nature of those phenomena that he does not see a self therein. With the words 'he becomes dispassionate, through dispassion he is liberated,' the teacher, wishing to show the state of being dependently arisen for supramundane phenomena, also speaks indirectly of that state for virtue and so on, for that same purpose, with the words beginning 'supramundane.'

44. Nāmasampayuttoti nāmena missito. Saupādisesā nibbānadhātūti arahattaphalaṃ adhippetaṃ. Tañca paññāpadhānanti āha – “saupādisesā nibbānadhātu vijjāti. Sesaṃ sabbaṃ uttānameva.

44. As for 'associated with mentality': it means 'mingled with mentality.' In this phrase, 'the Nibbāna-element with residue remaining,' the fruit of Arahantship is intended. And that fruit of Arahantship has wisdom as its chief; therefore, he said: 'The Nibbāna-element with residue remaining is wisdom.' All the rest is self-evident.

Otaraṇahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Analysis of the Mode of Descent is concluded.

13. Sodhanahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā

13. The Explanation of the Analysis of the Mode of Clarification

45. Tattha katamo sodhano hāroti sodhanahāravibhaṅgo. Tattha bhagavā padaṃ sodhetīti “avijjāya nivuto loko”ti (su. ni. 1039; cūḷani. ajitamāṇavapucchā 58, ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 2) vadanto bhagavā – “kenassu nivuto loko”ti (su. ni. 1038; cūḷani. ajitamāṇavapucchā 57, ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 1) āyasmatā ajitena [V 0.0254] pucchāvasena vuttaṃ padaṃ sodheti nāma, tadatthassa vissajjanato. No ca ārambhanti na tāva ārambhaṃ sodheti, ñātuṃ icchitassa atthassa apariyositattā. Suddho ārambhoti ñātuṃ icchitassa atthassa pabodhitattā sodhito ārambhoti attho. Aññāṇapakkhandānaṃ dveḷhakajātānaṃ vā pucchanakāle pucchitānaṃ pucchāvisayo avijaṭaṃ mahāgahanaṃ viya mahāduggaṃ viya ca andhakāraṃ avibhūtaṃ hoti. Yadā ca bhagavatā paṇḍitehi vā bhagavato sāvakehi apade padaṃ dassentehi nijjaṭaṃ nigumbaṃ katvā pañhe vissajjite mahatā gandhahatthinā abhibhavitvā obhaggapadālito gahanappadeso viya vigatandhakāro vibhūto upaṭṭhahamāno visodhito nāma hoti.

45. Herein, what is the mode of clarification? This is the analysis of the mode of clarification. Herein, the Blessed One clarifies a phrase. When the Blessed One, speaking thus: “The world is shrouded by ignorance,” clarifies the phrase “By what is the world shrouded?” which was spoken by Venerable Ajita by way of a question, this is called clarifying the phrase, because its meaning is explained. ‘No ca ārambhanti,’ meaning, he does not yet clarify the undertaking, because the meaning desired to be known is not yet fully concluded. ‘Suddho ārambho,’ meaning, the undertaking is clarified because the meaning desired to be known has been made clear. For those whose ignorance rushes forth or who have become doubtful, at the time of questioning, the subject of their question is entangled like a great thicket and a great wilderness; it is darkness and is unmanifest. But when the Blessed One or his wise disciples, by showing the footing in what is not a footing, make the questions free from entanglement and thickets, and answer them—then, like a thicket-region overwhelmed, broken, and trampled by a great scented elephant, it becomes free of darkness, manifest, standing forth, and is called clarified.

Sodhanahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Analysis of the Mode of Clarification is concluded.

14. Adhiṭṭhānahāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā

14. The Explanation of the Analysis of the Mode of Determination

46. Tattha [M 0.0129] katamo adhiṭṭhāno hāroti adhiṭṭhānahāravibhaṅgo. Tattha tathā dhārayitabbāti ekattavemattatāsaṅkhātasāmaññavisesamattato dhārayitabbā, na pana tattha kiñci vikappetabbāti adhippāyo. Avikappetabbatāya kāraṇaṃ niddesavāravaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttameva. Taṃ taṃ phalaṃ maggati gavesatīti maggo, tadatthikehi maggīyati gavesīyatīti vā maggo. Niratiyaṭṭhena nirassādaṭṭhena ca nirayo. Uddhaṃ anugantvā tiriyaṃ añcitāti tiracchānā. Tiracchānāva tiracchānayoni. Petatāya petti, ito pecca gatabhāvoti attho. Petti eva pettivisayo. Na suranti na bhāsanti na dibbantīti asurā. Asurā eva asurayoni. Dibbehi rūpādīhi suṭṭhu aggāti saggā. Manassa ussannatāya manussā. Vānaṃ vuccati taṇhā, taṃ tattha natthīti nibbānaṃ. Nirayaṃ gacchatīti nirayagāmī. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Asurayoniyoti asurayoniyā hito, asurajātinibbattanakoti attho. Saggaṃ gametīti saggagāmiyo. Manussagāmīti manussalokagāmī. Paṭisaṅkhānirodhoti paṭisaṅkhāya paṭipakkhabhāvanāya nirodho, paṭipakkhe vā tathā appavatte uppajjanārahassa paṭipakkhavuttiyā anuppādo. Appaṭisaṅkhānirodhoti saṅkhatadhammānaṃ sarasanirodho, khaṇikanirodhoti attho.

46. Herein, what is the mode of determination? This is the analysis of the mode of determination. Herein, “it should be comprehended thus,” meaning, it should be comprehended as unity and diversity, in terms of commonality and particularity, and nothing should be conceptualized there. The reason for not conceptualizing has already been stated in the explanation of the analysis section. “It seeks that fruit, it searches for it, thus it is a path; or, it is sought and searched for by those who desire it, thus it is a path.” Hell (niraya) is so called because of its meaning of being without delight (nirati) and without savor (nirassāda). Tiracchānā are so called because they go horizontally, not going upwards. Tiracchānāyoni is simply the animal realm. Petti is the state of being a peta, meaning the state of having gone from here after death. Pettivisayo is simply the realm of petas. Asurā are so called because they do not shine (na suranti), do not speak (na bhāsanti), and do not enjoy divine pleasures (na dibbanti). Asurayoni is simply the demon realm. Saggā are so called because they are excellent (suṭṭhu agga) due to divine forms and so on. Manussā are so called because of the preponderance of the mind (manassa ussannatā). Vāna is called craving; Nibbāna is so called because that (craving) is not present there. One who goes to hell is a hell-goer. The same method applies to the remaining terms. Asurayoniyo means “conducive to the asura realm,” meaning “causing birth in the asura species.” One who leads to heaven is a heaven-goer. A human-goer is one who goes to the human world. Paṭisaṅkhānirodho is cessation by means of reflection and the development of the opposite; or, when the opposite does not occur in that way, it is the non-arising of that which is fit to arise due to the occurrence of the opposite. Appaṭisaṅkhānirodho is the spontaneous cessation of conditioned phenomena, meaning momentary cessation.

47. Rūpanti ekattatā. Bhūtānaṃ upādāyāti vemattatā. Upādārūpanti ekattatā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāroti vemattatā. Tathā bhūtarūpanti ekattatā. Pathavīdhātu [V 0.0255] …pe… vāyodhātūti vemattatā. Pathavīdhātūti ekattatā. Vīsati ākārā vemattatā. Āpodhātūti ekattatā. Dvādasa ākārā vemattatā. Tejodhātūti ekattatā. Cattāro ākārā vemattatā. Vāyodhātūti ekattatā. Cha ākārā vemattatāti imamatthaṃ dassento “dvīhi ākārehi dhātuyo pariggaṇhātī”tiādimāha.

47. 'Material form' is unity. 'Of primary elements and derived materiality' is diversity. 'Derived material form' is unity. 'The eye-base… and so on… edible food' is diversity. Similarly, 'primary material form' is unity. 'The earth element… and so on… the air element' is diversity. 'The earth element' is unity. Twenty aspects are diversity. 'The water element' is unity. Twelve aspects are diversity. 'The fire element' is unity. Four aspects are diversity. 'The air element' is unity. Six aspects are diversity. To show this meaning, he stated the passage beginning, “He comprehends the elements in two ways.”

Tattha kesāti kesā nāma upādinnakasarīraṭṭhakā kakkhaḷalakkhaṇā imasmiṃ sarīre pāṭiyekko pathavīdhātukoṭṭhāso. Lomā nāma…pe… matthaluṅgaṃ nāma sarīraṭṭhakaṃ kakkhaḷalakkhaṇaṃ imasmiṃ sarīre pāṭiyekko koṭṭhāsoti ayaṃ vemattatā. Āpodhātūtiādikoṭṭhāsesu pittādīsu [M 0.0130] eseva nayo. Ayaṃ pana viseso – yena cāti yena tejodhātunā kupitena. Santappatīti ayaṃ kāyo santappati ekāhikajarādibhāvena usumajāto hoti. Yena ca jīrīyatīti yena ayaṃ kāyo jarīyati. Indriyavekallataṃ balakkhayaṃ valittacapalitādiñca pāpuṇāti.
