Regarding 'having placed right view foremost': by having right intention as one's range, one has dispelled wrong views; and having made right view—which is characterized by the understanding of kamma as one's own and by the knowledge of things as they truly are—the forerunner, one is diligently engaged in virtue and concentration. And precisely from that, 'having known rise and fall'—that is, having known the arising and cessation in the five aggregates of clinging according to the fifty aspects, and having aroused insight—while gradually grasping the noble paths, by means of the supreme path, 'a monk, overcoming sloth and torpor, should abandon all miserable destinations.' Thus, a monk, being one whose defilements are broken, a destroyer of taints, should, as is possible, abandon all destinations designated as 'miserable' due to their connection with the threefold suffering. Beyond those destinations, one would be established in Nibbāna. This is the meaning.

Yaṃ taṇhāya avijjāya ca pahānaṃ, ayaṃ nirodhoti pahānassa nirodhassa paccayabhāvato asaṅkhatadhātu pahānaṃ nirodhoti ca vuttā. Imāni cattāri saccānīti purimagāthāya purimāni dve, pacchimagāthāya pacchimāni dveti dvīhi gāthāhi bhāsitāni imāni cattāri ariyasaccāni. Tesu samudayena assādo, dukkhena ādīnavo, magganirodhehi nissaraṇaṃ, sabbagatijahanaṃ phalaṃ, rakkhitacittatādiko upāyo, arakkhitacittatādinisedhanamukhena rakkhitacittatādīsu niyojanaṃ bhagavato āṇattīti. Evaṃ desanāhārapadatthā assādādayo niddhāretabbā. Tenevāha – “niyutto desanāhārasampāto”ti.

'The abandonment of craving and ignorance, this is cessation.' Because it is the condition for abandonment and cessation, the unconditioned element is called both 'abandonment' and 'cessation.' 'These are the Four Truths': the first two in the former verse and the latter two in the latter verse—thus, these Four Noble Truths are spoken of in two verses. Among them, gratification is through the origin; danger is through suffering; escape is through the path and cessation; the abandonment of all destinations is the fruit; having a guarded mind and so on is the means; the Blessed One’s instruction is the urging towards having a guarded mind and so on by way of prohibiting an unguarded mind and so on. In this way, gratification and so on, which are the meanings of the terms of the 'Conveying the Teaching' method, should be determined. Therefore, he said: 'The convergence of the Conveying the Teaching method is applied.'

Desanāhārasampātavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Convergence of the Conveying the Teaching Method is concluded.

2. Vicayahārasampātavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Convergence of the Scrutiny Method

53. Evaṃ [M 0.0147] desanāhārasampātaṃ dassetvā idāni vicayahārasampātaṃ dassento yasmā desanāhārapadatthavicayo vicayahāro, tasmā desanāhāre vipallāsahetubhāvena niddhāritāya taṇhāya kusalādivibhāgapavicayamukhena vicayahārasampātaṃ dassetuṃ “tattha taṇhā duvidhā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha kusalāti kusaladhammārammaṇā. Kusala-saddo cettha bāhitikasutte (ma. ni. 2.358 ādayo) viya anavajjatthe daṭṭhabbo. Kasmā panettha taṇhā kusalapariyāyena uddhaṭā? Heṭṭhā desanāhāre vipallāsahetubhāvena taṇhaṃ uddharitvā tassā vasena saṃkilesapakkho [V 0.0271] dassito. Vicittapaṭibhānatāya pana idhāpi taṇhāmukheneva vodānapakkhaṃ dassetuṃ kusalapariyāyena taṇhā uddhaṭā. Tattha saṃsāraṃ gametīti saṃsāragāminī, saṃsāranāyikāti attho. Apacayaṃ nibbānaṃ gametīti apacayagāminī. Kathaṃ pana taṇhā apacayagāminīti? Āha “pahānataṇhā”ti. Tadaṅgādippahānassa hetubhūtā taṇhā. Kathaṃ pana ekantasāvajjāya taṇhāya kusalabhāvoti? Sevitabbabhāvato. Yathā taṇhā, evaṃ mānopi duvidho kusalopi akusalopi, na taṇhā evāti taṇhāya nidassanabhāvena māno vutto.

53. Having thus shown the convergence of the method of teaching, now, in showing the convergence of the method of scrutiny—because the scrutiny of the meaning of the terms in the method of teaching is the method of scrutiny—therefore, in order to show the convergence of the method of scrutiny by means of scrutinizing the division into wholesome and so on with regard to craving, which was determined in the method of teaching as the cause of perversion, the text beginning 'Therein, craving is twofold' is introduced. Therein, 'wholesome' means having wholesome states as its object. And here the word 'wholesome' should be understood in the sense of 'blameless,' as in the Bāhitika Sutta. Why, then, is craving presented here by way of the wholesome? Below, in the method of teaching, having extracted craving as the cause of perversion, the side of defilement was shown through its power. But here, due to ingenuity, in order to show the side of purification precisely by means of craving, craving is presented by way of the wholesome. Therein, 'it leads to saṃsāra' (saṃsāraṃ gameti), thus it is 'leading to saṃsāra' (saṃsāragāminī); the meaning is 'leader to saṃsāra' (saṃsāranāyikā). 'It leads to cessation' (apacayaṃ gameti), thus it is 'leading to cessation' (apacayagāminī); apacaya is Nibbāna. But how is craving 'leading to cessation'? He said: 'craving for abandonment.' It is craving that is the cause for abandonment by substitution and so on. But how can there be a wholesome quality for craving, which is entirely faulty? Because it is to be cultivated. Just as craving, so too is conceit twofold—wholesome and unwholesome. It is not only craving that is twofold; thus, conceit is mentioned as an illustration for craving.

Tattha mānassa yathādhippetaṃ kusalādibhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ mānaṃ nissāyā”tiādimāha. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā – “mānamahaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi sevitabbampi asevitabbampī”tiādi. Yaṃ nekkhammassitaṃ domanassantiādi “kusalā”ti vuttataṇhāya sarūpadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha nekkhammassitaṃ domanassaṃ nāma –

Therein, to show the intended wholesome nature and so on of conceit, he stated the text beginning, 'Depending on which conceit…' For this was said by the Blessed One: 'Conceit, O lord of the devas, I declare in two ways: as that which is to be cultivated and that which is not to be cultivated,' and so on. The text beginning, 'The sorrow based on renunciation…' is stated to show the nature of the craving that was called 'wholesome.' Therein, what is called 'sorrow based on renunciation' is—

“Tattha katamāni cha nekkhammassitāni domanassāni? Rūpānaṃtveva aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmavirāganirodhaṃ ‘pubbe ceva rūpā etarahi ca, sabbete rūpā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti ‘kudāssu nāmāhaṃ tadāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharissāmi, yadariyā etarahi āyatanaṃ upasampajja viharantī’ti. Iti anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato uppajjati [M 0.0148] pihā, pihāpaccayā domanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ domanassaṃ, idaṃ vuccati nekkhammassitaṃ domanassa”nti (ma. ni. 3.307) –

“Here, what are the six sorrows dependent on renunciation? Having known the impermanence of forms, their alteration, fading away, and cessation, and having seen this with right wisdom as it really is: ‘Forms that existed previously and also now—all those forms are impermanent, suffering, and subject to alteration,’ one establishes a yearning for the unsurpassed liberations: ‘When, indeed, shall I attain and dwell in that sphere which the noble ones now attain and dwell in?’ Thus, for one who establishes a yearning for the unsurpassed liberations, yearning arises; with yearning as a condition, sorrow arises. Whatever sorrow is of such a nature, this is called ‘sorrow dependent on renunciation.’”

Evaṃ chasu dvāresu iṭṭhārammaṇe āpāthagate anuttaravimokkhasaṅkhātaariyaphaladhammesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā tadadhigamāya aniccādivasena vipassanaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā ussukkāpetuṃ asakkontassa “imampi pakkhaṃ imampi māsaṃ, imampi saṃvaccharaṃ, vipassanaṃ ussukkāpetvā ariyabhūmiṃ sampāpuṇituṃ nāsakkhi”nti anusocato uppannaṃ domanassaṃ nekkhammavasena vipassanāvasena anussativasena paṭhamajjhānādivasena paṭipattiyā hetubhāvena uppajjanato nekkhammassitaṃ domanassaṃ nāma. Ayaṃ taṇhā kusalāti ayaṃ “pihā”ti vuttā taṇhā kusalā. Kathaṃ? Rāgavirāgā cetovimutti, tadārammaṇā kusalāti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – rāgavirāgā cetovimutti, na sabhāvena kusalā, anavajjaṭṭhena kusalā. Taṃ uddissa pavattiyā tadārammaṇā pana taṇhā kusalārammaṇatāya kusalāti. Avijjāvirāgā paññāvimutti anavajjaṭṭhena kusalā. Tassāti paññāvimuttiyā[V 0.0272]. Yāya vasena “tasmā rakkhitacittassā”ti gāthāyaṃ “sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti vuttaṃ.

Thus, when a desirable object comes into range at the six doors, having established a yearning for the noble fruition-states, which are designated as the unsurpassed liberations, for one who is unable to strive to attain them by establishing insight into impermanence and so on, and who grieves, 'For this fortnight, this month, this year, I was unable to strive in insight and attain the noble plane'—the sorrow that arises for one so grieving is called 'sorrow based on renunciation' because it arises as a cause for the practice by way of renunciation, by way of insight, by way of recollection, by way of the first jhāna, and so on. 'This craving is wholesome' means this craving called 'yearning' is wholesome. How so? The liberation of mind through dispassion for lust is wholesome; having that as its object, the craving is wholesome. This is what is meant: the liberation of mind through dispassion for lust is not wholesome by its intrinsic nature; it is wholesome in the sense of being blameless. But because it arises directed towards that, the craving that has that as its object is wholesome due to having a wholesome object. The liberation by wisdom through the fading of ignorance is wholesome in the sense of being blameless. 'Of that' (tassā) means of the liberation by wisdom. It is by means of this that in the verse beginning, 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind,' it is said, 'one would abandon all bad destinations.'

Iti cirataraṃ vipassanāparivāsaṃ parivasitvā dukkhāpaṭipadādandhābhiññāya adhigatāya paññāvimuttiyā vasena vicayahārasampātaṃ dassetuṃ “tassā ko pavicayo”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yasmā paññāvimutti ariyamaggamūlikā, tasmā catutthajjhānapādake ariyamaggadhamme uddisitvā tesaṃ āgamanapaṭipadaṃ dassetuṃ “kattha daṭṭhabbo, catutthe jhāne”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha pāramitāyāti ukkaṃsagatāya catutthajjhānabhāvanāya. Yehi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgataṃ catutthajjhānacittaṃ vuttaṃ, tāni aṅgāni dassetuṃ “parisuddha”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

Thus, having for a very long time undertaken the practice of insight, in order to demonstrate the convergence of the method of scrutiny by means of the liberation by wisdom attained through difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, the text beginning, 'What is its scrutiny?' is introduced. Therein, since liberation by wisdom is rooted in the noble path, therefore, having pointed out the noble path factors that have the fourth jhāna as their basis, in order to show the practice that leads to them, the text beginning, 'Where is it to be seen? In the fourth jhāna,' was stated. Therein, 'by perfection' (pāramitāya) means by the cultivation of the fourth jhāna that has reached excellence. In order to show those eight factors with which the fourth jhāna consciousness is said to be endowed, the text beginning, 'purified,' was stated.

Tattha upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvena parisuddhaṃ. Parisuddhattā eva pariyodātaṃ, pabhassaranti vuttaṃ hoti. Sukhādīnaṃ paccayaghātena vītarāgādiaṅgaṇattā anaṅgaṇaṃ. Anaṅgaṇattā eva vigatūpakkilesaṃ, aṅgaṇena hi cittaṃ upakkilissati, subhāvitattā mudubhūtaṃ vasibhāvappattanti attho. Vase vattamānañhi cittaṃ “mudū”ti vuccati. Muduttā eva ca kammaniyaṃ, kammakkhamaṃ kammayogganti attho. Muduñhi cittaṃ kammaniyaṃ hoti[M 0.0149], evaṃ bhāvitaṃ muduñca hoti kammaniyañca, yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, citta”nti (a. ni. 1.22). Etesu parisuddhabhāvādīsu ṭhitattā ṭhitaṃ. Ṭhitattāyeva āneñjappattaṃ, acalaṃ niriñjananti attho. Mudukammaññabhāvena vā attano vase ṭhitattā ṭhitaṃ. Saddhādīhi pariggahitattā āneñjappattaṃ. Saddhāpariggahitañhi cittaṃ assaddhiyena na iñjati, vīriyapariggahitaṃ kosajjena na iñjati, satipariggahitaṃ pamādena na iñjati, samādhipariggahitaṃ uddhaccena na iñjati, paññāpariggahitaṃ avijjāya na iñjati, obhāsagataṃ kilesandhakārena na iñjati. Imehi chahi dhammehi pariggahitaṃ āneñjappattaṃ hoti. Evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ cittaṃ abhinīhārakkhamaṃ hoti. Abhiññāsacchikaraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ abhiññāsacchikiriyāya.

Herein, it is purified by the nature of the purity of mindfulness brought about by equanimity. Because it is purified, it is said to be clarified and radiant. Through the destruction of the conditions for pleasure and so on, because of being without the stain of passion and other defilements, it is unstained. Being unstained, it is free from corruptions—for the mind is corrupted by a stain. Because it is well-developed, it has become soft; the meaning is that it has attained mastery. For a mind that exists under mastery is called 'soft.' And because it is soft, it is workable—that is, capable of work and fit for work. For a soft mind is workable, just as it is said: '...a mind thus developed is both soft and workable, just as, O monks, this mind' (AN 1.22). Because it is established in these states of purity and so on, it is steady. Because it is steady, it has attained imperturbability—that is, unmoving and unshaken. Or, because of its state of softness and workability, it is steady by being established in one's own control. Because it is embraced by faith and so on, it has attained imperturbability. For a mind embraced by faith is not shaken by lack of faith. A mind embraced by energy is not shaken by laziness. A mind embraced by mindfulness is not shaken by heedlessness. A mind embraced by concentration is not shaken by restlessness. A mind embraced by wisdom is not shaken by ignorance. A mind that has reached illumination is not shaken by the darkness of defilements. Embraced by these six qualities, it attains imperturbability. Thus, a mind endowed with these eight factors is fit for directing, for the realization through direct knowledge of the things to be realized through direct knowledge.

Aparo nayo – catutthajjhānasamādhinā samāhitaṃ cittaṃ nīvaraṇadūrībhāvena parisuddhaṃ. Vitakkādisamatikkamena pariyodātaṃ. Jhānapaṭilābhapaccanīkānaṃ pāpakānaṃ icchāvacarānaṃ abhāvena anaṅgaṇaṃ. Icchāvacarānanti icchāya avacarānaṃ icchāvasena otiṇṇānaṃ pavattānaṃ nānappakārānaṃ kopaapaccayānanti attho. Abhijjhādīnaṃ cittupakkilesānaṃ vigamena vigatūpakkilesaṃ. Ubhayampi cetaṃ anaṅgaṇasuttavatthasuttānaṃ (ma. ni. 1.57 ādayo; 70 ādayo) vasena [V 0.0273] veditabbaṃ. Vasippattiyā mudubhūtaṃ. Iddhipādabhāvūpagamena kammaniyaṃ. Bhāvanāpāripūriyā paṇītabhāvūpagamena ṭhitaṃ āneñjappattaṃ. Yathā āneñjabhāvappattaṃ āneñjappattaṃ hoti, evaṃ ṭhitanti attho. Evampi aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ cittaṃ abhinīhārakkhamaṃ hoti. Abhiññāsacchikaraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ abhiññāsacchikiriyāya pādakaṃ padaṭṭhānabhūtaṃ. Tenevāha – “so tattha aṭṭhavidhaṃ adhigacchati cha abhiññā dve ca visese”ti.

Another method: the mind concentrated by the concentration of the fourth jhāna is purified by being distant from the hindrances. It is cleansed by the transcendence of initial and sustained thought. It is unblemished due to the absence of evil and volitional states that oppose the attainment of jhāna. 'Volitional states' means various kinds of anger-based conditions that arise driven by volition, by being associated with volition. By the removal of mental corruptions such as covetousness, it is free from corruptions. Both should be understood in accordance with the Anaṅgaṇa Sutta and the Vatthasutta (M.I, 57ff.; 70ff.). It is softened by mastery. It is workable due to the development of the bases of psychic power. It is steady, having attained imperturbability, due to the perfection of development and the attainment of refinement. Just as one who has attained imperturbability is called 'one who has attained imperturbability,' so too it is steady—this is the meaning. In this way also, a mind endowed with these eight factors is fit for directing. It serves as the foundation and proximate cause for the direct realization of things to be directly known. Therefore, it is said: 'There, one attains eight kinds—the six direct knowledges and the two special qualities.'

Tattha soti adhigatacatutthajjhāno yogī. Tatthāti tasmiṃ catutthajjhāne adhiṭṭhānabhūte. Aṭṭhavidhaṃ adhigacchatīti aṭṭhavidhaṃ guṇaṃ adhigacchati. Ko pana so aṭṭhavidho guṇoti? Āha “cha abhiññā dve ca visese”ti. Manomayiddhi vipassanāñāṇañca. Taṃ cittanti catutthajjhānacittaṃ. “Yato parisuddhaṃ, tato pariyodāta”ntiādinā purimaṃ purimaṃ pacchimassa pacchimassa kāraṇavacananti dasseti. Tadubhayanti yesaṃ rāgādiaṅgaṇānaṃ abhijjhādiupakkilesānañca abhāvena “anaṅgaṇaṃ vigatūpakkilesa”nti [M 0.0150] ca vuttaṃ. Tāni aṅgaṇāni upakkilesā cāti taṃ ubhayaṃ. Tadubhayaṃ taṇhāsabhāvattā taṇhāya anulomanato ca taṇhāpakkho. Yā ca iñjanāti yā ca cittassa asamādānena phandanā. Aṭṭhitīti anavaṭṭhānaṃ. Ayaṃ diṭṭhipakkhoti yā iñjanā aṭṭhiti ca, ayaṃ micchābhinivesahetutāya diṭṭhipakkho.

Therein, 'he' refers to the yogī who has attained the fourth jhāna. 'Therein' means in that fourth jhāna, which serves as the basis. 'He attains eightfold' means he attains an eightfold quality. But what is that eightfold quality? It is said: 'six direct knowledges and two special qualities.' These are the mind-made psychic power and the knowledge of insight. 'That mind' refers to the fourth jhāna consciousness. By the phrase beginning 'Because it is purified, therefore it is bright,' it shows that each preceding term is a statement of the cause for each succeeding term. 'Both of these' refers to those stains such as passion and those corruptions such as covetousness, due to the absence of which it was called 'unstained' and 'free from corruptions'; those stains and corruptions are what is meant by 'both of these'. Both of these, due to their nature of craving and their conformity to craving, belong to the faction of craving. 'Agitation' is the trembling of the mind due to lack of concentration. 'Unsteadiness' is instability. 'This is the faction of views' means: this agitation and unsteadiness belong to the faction of views because they are a cause for wrong adherence.

“Cattāri indriyānī”tiādinā vedanātopi catutthajjhānaṃ vibhāveti. Evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ catutthajjhānacittaṃ upari abhiññādhigamāya abhinīhārakkhamaṃ hoti. Sā ca abhinīhārakkhamatā cuddasahi ākārehi ciṇṇavasibhāvasseva hoti. So ca vasibhāvo aṭṭhasamāpattilābhino, na rūpāvacarajjhānamattalābhinoti āruppasamāpattiyā manasikāravidhiṃ dassento “so uparimaṃ samāpattiṃ santato manasikarotī”tiādimāha. Tattha uparimaṃ samāpattinti ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiṃ. Santato manasikarotīti aṅgasantatāyapi ārammaṇasantatāyapi “santā”ti manasikaroti. Yato yato hi āruppasamāpattiṃ santato manasikaroti, tato tato rūpāvacarajjhānaṃ avūpasantaṃ hutvā upaṭṭhāti. Tenevāha – “tassa uparimaṃ…pe… saṇṭhahatī”ti. Ukkaṇṭhā ca paṭighasaññāti paṭighasaññāsaṅkhātāsu pañcaviññāṇasaññāsu anabhirati saṇṭhahati. “So sabbaso”tiādinā ekadesena āruppasamāpattiṃ dasseti. Abhiññābhinīhāro rūpasaññāti rūpāvacarasaññā nāmetā yāvadeva abhiññatthābhinīhāramattaṃ, na pana arūpāvacarasamāpattiyo viya santāti adhippāyo. Vokāro nānattasaññāti [V 0.0274] nānattasaññā nāmetā nānārammaṇesu vokāro, tattha cittassa ākulappavattīti attho. Samatikkamatīti evaṃ tattha ādīnavadassī hutvā tā samatikkamati. Paṭighasaññā cassa abbhatthaṃ gacchatīti assa ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiṃ adhigacchantassa yogino dasapi paṭighasaññā vigacchanti. Iminā paṭhamāruppasamāpattimāha.

By “Four faculties,” etc., he elucidates the fourth jhāna even from the perspective of feeling. Thus, the fourth jhāna consciousness, endowed with eight factors, becomes fit for directing the mind to the attainment of higher knowledge. And that fitness for directing the mind is only for one who has cultivated mastery in fourteen ways. And that mastery belongs to one who has attained the eight attainments, not to one who has attained only the form-sphere jhānas. Therefore, showing the method of attention for the formless attainments, he said: “He attends to the higher attainment as peaceful,” etc. Therein, “higher attainment” refers to the attainment of the base of the infinity of space. “Attends to it as peaceful” means he attends to it as “peaceful” both in terms of the peacefulness of its factors and the peacefulness of its object. For whenever one attends to the formless attainment as peaceful, the form-sphere jhāna, being unpacified, presents itself. Therefore, he said: “For him, the higher... becomes established.” As for “discontent and the perception of resistance,” non-delight in the five sense-perceptions, designated as perceptions of resistance, becomes established. By “Completely,” etc., he indicates the formless attainment in part. As for “The perception of form is the directing of the mind to higher knowledge,” the intended meaning is that these are called perceptions of the form-sphere only to the extent of directing the mind for the purpose of higher knowledge; they are not, however, peaceful like the formless attainments. As for “‘Diversity’ is the perception of multiplicity,” these are called perceptions of multiplicity, which is the mingling in various objects; the meaning is the agitated activity of the mind therein. “He transcends” means, having seen the danger therein, he thus transcends them. “And for him the perception of resistance ceases” means that for that yogi attaining the attainment of the base of the infinity of space, the ten perceptions of resistance vanish. By this, he states the first formless attainment.

Evaṃ samāhitassāti evaṃ iminā vuttanayena rūpāvacarajjhāne cittekaggatāyapi samatikkamena samāhitassa. Samāhitassāti āruppasamādhinā santavuttinā samāhitassa. Obhāsoti yo pure rūpāvacarajjhānobhāso. Antaradhāyatīti so rūpāvacarajjhānobhāso arūpāvacarajjhānasamāpajjanakāle vigacchati. Dassanañcāti rūpāvacarajjhānacakkhunā [M 0.0151] dassanañca antaradhāyati. So samādhīti so yathāvutto rūpārūpasamādhi. Chaḷaṅgasamannāgatoti upakārakaparikkhārasabhāvabhūtehi chahi aṅgehi samannāgato. Paccavekkhitabboti pati avekkhitabbo, punappunaṃ cintetabboti attho. Paccavekkhaṇākāraṃ saha visayena dassetuṃ “anabhijjhāsahagata”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sabbaloketi sabbasmiṃ piyarūpe sātarūpe sattaloke saṅkhāraloke ca. Tena kāmacchandassa pahānamāha. Tathā “abyāpanna”ntiādinā byāpādakosajjasārambhasāṭheyyavikkhepasammosānaṃ pahānaṃ. Puna tāni cha aṅgāni samathavipassanāvasena vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “yañca anabhijjhāsahagata”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ suviññeyyaṃ.

“Thus concentrated” means thus, in the way described, concentrated by transcending even the one-pointedness of mind in the form-sphere jhāna. “Concentrated” means concentrated by the formless concentration, which has a peaceful occurrence. “The light” means the light that was previously the light of the form-sphere jhāna. “Disappears” means that light of the form-sphere jhāna vanishes at the time of entering the formless-sphere jhāna. “And the vision” means the vision with the eye of the form-sphere jhāna also disappears. “That concentration” means that concentration of the form and formless spheres as described. “Endowed with six factors” means endowed with six factors that are by nature supportive and preparatory. “To be reviewed” means to be examined again and again; the meaning is it should be repeatedly reflected upon. To show the mode of reviewing together with its object, it is said, “accompanied by non-covetousness,” etc. Therein, “in the whole world” means in all that is pleasing and delightful, in the world of beings and in the world of formations. By that, he states the abandoning of sensual desire. Similarly, by “free from ill will,” etc., he states the abandoning of ill will, sloth, contention, deceit, distraction, and confusion. Again, to show those six factors by dividing them according to serenity and insight, it is said, “and that which is accompanied by non-covetousness,” etc. All that is easily understood.

54. Ettāvatā “paññāvimuttī”ti vuttassa arahattaphalassa samādhimukhena pubbabhāgapaṭipadaṃ dassetvā idāni arahattaphalasamādhiṃ dassetuṃ “so samādhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha so samādhīti yo so sammāsamādhi. Pubbe vuttassa ariyamaggasamādhissa phalabhūto samādhi pañcavidhena veditabbo idāni vuccamānehi pañcahi paccavekkhaṇañāṇehi attano paccavekkhitabbākārasaṅkhātena pañcavidhena veditabbo. “Ayaṃ samādhi paccuppannasukho”tiādīsu arahattaphalasamādhi appitappitakkhaṇe sukhattā paccuppannasukho. Purimo purimo pacchimassa pacchimassa samādhisukhassa paccayattā āyatiṃ sukhavipāko. Kilesehi ārakattā ariyo. Kāmāmisavaṭṭāmisalokāmisānaṃ abhāvā nirāmiso. Buddhādīhi mahāpurisehi sevitattā akāpurisasevito. Aṅgasantatāya sabbakilesadarathasantatāya ca santo. Atittikaraṭṭhena paṇīto. Kilesapaṭippassaddhiyā laddhattā, kilesapaṭippassaddhibhāvena vā laddhattā paṭippassaddhiladdho. Passaddhaṃ passaddhīti hi idaṃ atthato ekaṃ. Paṭippassaddhikilesena vā arahatā laddhattāpi paṭippassaddhiladdho[V 0.0275]. Ekodibhāvena adhigatattā, ekodibhāvameva vā adhigatattā ekodibhāvādhigato. Appaguṇasāsavasamādhi viya sasaṅkhārena sappayogena paccanīkadhamme niggayha kilese vāretvā anadhigatattā nasasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagatoti.

54. Thus far, having shown the preliminary practice for the “liberation by wisdom” called the fruit of arahantship by way of concentration, now, to show the concentration of the fruit of arahantship, “that concentration,” etc., is said. Herein, “that concentration” refers to that right concentration. The concentration which is the fruit of the noble path concentration previously mentioned should be understood in five ways; it should be understood in five ways, designated as the modes for one's own reviewing, by means of the five reviewing knowledges now being described. In the phrases “this concentration is pleasant in the present,” etc., the concentration of the fruit of arahantship is “pleasant in the present” because it is pleasant in each and every moment of absorption. Because each preceding moment is a condition for the happiness of each succeeding moment of concentration, it has a “pleasant result in the future.” Because it is far from the defilements, it is “noble.” Because of the absence of the bait of sensual pleasures, the bait of the round of existence, and the bait of the world, it is “without bait.” Because it is resorted to by great beings such as the Buddhas, it is “resorted to by non-ignoble persons.” Because of the peacefulness of its factors and the subsiding of all torment of the defilements, it is “peaceful.” Because of its nature of not causing satiety, it is “sublime.” Because it is obtained through the pacification of defilements, or because it is obtained as the state of having pacified defilements, it is “obtained by pacification.” For the words `passaddhaṃ` (pacified) and `passaddhi` (pacification) are one in meaning. Or, because it is obtained by an Arahant whose defilements are pacified, it is “obtained by pacification.” Because it is attained through one-pointedness, or because one-pointedness itself is attained, it is “attained by one-pointedness.” Because it is not attained, like a worldly concentration of limited quality and subject to the taints, by suppressing opposing states and warding off defilements with exertion and with effort, it is “not attained by exertion, suppression, and warding off.”

Yato yato bhāgato tañca samādhiṃ samāpajjanto, tato vā vuṭṭhahanto sativepullappatto satova samāpajjati satova vuṭṭhahati, yathāparicchinnakālavasena vā sato samāpajjati sato vuṭṭhahati. Tasmā [M 0.0152] yadettha “ayaṃ samādhi paccuppannasukho ceva āyatiñca sukhavipāko”ti evaṃ paccavekkhantassa paccattameva aparappaccayañāṇaṃ uppajjati, ayameko ākāro. Esa nayo sesesupi. Evametesaṃ pañcannaṃ paccavekkhitabbākārānaṃ vasena samādhi pañcavidhena veditabbo.

Whenever and from whatever part he enters that concentration or emerges from it, having attained an abundance of mindfulness, he enters mindfully and emerges mindfully. Or, according to the determined period of time, he enters mindfully and emerges mindfully. Therefore, herein, for one who reviews thus: “This concentration is both pleasant in the present and has a pleasant result in the future,” the knowledge that is personal and not dependent on another arises. This is one mode. This is the method in the remaining modes as well. Thus, the concentration is to be understood in five ways by means of these five modes that are to be reviewed.

Puna “yo ca samādhī”tiādinā arahattaphale samathavipassanāvibhāgaṃ dasseti. Tattha samādhisukhassa “sukha”nti adhippetattā “yo ca samādhi paccuppannasukho, yo ca samādhi āyatiṃ sukhavipāko, ayaṃ samatho”ti vuttaṃ. Ariyanirāmisādibhāvo pana paññānubhāvena nipphajjatīti āha – “yo ca samādhi ariyo…pe… ayaṃ vipassanā”ti.

Again, by the passage beginning, “And what concentration…,” the distinction between serenity and insight in the fruit of Arahantship is shown. There, because the happiness of concentration is intended by the word “happiness,” it is said: “And that concentration which is pleasant in the present, and that concentration which has a pleasant result in the future—this is serenity.” But the state of being noble, untainted, and so on, is accomplished through the power of wisdom; thus, it is said: “And that concentration which is noble… this is insight.”

Evaṃ arahattaphalasamādhiṃ vibhāgena dassetvā idāni tassa pubbabhāgapaṭipadaṃ samādhivibhāgena dassetuṃ “so samādhī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha so samādhīti yo so arahattaphalasamādhissa pubbabhāgapaṭipadāyaṃ vutto rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānasamādhi, so samādhi. Pañcavidhenāti vakkhamānena pañcappakārena veditabbo. “Pītipharaṇatā”tiādīsu pītiṃ pharamānā uppajjatīti dvīsu jhānesu paññā pītipharaṇatā nāma. Sukhaṃ pharamānā uppajjatīti tīsu jhānesu paññā sukhapharaṇatā nāma. Paresaṃ ceto pharamānā uppajjatīti cetopariyapaññā cetopharaṇatā nāma. Ālokapharaṇe uppajjatīti dibbacakkhupaññā ālokapharaṇatā nāma. Paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ paccavekkhaṇānimittaṃ nāma. Vuttampi cetaṃ “dvīsu jhānesu paññā pītipharaṇatā, tīsu jhānesu paññā sukhapharaṇatā, paracitte ñāṇaṃ cetopharaṇatā, dibbacakkhu ālokapharaṇatā, tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhitassa paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ paccavekkhaṇanimitta”nti (vibha. 804).

Having thus explained the concentration of the fruit of Arahantship by way of division, now, in order to explain its preliminary-stage practice by way of a division of concentration, it is said, “That concentration…” Therein, by “that concentration” is meant that concentration of the fourth jhāna of the fine-material sphere which was spoken of in the preliminary-stage practice for the concentration of the fruit of Arahantship. It should be understood in five ways, as will be stated. In the phrases “pervasion of rapture,” etc., because wisdom arises pervading with rapture, the wisdom in the two jhānas is called “pervasion of rapture.” Because it arises pervading with happiness, the wisdom in the three jhānas is called “pervasion of happiness.” Because it arises pervading the minds of others, the wisdom of penetrating minds is called “pervasion of mind.” Because it arises in the pervasion of light, the wisdom of the divine eye is called “pervasion of light.” The knowledge of reviewing is called “the sign of reviewing.” And this has been said: “Wisdom in two jhānas is pervasion of rapture; wisdom in three jhānas is pervasion of happiness; knowledge of others’ minds is pervasion of mind; the divine eye is pervasion of light; for one who has emerged from that particular concentration, the knowledge of reviewing is the sign of reviewing.”

Idha samathavipassanāvibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “yo ca pītipharaṇo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ettha ca paññāsīsena [V 0.0276] desanā katāti paññāvasena saṃvaṇṇanā katā. Paññā pītipharaṇatātiādīsu samādhisahagatā evāti tattha samādhivasena samatho uddhaṭo. Tasmā pītisukhacetopharaṇatā visesato samādhivipphāravasena ijjhantīti tā “samatho”ti vuttā. Itarāni ñāṇavipphāravasenāti tāni “vipassanā”ti vuttāni.

Here, to show the distinction between serenity and insight, the passage beginning, “And that which is pervaded by rapture…” is stated. And here, the teaching is given with wisdom as its head, thus the explanation is made by way of wisdom. In phrases such as “the pervasion of rapture by wisdom,” wisdom is always accompanied by concentration; therefore, serenity is extracted there by way of concentration. Therefore, because the pervasion of rapture, happiness, and mind are accomplished specifically by way of the diffusion of concentration, they are called “serenity.” The others are accomplished by way of the diffusion of knowledge, thus they are called “insight.”

55. Idāni [M 0.0153] taṃ samādhiṃ ārammaṇavasena vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “dasa kasiṇāyatanānī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha kasiṇajjhānasaṅkhātāni kasiṇāni ca tāni yogino sukhavisesānaṃ adhiṭṭhānabhāvato, manāyatanadhammāyatanabhāvato ca āyatanāni cāti kasiṇāyatanāni. Pathavīkasiṇanti kataparikammaṃ pathavīmaṇḍalampi, tattha pavattaṃ uggahapaṭibhāganimittampi, tasmiṃ nimitte uppannajjhānampi vuccati. Tesu jhānaṃ idhādhippetaṃ. Ākāsakasiṇanti kasiṇugghāṭimākāse pavattapaṭhamāruppajjhānaṃ. Viññāṇakasiṇanti paṭhamāruppaviññāṇārammaṇaṃ dutiyāruppajjhānaṃ. Pathavīkasiṇādike suddhasamathabhāvanāvasena pavattite sandhāya “imāni aṭṭha kasiṇāni samatho”ti vuttaṃ. Sesakasiṇadvayaṃ vipassanādhiṭṭhānabhāvena pavattaṃ “vipassanā”ti vuttaṃ.

55. Now, to explain that concentration by dividing it according to its objects, the passage beginning, “The ten kasiṇa bases…” is stated. Therein, they are kasiṇas, known as kasiṇa-jhānas, and they are also bases because they are a foundation for the yogī’s special happiness, and because of being the mind-base and the mental-object-base; thus, they are called kasiṇa-bases. “Earth kasiṇa” refers to the prepared earth-disc, the learning-sign and counterpart-sign that occur in relation to it, and the jhāna that has arisen in that sign. Among these, jhāna is intended here. “Space kasiṇa” is the first immaterial jhāna that occurs in the space obtained by removing the kasiṇa. “Consciousness kasiṇa” is the second immaterial jhāna which has the consciousness of the first immaterial jhāna as its object. With reference to the earth kasiṇa and so on, when they are developed by way of the development of pure serenity, it is said: “These eight kasiṇas are serenity.” The remaining two kasiṇas, occurring as a foundation for insight, are called “insight.”

Evanti iminā nayena. Sabbo ariyamaggoti sammādiṭṭhiādibhāvena abhinnopi ariyamaggo satipaṭṭhānādipubbabhāgapaṭipadābhedena anekabhedabhinno niravaseso ariyamaggo. Yena yena ākārenāti anabhijjhādīsu, paccuppannasukhatādīsu ca ākāresu yena yena ākārena vutto. Tena tenāti tesu tesu ākāresu ye ye samathavasena, ye ca ye ca vipassanāvasena yojetuṃ sambhavanti, tena tena ākārena samathavipassanāhi ariyamaggo vicinitvā yojetabbo. Teti samathādhiṭṭhānavipassanādhammā. Tīhi dhammehi saṅgahitāti tīhi anupassanādhammehi saṅgahitā, gaṇanaṃ gatāti attho. Katamehi tīhīti? Āha “aniccatāya dukkhatāya anattatāyā”ti. Aniccatāya sahacaraṇato vipassanā “aniccatā”ti vuttā. Esa nayo sesesupi.

“Thus” means by this method. “The entire Noble Path” means the Noble Path, though undivided in terms of right view and so on, is divided into many kinds by the different preliminary-stage practices such as the foundations of mindfulness; it is the entire Noble Path without remainder. “In whatever way” means in whatever way it is spoken of in aspects such as non-covetousness, and in aspects such as present happiness. “By that way” means that in those various aspects, in whatever way it is possible to apply them by way of serenity, and in whatever way by insight, the Noble Path should be investigated and applied by that way with serenity and insight. “Those” refers to the insight phenomena which have serenity as their foundation. “Are included in three things” means they are included in the three contemplation-phenomena; this is the meaning. By what three? It is said: “By impermanence, by suffering, by non-self.” Because it occurs together with impermanence, insight is called “impermanence.” This is the method in the remaining cases as well.

So samathavipassanaṃ bhāvayamāno tīṇi vimokkhamukhāni bhāvayatīti so ariyamaggādhigamāya yuttappayutto yogī kālena samathaṃ samāpajjanavasena kālena vipassanaṃ sammasanavasena vaḍḍhayamāno animittavimokkhamukhādisaṅkhātā tisso anupassanā brūheti. Tayo khandhe bhāvayatīti tisso anupassanā uparūparivisesaṃ pāpento sīlakkhandho samādhikkhandho paññākkhandhoti [V 0.0277] ete tayo khandhe vaḍḍheti. Yasmā pana tīhi khandhehi ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅgahito, tasmā “tayo khandhe bhāvayanto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayatī”ti vuttaṃ.

“He, developing serenity and insight, develops the three gateways to liberation” means: that yogī, diligently striving for the attainment of the Noble Path, while developing serenity at times by way of attainment and insight at other times by way of comprehension, cultivates the three contemplations known as the signless gateway to liberation, etc. “He develops the three aggregates” means: while bringing the three contemplations to progressively higher distinction, he develops these three aggregates: the aggregate of virtue, the aggregate of concentration, and the aggregate of wisdom. And because the Noble Eightfold Path is included in the three aggregates, it is therefore said: “Developing the three aggregates, he develops the Noble Eightfold Path.”

Idāni [M 0.0154] yesaṃ puggalānaṃ yattha sikkhantānaṃ visesato niyyānamukhāni yesañca kilesānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtāni tīṇi vimokkhamukhāni, tehi saddhiṃ tāni dassetuṃ “rāgacarito”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha animittena vimokkhamukhenāti aniccānupassanāya. Sā hi niccanimittādisamugghāṭanena animitto, rāgādīnaṃ samucchedavimuttiyā vimokkhoti laddhanāmassa ariyamaggassa mukhabhāvato dvārabhāvato “animittavimokkhamukha”nti vuccati. Adhicittasikkhāyāti samādhismiṃ. Sukhavedanīyaṃ phassaṃ anupagacchantoti sukhavedanāya hitaṃ sukhavedanākāraṇato phassaṃ taṇhāya anupagacchanto. Sukhaṃ vedanaṃ parijānantoti “ayaṃ sukhā vedanā vipariṇāmādinā dukkhā”ti parijānanto, savisayaṃ rāgaṃ samatikkanto. “Rāgamalaṃ pavāhento”tiādinā tehi pariyāyehi rāgasseva pahānamāha. “Dosacarito puggalo”tiādīsupi vuttanayānusārena attho veditabbo.

Now, to show those three gateways to liberation along with the persons for whom, while they are training, they are especially a means of escape, and the defilements for which they are the antidote, it is said, 'one of greedy temperament,' and so forth. Therein, 'by the signless gateway to liberation' means by the contemplation of impermanence. For that contemplation is called 'signless' through its eradication of the sign of permanence, etc., and it is called the 'signless gateway to liberation' because it is the 'mouth' or 'door' to the Noble Path, which has gained the name 'liberation' through the liberation that is the complete cutting off of greed and so on. 'In the training in higher mind' means in concentration. 'Not approaching contact that is to be felt as pleasant' means not approaching through craving the contact that is conducive to pleasant feeling because it is a cause of pleasant feeling. 'Fully understanding pleasant feeling' means fully understanding, 'This pleasant feeling is suffering on account of change, etc.,' and having transcended greed together with its object. By such expressions as 'washing away the stain of greed,' he speaks only of the abandonment of greed. In the cases of 'a person of hating temperament,' and so forth, the meaning should be understood in accordance with the method explained.

Paññādhikassa santatisamūhakiccārammaṇādighanavinibbhogena saṅkhāresu attasuññatā pākaṭā hotīti visesato anattānupassanā paññāpadhānāti āha – “suññatavimokkhamukhaṃ paññākkhandho”ti. Tathā saṅkhārānaṃ sarasapabhaṅgutāya ittarakhaṇattā uppannānaṃ tattha tattheva bhijjanaṃ sammā samāhitasseva pākaṭaṃ hotīti visesato aniccānupassanā samādhippadhānāti āha – “animittavimokkhamukhaṃ samādhikkhandho”ti. Tathā sīlesu paripūrakārino khantibahulassa uppannaṃ dukkhaṃ aratiñca abhibhuyya viharato saṅkhārānaṃ dukkhatā vibhūtā hotīti dukkhānupassanā sīlappadhānāti āha – “appaṇihitavimokkhamukhaṃ sīlakkhandho”ti. Iti tīhi vimokkhamukhehi tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ saṅgahitattā vuttaṃ – “so tīṇi vimokkhamukhāni bhāvayanto tayo khandhe bhāvayatī”ti. Yasmā ca tīhi ca khandhehi ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa saṅgahitattā tayo khandhe bhāvayanto “ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā tehi tassa saṅgahaṃ dassento “yā ca sammāvācā”tiādimāha.

For one with predominant wisdom, the emptiness of self in formations becomes evident through the dismantling of the compactness of continuity, collection, function, object, and so on. Therefore, because the contemplation of not-self is especially predominant in wisdom, he said, 'The gateway to liberation through emptiness is the aggregate of wisdom.' Similarly, because the breaking up of arisen formations right then and there, due to their nature of perishing by themselves and their momentary existence, becomes evident only to one who is rightly concentrated, the contemplation of impermanence is especially predominant in concentration. Therefore, he said, 'The signless gateway to liberation is the aggregate of concentration.' Likewise, for one who fulfills the virtues and is full of patience, who dwells having overcome arisen suffering and discontent, the state of suffering of formations becomes manifest. Therefore, because the contemplation of suffering is predominant in virtue, he said, 'The desireless gateway to liberation is the aggregate of virtue.' Thus, because the three aggregates are included by the three gateways to liberation, it is said, 'He, developing the three gateways to liberation, develops the three aggregates.' And since the Noble Eightfold Path is included by the three aggregates, it is said that one who develops the three aggregates 'develops the Noble Eightfold Path.' Therefore, showing its inclusion by them, he said, 'And what is right speech,' and so on.

Puna tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ samathavipassanābhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “sīlakkhandho”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sīlakkhandhassa khantipadhānattā, samādhissa bahūpakārattā ca samathapakkhabhajanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Bhavaṅgānīti upapattibhavassa aṅgāni. Dve padānīti dve pādā. Yebhuyyena hi pañcadasa caraṇadhammā [V 0.0278] sīlasamādhisaṅgahitāti. Bhāvitakāyoti [M 0.0155] ābhisamācārikasīlassa pāripūriyā bhāvitakāyo. Ādibrahmacariyakasīlassa pāripūriyā bhāvitasīlo. Atha vā bhāvitakāyoti indriyasaṃvarena bhāvitapañcadvārakāyo. Bhāvitasīloti avasiṭṭhasīlavasena bhāvitasīlo. Sammā kāyabhāvanāya sati accantaṃ kāyaduccaritappahānaṃ anavajjañca uṭṭhānaṃ sampajjati. Tathā anuttare sīle sijjhamāne anavasesato micchāvācāya micchājīvassa ca pahānaṃ sampajjati. Cittapaññāsu ca bhāvitāsu sammāsatisammāsamādhisammādiṭṭhisammāsaṅkappā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gatā eva honti taṃsabhāvattā tadubhayakāraṇattā cāti imamatthaṃ dasseti “kāye bhāviyamāne”tiādinā.

Again, to show the state of the three aggregates as calm and insight, it is said, 'the aggregate of virtue,' and so on. Therein, the inclusion of the aggregate of virtue in the side of calm should be understood, because patience is its chief aspect and because it is of great help to concentration. 'Factors of existence' means the components of rebirth existence. 'Two feet' means two bases. For, for the most part, the fifteen factors of conduct are included in virtue and concentration. 'Developed in body' means the body is developed through the fulfillment of the virtue of proper conduct. 'Developed in virtue' means virtue is developed through the fulfillment of the virtue fundamental to the holy life. Alternatively, 'developed in body' means the five-door body is developed through restraint of the senses. 'Developed in virtue' means virtue is developed by way of the remaining virtues. When the body is rightly developed, the complete abandonment of bodily misconduct and blameless exertion are accomplished. Similarly, when supreme virtue is being perfected, the abandonment of wrong speech and wrong livelihood is accomplished without remainder. And when mind and wisdom are developed, right mindfulness, right concentration, right view, and right intention indeed reach the fulfillment of development, because of being of that very nature and being the cause of both. He shows this meaning by the passage beginning, 'When the body is being developed...'

Pañcavidhaṃ adhigamaṃ gacchatīti ariyamaggādhigamameva avatthāvisesavasena pañcadhā vibhajitvā dasseti. Ariyamaggo hi khippaṃ sakiṃ ekacittakkhaṇeneva catūsu saccesu attanā adhigantabbaṃ adhigacchatīti na tassa lokiyasamāpattiyā viya vasibhāvanākiccaṃ atthīti khippādhigamo ca hoti. Pajahitabbānaṃ accantavimuttivasena pajahanato vimuttādhigamo ca. Lokiyehi mahantānaṃ sīlakkhandhādīnaṃ adhigamanabhāvato mahādhigamo ca. Tesaṃyeva vipulaphalānaṃ adhigamanato vipulādhigamo ca. Attanā kattabbassa kassaci anavasesato anavasesādhigamo ca hotīti. Ke panete adhigamā? Keci samathānubhāvena, keci vipassanānubhāvenāti imaṃ vibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “tattha samathenā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

By the passage 'one attains five kinds of attainment,' he shows the attainment of the Noble Path itself, having divided it into five by way of distinctions in stages. For the Noble Path quickly, at once, in a single mind-moment, attains in the four truths what is to be attained by oneself. Therefore, it does not have the task of developing mastery like a mundane attainment, and thus it is a swift attainment. It is also a liberating attainment because it abandons what is to be abandoned by way of complete liberation. It is a great attainment because of attaining the aggregates of virtue and so on, which are greater than mundane things. It is a vast attainment because of attaining those very things which have abundant fruit. And it is an attainment without remainder because there is no remainder of anything to be done by oneself. But what are these attainments? To show this distinction—that some are by the power of calm, and some by the power of insight—it is said, 'Therein, by calm,' and so on.

56. Iti mahāthero “tasmā rakkhitacittassā”ti gāthāya vasena arahattaphalavimuttimukhena vicayahārasampātaṃ niddisanto desanākusalatāya anekehi suttappadesehi tassā pubbabhāgapaṭipadāya bhāvanāvisesānaṃ bhāvanānisaṃsānañca vibhajanavasena nānappakārato vicayahāraṃ dassetvā idāni dasannaṃ tathāgatabalānampi vasena taṃ dassetuṃ “tattha yo desayatī”tiādimāha. Ovādena sāvake na visaṃvādayatīti attano anusiṭṭhiyā dhammassa savanato “sāvakā”ti laddhanāme veneyye na vippalambheti na vañceti, visaṃvādanahetūnaṃ pāpadhammānaṃ ariyamaggena bodhimūle eva suppahīnattā. Tividhanti tippakāraṃ, tīhi ākārehīti attho. Idaṃ karothāti imaṃ saraṇagamanaṃ sīlādiñca upasampajja [M 0.0156] viharatha. Iminā upāyena karothāti anenapi vidhinā saraṇāni sodhentā sīlādīni paripūrentā sampādetha. Idaṃ vo kurumānānanti idaṃ saraṇagamanaṃ sīlādiñca tumhākaṃ anutiṭṭhantānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasamparāyanibbānānaṃ vasena hitāya sukhāya ca bhavissati, tāni sampādethāti attho.

56. Thus, the great elder, by means of the verse "Therefore, for one with a guarded mind," while pointing out the connection of the Vicaya method by way of the liberation which is the fruit of Arahantship, and due to his skill in teaching, having shown the Vicaya method in various ways by means of many passages from the suttas, by way of distinguishing its preliminary practice, the special qualities of the development, and the benefits of the development, now, to show it by means of the ten powers of the Tathāgata, said the passage beginning with "Therein, one who teaches...". "He does not mislead the disciples with his instruction" means: he does not deceive or cheat the trainable ones who have obtained the name "disciples" from hearing the Dhamma through his instruction, because the evil states that are the causes for misleading have been completely abandoned by the noble path right at the foot of the Bodhi tree. "Threefold" means of three kinds; by three modes, this is the meaning. "Do this" means: having undertaken this going for refuge and virtue, etc., you should dwell. "Do it by this means" means: by this method, purifying the refuges and fulfilling virtue, etc., you should accomplish them. The phrase "This, for you who are practicing" means: this going for refuge, virtue, and so forth, for you who are practicing accordingly, will be for your welfare and happiness by way of the present life, the future life, and Nibbāna; therefore, accomplish those things. This is the meaning.

Evaṃ [V 0.0279] ovadanākāraṃ dassetvā yaṃ vuttaṃ – “ovādena sāvake na visaṃvādayatī”ti, taṃ tathāgatabalehi vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “so tathā ovadito”tiādimāha. Tattha tathāti tena pakārena “idaṃ karotha, iminā upāyena karothā”tiādinā vuttappakārena. Ovaditoti dhammadesanāya sāsito. Anusiṭṭhoti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Tathā karontoti yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā karonto. Taṃ bhūminti yassā bhūmiyā adhigamatthāya ovadito, taṃ dassanabhūmiñca bhāvanābhūmiñca. Netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti etaṃ kāraṇaṃ na vijjati. Kāraṇañhi tiṭṭhati ettha phalaṃ tadāyattavuttitāyāti “ṭhāna”nti vuccati. Dutiyavāre bhūminti sīlakkhandhena pattabbaṃ sampattibhavasaṅkhātaṃ bhūmiṃ.

Having thus shown the manner of instruction, to show what was said—"He does not mislead the disciples with his instruction"—by analyzing it with the powers of the Tathāgata, he said the passage beginning with "He, being thus instructed...". Therein, "thus" means in that manner, in the manner spoken of, beginning with "Do this, do it by this means". "Instructed" means taught by the teaching of the Dhamma. "Anusiṭṭho" is a synonym for that very word. "Acting thus" means acting as instructed. "That plane" means the plane of vision and the plane of development, for the attainment of which plane he was instructed. "This is not a possible condition" means this cause does not exist. Indeed, a cause stands, and on it the fruit rests, being dependent on it; therefore it is called a "condition" (ṭhāna). In the second instance, "plane" means the plane called a prosperous existence, which is to be attained through the aggregate of virtue.

Idāni yasmā bhagavato catuvesārajjānipi aviparītasabhāvatāya paṭhamaphalañāṇassa visayaviseso hoti, tasmā tānipi tassa visayabhāvena dassetuṃ “sammāsambuddhassa te sato”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sammāsambuddhassa te satoti ahaṃ sammāsambuddho, mayā sabbe dhammā abhisambuddhāti paṭijānanena sammāsambuddhassa te sato. Ime dhammā anabhisambuddhāti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti “ime nāma tayā dhammā anabhisambuddhā”ti koci sahadhammena sahetunā sakāraṇena vacanena, sunakkhatto (dī. ni. 3.1 ādayo; ma. ni. 1.146 ādayo) viya vippalapantā pana appamāṇaṃ. Tasmā sahadhammena paṭicodessatīti etaṃ kāraṇaṃ na vijjati. Esa nayo sesapadesupi. Yassa te atthāya dhammo desitoti rāgādīsu yassa yassa pahānatthāya asubhabhāvanādidhammo kathito. Takkarassāti tathā paṭipannassa. Visesādhigamanti abhiññāpaṭisambhidādivisesādhigamaṃ.

Now, because the four confidences of the Blessed One, due to their unerring nature, are also a special domain of the knowledge which is the first power, therefore, to show them also as its domain, the passage beginning with "You being a Perfectly Enlightened One..." was said. Therein, "You being a Perfectly Enlightened One" means: by the declaration "I am a Perfectly Enlightened One, all dhammas have been fully awakened to by me," you are a Perfectly Enlightened One. The phrase "There is no possible condition that 'these dhammas have not been fully awakened to'" means: that someone, with a statement that is in accordance with the Dhamma, with reason, and with cause, will challenge, saying, "These dhammas have not been fully awakened to by you"—but those who babble like Sunakkhatta are not a valid measure. Therefore, that someone will challenge in accordance with the Dhamma—this cause does not exist. This is the method in the remaining passages as well. "For whose sake the Dhamma was taught by you" means: for the sake of abandoning whichever of lust, etc., the Dhamma of the meditation on foulness, etc., was taught. "For one who does so" means for one who has practiced in such a way. "Attainment of distinction" means the attainment of the distinction of the higher knowledges, the analytical knowledges, etc.

Antarāyikāti antarāyakaraṇaṃ antarāyo, so sīlaṃ etesanti antarāyikā. Antarāye niyuttā, antarāyaṃ vā phalaṃ arahanti, antarāyappayojanāti [M 0.0157] vā antarāyikā. Te pana kammakilesādibhedena pañcavidhā. Aniyyānikāti ariyamaggavajjā sabbe dhammā.

"Obstructive" (antarāyikā) means: the making of an obstacle is an obstacle (antarāyo); that is their nature (sīla), therefore they are "obstructive". Or, they are engaged in causing an obstacle; or, they deserve the result which is an obstacle; or, they have an obstacle as their purpose, therefore they are "obstructive". They, however, are of five kinds by the division of kamma, defilement, etc. "Not leading out" (aniyyānika) means all states except for the noble path.

Diṭṭhisampannoti maggadiṭṭhiyā sampanno sotāpanno ariyasāvako. Suhatanti ativadhitaṃ. Idampi ekadesakathanameva. Matakapetādidānampi so na karoti eva. Puthujjanoti puthūnaṃ kilesābhisaṅkhārādīnaṃ jananādīhi kāraṇehi puthujjano. Vuttañhetaṃ –

"Endowed with view" means a noble disciple, a stream-enterer, who is endowed with the view of the path. "Well-struck" means utterly killed. This too is just a partial statement. He does not even perform offerings for the dead, pretas, etc. A "worldling" (puthujjana) is so called due to causes such as the generating of numerous defilements, formations, etc. For this has been said:

“Puthūnaṃ [V 0.0280] jananādīhi, kāraṇehi puthujjano;

Puthujjanantogadhattā, puthuvāyaṃ jano itī”ti. (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.7; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.2; a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.51; dha. sa. aṭṭha. 1007; paṭi. ma. aṭṭha. 2.1.130);

"A worldling (puthujjana) is so called due to causes such as generating numerous things; because of being included among worldlings; and because this person is separate."

“Mātara”ntiādīsu janikā mātā. Janako ca pitā. Manussabhūto khīṇāsavo arahāti adhippeto. Kiṃ pana ariyasāvako aññe jīvitā voropeyyāti? Etampi aṭṭhānaṃ. Sacepi bhavantaragataṃ ariyasāvakaṃ attano ariyasāvakabhāvaṃ ajānantampi koci evaṃ vadeyya “idaṃ kunthakipillikaṃ jīvitā voropetvā sakalacakkavāḷagabbhe cakkavattirajjaṃ paṭipajjāhī”ti, neva so naṃ jīvitā voropeyya. Athāpi evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – “sace imaṃ na ghātessasi, sīsaṃ te chindissāmā”ti, sīsamevassa chindeyyuṃ, neva so taṃ ghāteyya. Puthujjanabhāvassa pana mahāsāvajjabhāvadassanatthaṃ ariyabhāvassa ca baladīpanatthaṃ evaṃ vuttaṃ. Ayañhettha adhippāyo – sāvajjo vata puthujjanabhāvo. Yatra hi nāma mātughākādīnipi ānantariyāni karissati, mahābalova ca ariyabhāvo, yo etāni kammāni na karotīti.

In "mother", etc., the birth-mother is intended, and the birth-father. An Arahant is intended to be a human being who is a destroyer of the taints. But would a noble disciple deprive others of life? This too is an impossible condition. Even if someone were to say to a noble disciple who had gone to another existence, even without knowing his own state as a noble disciple, "Having deprived this insect or ant of life, attain universal sovereignty within the entire cosmos," he would never deprive it of life. And even if they were to say, "If you do not kill this, we will cut off your head," they might cut off his head, but he would never kill it. However, this was said to show the great faultiness of the state of a worldling and to reveal the power of the noble state. This is the intention here: How faulty indeed is the state of a worldling, wherein one might indeed commit the deeds with immediate result, such as matricide! And how powerful is the noble state, which does not commit these deeds.

Saṅghaṃ bhindeyyāti samānasaṃvāsakaṃ samānasīmāyaṃ ṭhitaṃ pañcahi kāraṇehi saṅghaṃ bhindeyya. Vuttañhetaṃ – “pañcahupāli, ākārehi saṅgho bhijjati kammena uddesena voharanto anussāvanena salākaggāhenā”ti (pari. 458).

“To split the Saṅgha” means to split a Saṅgha that is established within the same boundary and living in concord, by five causes. For it was said: ‘By five ways, Upāli, the Saṅgha is split: by a formal act, by recitation, by speaking, by proclamation, and by the taking of a ballot.’

Tattha kammenāti apalokanādīsu catūsu kammesu aññatarakammena. Uddesenāti pañcasu pātimokkhuddesesu aññatarena uddesena. Voharantoti [M 0.0158] kathayanto, tāhi tāhi upapattīhi “adhammaṃ dhammo”tiādīni aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthūni dīpayanto. Anussāvanenāti “nanu tumhe jānātha mayhaṃ uccakulā pabbajitabhāvaṃ bahussutabhāvañca, mādiso nāma uddhammaṃ ubbinayaṃ satthusāsanaṃ gāheyyāti kiṃ tumhākaṃ cittampi uppādetuṃ yuttaṃ, kimahaṃ apāyato na bhāyāmī”tiādinā nayena kaṇṇamūle vacībhedaṃ katvā anussāvanena. Salākaggāhenāti evaṃ anussāvetvā tesaṃ cittaṃ upatthambhetvā anivattidhammaṃ katvā “gaṇhatha imaṃ salāka”nti salākaggāhena.

Therein, ‘by a formal act’ means by any one of the four formal acts, such as apalokana. ‘By recitation’ means by any one of the five Pātimokkha recitations. ‘By speaking’ means speaking, expounding the eighteen grounds for schism, such as ‘what is not Dhamma is Dhamma,’ with various arguments. ‘By proclamation’ means by proclamation, having spoken divisive words in their ear, saying: ‘Do you not know of my going forth from a high family and my great learning? Is it fitting for you even to think that someone like me would accept what is not-Dhamma, what is not-Vinaya, the Teacher’s Dispensation? Am I not afraid of the plane of misery?’ and so on. ‘By the taking of a ballot’ means, having thus proclaimed, having supported their minds and made them irreversible, by the taking of a ballot, saying, ‘Take this ballot-stick.’

Ettha ca kammameva uddeso vā pamāṇaṃ, vohārānussāvanasalākaggāhāpanaṃ pana pubbabhāgo[V 0.0281]. Aṭṭhārasavatthudīpanavasena hi voharantena tattha rucijananatthaṃ anussāvetvā salākāya gāhitāyapi abhinno eva hoti saṅgho. Yadā pana evaṃ cattāro vā atirekā vā salākaṃ gāhetvā āveṇikaṃ kammaṃ vā uddesaṃ vā karonti, tadā saṅgho bhinno nāma hoti. Evaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo saṅghaṃ bhindeyya saṅgharājiṃ vā janeyyāti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti.

Herein, the formal act itself or the recitation is the standard; but the speaking, proclamation, and causing the ballot to be taken are the preliminary part. For when one speaks by way of expounding the eighteen grounds, even after proclaiming to generate inclination therein and the ballot is taken, the Saṅgha is still undivided. But when four or more, having caused the ballot to be taken, perform a separate formal act or recitation, then the Saṅgha is called ‘split’. Thus, that a person accomplished in view might split the Saṅgha or create a fissure in the Saṅgha—this is not possible.

Duṭṭhacittoti vadhakacittena paduṭṭhacitto. Lohitaṃ uppādeyyāti jīvamānakasarīre khuddakamakkhikāya pivanamattampi lohitaṃ uppādeyya. Ettāvatā hi mātughātādīni pañcānantariyakammāni dassitāni honti. Yāni puthujjano karoti, na ariyasāvako. Duṭṭhacittoti vināsacittena paduṭṭhacitto. Thūpanti cetiyaṃ. Bhindeyyāti nāseyya.

“With a corrupt mind” means with a mind corrupted by a murderous intent. “Would cause blood to arise” means would cause blood to arise from a living body, even just the amount a small fly could drink. By this much, the five deeds with immediate result, such as matricide, are shown. These are deeds a worldling does, not a noble disciple. “With a corrupt mind” means with a mind corrupted by an intent to destroy. “A thūpa” means a cetiya. “Would break” means would destroy.

Aññaṃ satthāranti “ayaṃ me satthā satthu kiccaṃ kātuṃ samattho”ti bhavantarepi aññaṃ titthakaraṃ. Apadiseyyāti “ayaṃ me satthā”ti evaṃ gaṇheyyāti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Ito bahiddhā aññaṃ dakkhiṇeyyaṃ pariyeseyyāti sāsanato bahiddhā aññaṃ bāhirakaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā “ayaṃ dakkhiṇāraho, imasmiṃ katā kārā mahapphalā bhavissantī”ti adhippāyena tasmiṃ paṭipajjeyyāti attho. Kutūhalamaṅgalena suddhiṃ pacceyyāti “iminā idaṃ bhavissatī”ti evaṃ pavattattā kutūhalasaṅkhātena diṭṭhasutamutamaṅgalena attano suddhiṃ vodānaṃ saddaheyya.

“Another teacher” means, even in another existence, another sectarian teacher, thinking, “This is my teacher, capable of fulfilling a teacher’s duties.” “Would point to” means it is not possible that one would accept them, thinking, “This is my teacher.” “Would search for another worthy of offerings outside of this” means to search for another ascetic or brahmin outside the Dispensation with the intention, “This one is worthy of offerings, and acts of reverence done to this one will be of great fruit,” and to practice accordingly towards them. “Would believe in purity through auspicious signs and ceremonies” means one would have faith in one's own purity and purification through auspicious signs seen, heard, or cognized, which are called ‘commotions’ as they arise from thinking, “By this, that will happen.”

57. Itthī rājā cakkavattī siyāti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti yasmā itthiyā kosohitavatthaguyhādīnaṃ abhāvena lakkhaṇāni na paripūranti, itthiratanābhāvena [M 0.0159] ca sattaratanasamaṅgitā na sampajjati. Sabbamanussānampi ca na adhiko attabhāvo hoti, tasmā “itthī…pe… vijjatī”ti vuttaṃ. Yasmā sakkattādīni tīṇi ṭhānāni uttamāni, itthiliṅgañca hīnaṃ, tasmā tassā sakkattādīnipi paṭisiddhānīti. Nanu ca yathā itthiliṅgaṃ, evaṃ purisaliṅgampi brahmaloke natthi, tasmā puriso mahābrahmā siyāti na vattabbanti? No na vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Idha purisassa tattha nibbattanato. Itthiyo hi idha jhānaṃ bhāvetvā kālaṃ katvā brahmapārisajjānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, na mahābrahmānaṃ. Puriso pana katthaci na uppajjatīti na vattabbo. Samānepi tattha ubhayaliṅgābhāve purisasaṇṭhānāva tattha brahmāno, na itthisaṇṭhānā, tasmā suvuttametaṃ. Itthī tathāgatoti ettha tiṭṭhatu tāva sabbaññuguṇe nibbattetvā lokānaṃ tāraṇasamattho buddhabhāvo, paṇidhānamattampi itthiyā na sampajjati.

57. “A woman could be a wheel-turning monarch”—this is not possible. Because for a woman, due to the absence of the male organ concealed in a sheath and so on, the characteristics are not complete, and due to the absence of the queen-jewel, the endowment with the seven jewels is not accomplished. Moreover, her physical existence is not superior to that of all other human beings. Therefore, it is said, “A woman… is not possible.” Since the three positions—Sakka and the like—are supreme, and the female gender is inferior, those positions too are denied to her. But one might object: Just as the female gender, so too the male gender is not found in the Brahma world; therefore, should it not be said that a man cannot become a Great Brahmā? No, it should not be said. Why? Because a man from here is reborn there. Women here, having developed jhāna and passed away, are reborn into the company of Brahmā's attendants, not of the Great Brahmās. But it cannot be said of a man that he is not reborn somewhere there. Even with the absence of both genders there, the Brahmās there have a male form, not a female form. Therefore, this is well-stated. As for “a woman could be a Tathāgata”—let alone the state of a Buddha, who is capable of saving the worlds after having developed the qualities of an omniscient one, even the mere aspiration is not accomplished for a woman.

“Manussattaṃ [V 0.0282] liṅgasampatti, hetu satthāradassanaṃ;

Pabbajjā guṇasampatti, adhikāro ca chandatā;

Aṭṭhadhammasamodhānā, abhinīhāro samijjhatī”ti. (bu. vaṃ. 2.59) –

“Human existence, perfection of gender, the cause, seeing the Teacher; renunciation, perfection of qualities, qualification, and desire; through the combination of these eight factors, the aspiration succeeds.”

Imāni hi paṇidhānasampattikāraṇāni. Iti paṇidhānamattampi sampādetuṃ asamatthāya itthiyā kuto buddhabhāvoti “itthī tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho siyāti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti vuttaṃ. Sabbākāraparipūro puññussayo sabbākāraparipūrameva attabhāvaṃ nibbattetīti purisova arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho.

These, indeed, are the causes for the fulfillment of the aspiration. Thus, for a woman who is unable to fulfill even the mere aspiration, how could there be Buddhahood? Therefore, it is said, “It is not possible for a woman to be a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.” A store of merit complete in all aspects produces a personal existence complete in all aspects; therefore, only a man becomes an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Ekissā lokadhātuyāti dasasahassilokadhātuyā, yā jātikhettanti vuccati. Sā hi tathāgatassa gabbhokkantikālādīsu kampati. Āṇākhettaṃ pana koṭisatasahassacakkavāḷaṃ. Yā ekato saṃvaṭṭati ca vivaṭṭati ca, yattha ca āṭānāṭiyaparittādīnaṃ (dī. ni. 3.277 ādayo) āṇā pavattati. Visayakhettassa parimāṇaṃ natthi. Buddhānañhi “yāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ tāvatakaṃ neyyaṃ, yāvatakaṃ neyyaṃ tāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ, neyyapariyantikaṃ ñāṇaṃ, ñāṇapariyantikaṃ neyya”nti (mahāni. 69; cūḷani. mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa 85; paṭi. ma. 3.5) vacanato avisayo nāma natthi. Iti imesu tīsu khettesu tisso saṅgītiyo āruḷhe tepiṭake buddhavacane “ṭhapetvā imaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ aññasmiṃ cakkavāḷe buddhā uppajjantī”ti suttaṃ natthi, na uppajjantīti pana atthi.

In one world-system: that is, in the ten-thousandfold world-system, which is called the birth-sphere. For it trembles at the time of the Tathāgata’s conception in the mother's womb and so forth. The sphere of authority, however, is one hundred thousand koṭis of world-systems. It is that which contracts and expands together, and where the authority of the Āṭānāṭiya Protection and so forth operates. The extent of the sphere of range has no limit. For the Buddhas, indeed, there is nothing called 'beyond range,' as it is said: "As far as knowledge extends, so far does the knowable extend; as far as the knowable extends, so far does knowledge. Knowledge has the knowable as its limit, the knowable has knowledge as its limit." Thus, in these three spheres, in the Tipiṭaka, the Buddha’s words established by the three councils, there is no sutta stating, "Setting aside this world-system, Buddhas arise in another world-system," but there is one stating that they do not arise.

Apubbaṃ [M 0.0160] acarimanti apure apacchā ekato na uppajjanti, pure vā pacchā vā uppajjantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha gabbhokkantito pubbe pureti veditabbaṃ. Tato paṭṭhāya hi dasasahassicakkavāḷakampanena khettapariggaho kato nāma hoti, aññassa buddhassa uppatti natthi. Dhātuparinibbānato paraṃ pana pacchā, tato heṭṭhāpi aññassa buddhassa uppatti natthi, uddhaṃ na vāritā.

"Not before, not after" means they do not arise simultaneously, not before and not after; it is said that they arise either before or after. Here, 'before' should be understood as prior to conception in the mother's womb. For from that point onward, the delimitation of the sphere is made by the quaking of the ten-thousandfold world-system, and there is no arising of another Buddha. After the final passing away of the relics, however, is 'after'; even before that, there is no arising of another Buddha, but after that is not prevented.

Kasmā pana apubbaṃ acarimaṃ na uppajjantīti? Anacchariyattā. Acchariyamanussā hi buddhā bhagavanto. Yathāha – “ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati acchariyamanusso”tiādi (a. ni. 1.171). Yadi ca aneke buddhā ekato uppajjeyyuṃ, anacchariyā bhaveyyuṃ. Desanāya ca visesābhāvato. Yañhi satipaṭṭhānādibhedaṃ dhammaṃ eko [V 0.0283] deseti, aññenapi so eva desetabbo siyā, vivādabhāvato ca. Bahūsu hi buddhesu ekato uppannesu bahūnaṃ ācariyānaṃ antevāsikā viya “amhākaṃ buddho pāsādiko”tiādinā tesaṃ sāvakā vivadeyyuṃ. Kiṃ vā etena kāraṇagavesanena, dhammatāvesā yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve tathāgatā ekato na uppajjantīti (mi. pa. 5.1.1).

But why do they not arise 'not before, not after'? Because of their not being extraordinary. For the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are extraordinary human beings. As it is said: "One person, monks, arising in the world, arises as an extraordinary human being," and so forth. If many Buddhas were to arise simultaneously, they would not be extraordinary. And because there would be no distinction in their teaching. For whatever Dhamma one teaches—such as the divisions of the foundations of mindfulness—another would have to teach the very same. And because of the existence of disputes. For if many Buddhas arose simultaneously, their disciples, like the pupils of many teachers, might argue, saying, "Our Buddha is more pleasing," and so forth. Or what is the use of this searching for reasons? It is simply the nature of things that two Tathāgatas do not arise simultaneously in one world-system.

Yathā nimbabījakosātakibījādīni madhuraṃ phalaṃ na nibbattenti, asātaṃ amadhurameva phalaṃ nibbattenti, evaṃ kāyaduccaritādīni madhuravipākaṃ na nibbattenti amadhurameva nibbattenti. Yathā ca ucchubījasālibījādīni madhuraṃ sādurasameva phalaṃ nibbattenti na asātaṃ kaṭukaṃ. Evaṃ kāyasucaritādīni madhurameva vipākaṃ nibbattenti na amadhuraṃ. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

Just as seeds of neem, bitter gourd, and so forth do not produce sweet fruit, but produce only unpleasant and unsweet fruit, so too do bodily misconduct and so forth not yield a sweet result—they yield only what is unsweet. And just as seeds of sugarcane, rice, and so forth produce sweet and savory fruit, not unpleasant or bitter fruit, so too do bodily good conduct and so forth yield only a sweet result, not an unsweet result. This, too, has been said:

“Yādisaṃ vapate bījaṃ, tādisaṃ harate phalaṃ;

Kalyāṇakārī kalyāṇaṃ, pāpakārī ca pāpaka”nti. (saṃ. ni. 1.256; netti. 122);

"As is the seed that one sows, so is the fruit that one reaps; the doer of good reaps good, and the doer of evil, evil."

Tasmā “tiṇṇaṃ duccaritāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

Therefore, it was said: "Of the three kinds of misconduct," and so forth.

Aññataro samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vāti yo koci pabbajjāmattena samaṇo vā jātimattena brāhmaṇo vā. Pāpiccho sambhāvanādhippāyena vimhāpanato kuhako. Paccayasannissitāya payuttavācāya vasena lapako. Paccayanibbattakanimittāvacarato nemittako. Kuhanalapananemittakattaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvāti kuhanādibhāvameva purakkhatvā santindriyo [M 0.0161] santamānaso viya caranto. Pañca nīvaraṇeti kāmacchandādike pañca nīvaraṇe. Appahāya asamucchinditvā, cetaso upakkileseti nīvaraṇe. Nīvaraṇā hi cittaṃ upakkilesenti kiliṭṭhaṃ karonti vibādhenti upatāpenti ca. Tasmā “cetaso upakkilesā”ti vuccanti. Paññāya dubbalīkaraṇeti nīvaraṇe. Nīvaraṇā hi uppajjamānā anuppannāya paññāya uppajjituṃ na denti. Tasmā “paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā”ti vuccanti. Anupaṭṭhitassatīti catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu na upaṭṭhitassati. Abhāvayitvāti avaḍḍhayitvā. Anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhinti arahattapadaṭṭhānaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ.

A certain ascetic or brahmin: that is, whoever is an ascetic merely by virtue of his going forth, or a brahmin merely by virtue of his birth. With evil desires, with the intention of being praised, he is a fraud by causing astonishment. He is a chatterer by means of speech employed with reliance on requisites. He is a diviner by practicing signs that produce requisites. Having made fraud, chatter, and divination his foremost qualities: that is, having given prominence to the state of fraud and so forth, he behaves as if with calm faculties and a calm mind. The five hindrances: the five hindrances such as sensual desire. Not having abandoned, not having cut off: the hindrances, the defilements of the mind. For the hindrances defile the mind, make it corrupt, disturb it, and afflict it. Therefore, they are called 'defilements of the mind.' Weakening wisdom: the hindrances. For when the hindrances arise, they do not allow wisdom that has not yet arisen to arise. Therefore, they are called 'weakeners of wisdom.' Without established mindfulness: that is, with mindfulness not established in the four foundations of mindfulness. Not having developed: that is, not having cultivated. The unsurpassed perfect enlightenment: the omniscience that is the proximate cause for arahantship.

Pacchimavāre aññataro samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vāti sabbaññubodhisattaṃ sandhāya vadati. Tattha sabbadosāpagatoti sabbehi pāramitāpaṭipakkhabhūtehi dosehi apagato. Etena paripūritapāramibhāvaṃ [V 0.0284] dasseti. Satipaṭṭhānāni vipassanā, bojjhaṅgo maggo, anuttarā sammāsambodhi arahattaṃ. Satipaṭṭhānāni vā vipassanā, bojjhaṅgā missakā, sammāsambodhi arahattameva. Sesaṃ anantaravāre vuttapaṭipakkhato veditabbaṃ. Yaṃ ettha ñāṇanti yaṃ etasmiṃ yathāvutte ṭhāne ca ṭhānaṃ, aṭṭhāne ca aṭṭhānanti pavattaṃ ñāṇaṃ. Hetusoti tassa ṭhānassa aṭṭhānassa ca hetuto. Ṭhānasoti taṅkhaṇe eva āvajjanasamanantaraṃ. Anodhisoti odhiabhāvena, kiñci anavasesetvāti attho.

In the last section, 'a certain ascetic or brahmin' is said in reference to the Bodhisatta who will attain omniscience. There, 'free from all faults' means free from all faults that are the opposite of the perfections. By this, it shows the state of having fulfilled the perfections. The foundations of mindfulness are insight, the factors of enlightenment are the path, unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is arahantship. Or, the foundations of mindfulness are insight, the factors of enlightenment are associated, perfect enlightenment is arahantship itself. The rest should be understood from the opposite of what was said in the preceding section. Here, 'knowledge' means the knowledge that proceeds regarding what is a cause as a cause and what is not a cause as not a cause in this stated context. 'By cause' means by the cause of that cause and non-cause. 'Instantly' means in that very moment, immediately after adverting. 'Without limit' means due to the absence of a limit, that is, leaving nothing whatsoever remaining.

Iti ṭhānāṭṭhānagatātiādīsu evaṃ ṭhānāṭṭhānabhāvaṃ gatā. Sabbeti khayavayavirajjananirujjhanasabhāvā saṅkhatadhammā, te eva ca sattapaññattiyā upādānabhūtā keci saggūpagā ye dhammacārino, keci apāyūpagā ye adhammacārino, keci nibbānūpagā ye kammakkhayakaraṃ ariyamaggaṃ paṭipannā.

Thus, in phrases such as 'gone to what is a cause and not a cause,' the meaning should be understood in this way: gone to the state of being a cause and not being a cause. As for 'all,' it refers to conditioned phenomena, which have the nature of destruction, vanishing, fading away, and cessation. And those very conditioned phenomena have become the basis of clinging for the concept of 'being.' Some, those who practice the Dhamma, go to the heavenly realm. Some, those who practice unrighteousness, go to the plane of misery. And some, those who have entered upon the noble path that brings about the destruction of kamma, go to Nibbāna.

58. Idāni yathāvuttamatthaṃ vivaranto “sabbe sattā marissantī”ti gāthādvayamāha. Tassa atthaṃ “sabbe sattāti ariyā ca anariyā cā”tiādinā sayameva niddisati. Tattha jīvitapariyanto maraṇapariyantoti jīvitassa pariyanto nāma maraṇasaṅkhāto anto. Yathākammaṃ gamissantīti ettha yadetaṃ sattānaṃ yathākammaṃ gamanaṃ, ayaṃ kammassakatāti attho[M 0.0162]. Kammānaṃ phaladassāvitā ca avippavāso cāti “puññapāpaphalūpagā”ti iminā vacanena kammānaṃ phalassa paccakkhakāritā, katūpacitānaṃ kammānaṃ attano phalassa appadānābhāvo ca dassitoti attho.

58. Now, explaining the meaning as stated, he uttered the two verses beginning, 'All beings will die.' The venerable teacher Kaccāyana himself points out their meaning with the phrase, 'All beings means noble ones and ignoble ones,' and so on. Therein, as for 'life has death as its end,' the end of life is the end called death. Here, in the phrase 'They will go according to their kamma,' this going of beings according to their kamma means ownership of kamma; this is the meaning. And in the phrase 'the showing of the fruit of kamma and its non-disappearance,' by the words 'experiencing the fruit of merit and demerit,' the state of making the fruit of kamma directly visible and the state of non-failure of kamma that has been done and accumulated to give its own fruit are shown; this is the meaning.

Kammameva kammantaṃ, pāpaṃ kammantaṃ etesanti pāpakammantā, tassa atthaṃ dassetuṃ “apuññasaṅkhārā”ti vuttaṃ. Apuñño saṅkhāro etesanti apuññasaṅkhārā. Pāpakammantāti vā nissakkavacanaṃ, pāpakammantahetūti attho. Tathā puññasaṅkhārātiādīsupi. Puna “nirayaṃ pāpakammantā”tiādinā antadvayena saddhiṃ majjhimapaṭipadaṃ dasseti. Tathā “ayaṃ saṃkileso”tiādinā vaṭṭavivaṭṭavasena ādīnavassādanissaraṇavasena hetuphalavasena ca gāthāyaṃ tayo atthavikappā dassitā. Puna “nirayaṃ pāpakammantāti ayaṃ saṃkileso”tiādinā vodānavasena gāthāya atthaṃ dasseti.

Kamma itself is `kammanta`. 'They have evil action' (`pāpaṃ kammantaṃ etesaṃ`), therefore they are `pāpakammantā` (those of evil action). To show its meaning, the term `apuññasaṅkhārā` (demeritorious formations) is stated. 'They have a demeritorious formation' (`apuñño saṅkhāro etesaṃ`), therefore they are `apuññasaṅkhārā`. Alternatively, `pāpakammantā` is an ablative expression, meaning 'on account of evil action.' It is likewise also for `puññasaṅkhārā` (meritorious formations), and so on. Again, with the phrase 'Those of evil action to hell,' etc., he shows the middle path together with the two extremes. Furthermore, with the phrase 'this is defilement,' etc., three alternative meanings in the verse are shown: by way of the round and the ending of the round, by way of danger, gratification, and escape, and by way of cause and effect. Again, with the phrase 'Those of evil action to hell, this is defilement,' etc., he shows the meaning of the verse by way of purification.

59. Tena [V 0.0285] tenāti tena tena ajjhositavatthunā rūpabhavaarūpabhavādinā. Chattiṃsāti kāmataṇhā tāva rūpādivisayabhedena cha, tathā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā cāti aṭṭhārasa. Tā eva ajjhattikesu rūpādīsu aṭṭhārasa, bāhiresu rūpādīsu aṭṭhārasāti evaṃ chattiṃsa. Yena yenāti “subhaṃ sukha”ntiādinā.

59. As for 'by that, by that,' it means by that very object clung to—which is an object attended to through the power of craving and adherence—such as the form existence, the formless existence, and so on. As for 'thirty-six': craving for sensual pleasures is of six kinds according to the division of objects such as forms; likewise, craving for existence and craving for non-existence are also six each. Thus, there are eighteen. Those very eighteen cravings are eighteen with respect to internal forms, etc., and eighteen with respect to external forms, etc. In this way, there are thirty-six. As for 'by whatever, by whatever,' it means by such as 'beautiful' or 'pleasant.'

Vodānaṃ tividhaṃ khandhattayavasenāti taṃ dassetuṃ “taṇhāsaṃkileso”tiādi vuttaṃ. Puna “sabbe sattā marissantī”tiādi paṭipadāvibhāgena gāthānamatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha tattha gāminīti tattha tattheva nibbāne gāminī, nibbānassa gamanasīlāti attho.

That purification is threefold by way of the three aggregates—to show this, 'defilement of craving,' and so on, is stated. Again, to show the meaning of the verses by way of analyzing the path, 'All beings will die,' and so on, is stated. As for `tattha tattha gāminī` (leading to that very place), it means leading unerringly to that very Nibbāna; the meaning is that it has the nature of going to Nibbāna.

Puna tatthatatthagāminīsabbatthagāminīnaṃ paṭipadānaṃ vibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “tayo rāsī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yanti yaṃ nirayādi. Taṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ yathārahaṃ gametīti sabbatthagāminī. Paṭipadāsaṅkhāte apuññakamme puññakamme ca kammakkhayakaraṇakamme ca vibhāgaso bhagavato pavattanañāṇaṃ. Idaṃ sabbatthagāminī paṭipadāñāṇaṃ nāma tathāgatabalaṃ. Iminā hi ñāṇena bhagavā sabbampi paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti.

Again, to show the distinction of the paths leading to that very place and the paths leading everywhere, 'three heaps,' and so on, is stated. They go to whatever place, such as hell. Because it causes one to go to that respective place according to what is fit, it is called `sabbatthagāminī` (leading everywhere).
