Therefore, having conceived whatever is obtained as ‘mine,’ they grasp what is other than that as ‘self.’ ‘This is called the twenty-grounded view of personality’ means: this view, which is twenty-grounded by way of four kinds of grasping in each of the five aggregates of clinging, is a view in the existing body designated as the five aggregates. Or, it is the view of personality because it is a view existing therein.

Lokuttarā sammādiṭṭhīti paṭhamamaggasammādiṭṭhi. Anvāyikāti sammādiṭṭhiyā anugāmino. Yadā sammādiṭṭhi sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā pajahanavasena pavattā, tadā tassā anuguṇabhāvena pavattamānakāti attho. Ke pana teti? Āha “sammāsaṅkappo”tiādi. “Te tayo khandhā”tiādinā ariyamaggato khandhamukhena samathavipassanā niddhāreti. “Tattha sakkāyo”tiādi catusaccaniddhāraṇaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ suviññeyyameva.

‘Supramundane right view’ means the right view of the first path. ‘Concomitant’ means followers of right view. The meaning is: when right view arises by way of abandoning the view of personality, then they are those that arise in conformity with it. But who are they? He said: ‘right intention,’ and so on. By the phrase beginning with ‘Those three aggregates,’ he determines serenity and insight from the noble path by way of the aggregates. The phrase beginning with ‘Therein, the personality’ is the determination of the four truths. All of that is easily understandable.

Puna “tattha ye rūpaṃ attato upagacchantī”tiādinā sakkāyadassanamukhena ucchedādiantadvayaṃ, majjhimañca paṭipadaṃ niddhāreti. Tattha ime vuccanti ucchedavādinoti ime rūpādike pañcakkhandhe attato upagacchantā rūpādīnaṃ aniccabhāvato ucchijjati attā vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇāti evaṃ abhinivisanato “ucchedavādino”ti vuccanti. Ime vuccanti sassatavādinoti ime “rūpavantaṃ vā attāna”ntiādinā rūpādivinimutto añño koci attāti upagacchantā “so nicco dhuvo sassato”ti abhinivisanato “sassatavādino”ti vuccanti. “Ucchedasassatavādā ubho antā, ayaṃ saṃsārapavattī”tiādi saccaniddhāraṇaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyaṃ.

Again, by the phrase beginning with ‘Therein, those who approach form as self,’ he determines, through the approach of the view of personality, the two extremes beginning with annihilationism, and the middle path. Therein, ‘these are called annihilationists’ means: these persons, who approach the five aggregates beginning with form as self, are called ‘annihilationists’ because, due to the impermanence of form and so on, they adhere to the view that ‘the self is annihilated, it is destroyed, it does not exist after death.’ ‘These are called eternalists’ means: these persons, who approach [the view] by way of the phrase beginning with ‘or a self possessing form’ that there is some other self apart from form and so on, are called ‘eternalists’ because they adhere to the view that ‘it is permanent, stable, eternal.’ The phrase beginning with ‘Annihilationism and eternalism are both extremes...’ is the determination of the truth; that is easily understood.

Ucchedasassataṃ samāsato vīsativatthukā sakkāyadiṭṭhīti attā ucchijjati attā niccoti ca ādippavattanato ucchedasassatadassanaṃ saṅkhepato [M 0.0196] vīsativatthukā sakkāyadiṭṭhi eva hoti. Sabbopi hi attavādo sakkāyadiṭṭhiantogadho evāti. Vitthārato dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatānīti ucchedasassatadassanaṃ vitthārena brahmajāle (dī. ni. 1.28 ādayo) āgatāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni. Tesanti evaṃ saṅkhepavitthāravantānaṃ ucchedasassatadassanānaṃ. Paṭipakkhoti pahāyakapaṭipakkho. Tecattālīsaṃ bodhipakkhiyā dhammāti aniccasaññā dukkhasaññā anattasaññā pahānasaññā virāgasaññā nirodhasaññā cattāro satipaṭṭhānā…pe… ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggoti ete tecattālīsaṃ bodhipakkhiyā dhammā.

‘Annihilationism and eternalism, in brief, are the twenty-grounded view of personality’ means: because it arises beginning with ‘the self is annihilated’ and ‘the self is eternal,’ the view of annihilationism and eternalism is, in brief, just the twenty-grounded view of personality. For indeed, every doctrine of self is included within the view of personality. ‘In detail, they are the sixty-two views’ means: the view of annihilationism and eternalism are the sixty-two views that come in detail in the Brahmajāla Sutta. ‘Of these’ means of these views of annihilationism and eternalism which are thus in brief and in detail. ‘The opposing factor’ means the opposing factor that abandons. ‘The forty-three qualities conducive to enlightenment’ means: the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation, the four foundations of mindfulness… up to… the noble eightfold path. These are the forty-three qualities conducive to enlightenment.

Evaṃ [V 0.0317] vipassanāvasena paṭipakkhaṃ dassetvā puna samathavasena dassetuṃ “aṭṭha vimokkhā dasa ca kasiṇāyatanānī”ti vuttaṃ. Dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni mohajālanti dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni mohajālahetukattā mohajālañca. Anādianidhanappavattanti purimāya koṭiyā abhāvato anādi. Asati paṭipakkhādhigame santānavasena anupacchedena pavattanato anidhanappavattaṃ. Yasmā pana mohajālahetukāni diṭṭhigatāni mohajāle padālite padālitāni honti, tasmā vuttaṃ – “tecattālīsaṃ bodhipakkhiyā dhammā ñāṇavajiraṃ mohajālappadālana”nti.

Thus, having shown the opposing factor by way of insight, in order to show it again by way of serenity, it is said, ‘the eight liberations and the ten kasiṇa bases.’ As for ‘the sixty-two wrong views are a net of delusion’: the sixty-two wrong views, because they have the net of delusion (delusion and craving for existence) as their cause, are also called the net of delusion. As for ‘continuing without beginning or end’: it is without beginning (anādi) due to the absence of a prior limit. When the attainment of the opposing factor is absent, because it occurs uninterruptedly by way of the continuity, it occurs without end (anidhanappavattaṃ). But since the wrong views, which have the net of delusion as their cause, are destroyed when the net of delusion is destroyed, it is therefore said, ‘The forty-three qualities conducive to enlightenment are the diamond of knowledge that shatters the net of delusion.’

Tattha ñāṇavajiranti vajirūpamañāṇaṃ. Aṭṭha samāpattiyo samāpajjitvā tejetvā tikkhasabhāvaṃ āpāditaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ maggañāṇañca ñāṇavajiraṃ. Idameva hi ñāṇaṃ bhagavato pavattaṃ “mahāvajirañāṇa”nti vuccati. Taṃ pana sasambhāraṃ katvā dassento “tecattālīsaṃ bodhipakkhiyā dhammā”ti āha. Mohajālappadālananti pubbabhāge vikkhambhanavasena maggakkhaṇe samucchedavasena avijjābhavataṇhānaṃ padālanaṃ. Atītādibhedabhinnesu rūpādīsu sakaattabhāvādīsu ca saṃsibbanavasena pavattanato jālaṃ bhavataṇhā. Tassā hi taṇhā jālinī sibbinī jālanti ca adhivacananti. Evaṃ attakilamathānuyogakāmasukhallikānuyogadiṭṭhitaṇhābhinivesasassatucchedānaṃ niddhāraṇavasena mohajālapariyāyavisesato avijjātaṇhā vibhajitvā yathānusandhinā saṃkilesapakkhaṃ nigamento “tena vuccati pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjāya ca bhavataṇhāya cā”ti āha.

Therein, ‘the diamond of knowledge’ (ñāṇavajira) means the knowledge resembling a diamond. Having attained the eight attainments, having energized them, and having brought them to a state of sharpness, both the insight knowledge and the path knowledge are the ‘diamond of knowledge.’ Indeed, this very knowledge that occurred for the Blessed One is called the ‘great diamond-like knowledge.’ But showing that diamond-like knowledge together with its components, he said, ‘the forty-three qualities conducive to enlightenment.’ ‘The shattering of the net of delusion’ (mohajālappadālana) is the destruction of ignorance and craving for existence by way of suppression in the preliminary stage, and by way of eradication at the moment of the path. Craving for existence (bhavataṇhā) is a net because it occurs by way of weaving together in forms, etc., which are divided by the distinctions of past, etc., and in one’s own personality, etc. For of that craving for existence, the designations are ‘craving’ (taṇhā), ‘weaver’ (jālinī), ‘sewer’ (sibbinī), and ‘net’ (jāla). Thus, having distinguished ignorance and craving by way of determining self-mortification, indulgence in sensual pleasures, adherence to views, adherence to craving, eternalism, and annihilationism, and specifically through the figurative expression ‘net of delusion,’ and concluding the side of defilements in accordance with the sequence, he said: ‘Therefore it is said: the prior limit of ignorance and craving for existence is not discerned.’

81. “Tattha [M 0.0197] diṭṭhicarito”tiādinā vodānapakkhaṃ dasseti. Tattha sallekhānusantatavuttīti anupaddutasallekhavutti. Kasmā? Yasmā sallekhe tibbagāravo. Diṭṭhicarito hi tapojigucchādinā anupāyenapi yebhuyyena kilesānaṃ sallekhanādhippāyena carati, tasmā so sāsane pabbajito dhutadhammavasena sallekhapaṭipadaṃ pūreti. Sikkhānusantatavuttīti acchiddacatupārisuddhisīlavutti. Diṭṭhiyā savisaye paññāsadisī pavattīti so visujjhamāno paññādhiko hotīti āha – “diṭṭhicarito sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamanto dhammānusārī bhavatī”ti. Taṇhāvasena micchāvimokkho hotīti taṇhācarito visujjhamāno saddhādhikova hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ – “taṇhācarito sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamanto saddhānusārī bhavatī”ti. Diṭṭhicarito sukhāya paṭipadāyātiādi paṭipadāniddeso heṭṭhā desanāhāravibhaṅge (netti. 5 ādayo) āgato eva, atthopi tattha sabbappakārato vutto eva.

81. By the passage beginning, ‘Therein, one of speculative temperament…,’ he shows the side of purification. Therein, ‘one whose conduct is continuously austere’ (sallekhānusantatavutti) means one who has an unceasing austere practice. Why? Because he has strong reverence for austerity. Indeed, a person of speculative temperament, even by improper means such as asceticism and disgust, for the most part acts with the intention of wearing away the defilements. Therefore, having gone forth in this Dispensation, he fulfills the austere practice by way of the ascetic practices. ‘One whose conduct is continuously devoted to the training’ (sikkhānusantatavutti) means one who has the conduct of the flawless fourfold purity of virtue. Because with respect to wrong view, in its own sphere, its functioning is similar to wisdom, therefore, when he is being purified, he becomes one with predominant wisdom. Thus he said: ‘One of speculative temperament, on entering the fixed course of rightness, becomes a Dhamma-follower.’ Because by way of craving there is wrong resolve, therefore, when a person of craving temperament is being purified, he becomes one with predominant faith. Therefore it is said: ‘One of craving temperament, on entering the fixed course of rightness, becomes a faith-follower.’ The exposition of the paths, beginning with ‘One of speculative temperament by the pleasant practice…,’ has already appeared below in the Analysis of the Teaching-Presentation, and its meaning has also been fully explained there in every way.

Apubbapadesu [V 0.0318] pana viveciyamānoti vimociyamāno. Paṭinissaratīti niyyāti vimuccatīti attho. Dandhañca dhammaṃ ājānātīti taṇhācaritassa mandapaññassa vasena vuttaṃ. Tikkhapañño pana khippaṃ dhammaṃ ājānātīti. “Sattāpi duvidhā”tiādinā indriyavibhāgena puna paṭipadāvibhāgaṃ dasseti, taṃ suviññeyyaṃ.

But among the new terms: ‘being secluded’ (viveciyamāno) means being liberated. ‘He relinquishes’ (paṭinissarati) means he goes forth, he is liberated; this is the meaning. ‘And he understands the Dhamma slowly’ is said with reference to a person of craving temperament who is of dull wisdom. But a person of sharp wisdom understands the Dhamma quickly. By the passage beginning, ‘Beings are of two kinds…,’ he again shows the division of the paths by way of the division of faculties. That is easy to understand.

“Ye hi kecī”tiādinā tāsaṃ paṭipadānaṃ niyyāne tīsupi kālesu ekantikabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tattha imāhi eva catūhi paṭipadāhīti imāhi eva catūhi paṭipadāhi, tabbinimuttāya aññāya paṭipadāya abhāvato. Catukkamagganti paṭipadācatukkaṃ, paṭipadā hi maggoti. Atha vā catukkamagganti nandiyāvaṭṭassa catuddisāsaṅkhātaṃ maggaṃ. Tā pana catasso disā disālocananaye āgamissanti. Kimatthaṃ pana catukkamaggaṃ paññapentīti āha “abudhajanasevitāyā”tiādi. Tattha abudhajanasevitāyāti apaṇḍitajanasevitāya. Bālakantāyāti bālajanakāmitāya. Rattavāsiniyāti rattesu rāgābhibhūtesu vasatīti rattavāsinī, tassā. Nandiyāti tatra tatrābhinandanaṭṭhena nandīsaṅkhātāya. Avaṭṭanatthanti samucchindanatthaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa bhūmīti ayaṃ taṇhāvijjānaṃ vasena saṃkilesapakkhe dve disā samathavipassanānaṃ vasena [M 0.0198] vodānapakkhepi dve disā catusaccayojanā nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa samuṭṭhānatāya bhūmīti.

By the passage beginning, ‘Whoever indeed…,’ he shows the certain nature of the going forth by means of those paths in all three times. Therein, ‘by these very four paths’ means by these four paths alone, because of the absence of any other path apart from them. ‘The fourfold path’ (catukkamagga) means the quartet of paths, for a path (paṭipadā) is indeed a way (magga). Alternatively, ‘the fourfold path’ means the way called the four directions of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa. These four directions will come in the section on the examination of directions. But as to why they teach the fourfold path, he says the passage beginning, ‘resorted to by the unwise…’ Therein, ‘resorted to by the unwise’ means resorted to by the foolish. ‘Dear to the childish’ means desired by childish people. ‘Residing in the passionate’ (rattavāsinī) means it dwells in those who are passionate, overcome by lust; hence it is called rattavāsinī. ‘Of that which is called Nandī’ means of that which is designated Nandī (delight) in the sense of delighting in this and that object. ‘For the purpose of not-turning’ (avaṭṭanatthaṃ) means for the purpose of eradicating. ‘This is called the ground of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method’ means: this application of the four truths—namely, two directions on the side of defilements by way of craving and ignorance, and two directions on the side of purification by way of serenity and insight—is called the ‘ground’ (bhūmi) because it is the basis for the arising of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method.

82. Evaṃ nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa bhūmiṃ niddisitvā idāni tassa disābhūtadhamme niddisantena yasmā cassa disābhūtadhammesu vuttesu disālocananayo vuttoyeva hoti, tasmā “veyyākaraṇesu hi ye kusalākusalā”ti disālocanalakkhaṇaṃ ekadesena paccāmasitvā “te duvidhā upaparikkhitabbā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha teti disābhūtadhammā. Duvidhāti “ime saṃkilesadhammā, ime vodānadhammā”ti evaṃ duvidhena. Upaparikkhitabbāti upapattito parito ikkhitabbā, dhammayuttito taṃtaṃdisābhāvena pekkhitabbā ālocitabbāti attho.

82. Having thus pointed out the ground of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method, now, by him who is pointing out its directional phenomena—and since, when its directional phenomena are spoken of, the method of examining directions is in fact spoken of—therefore, having partially reviewed the characteristic of the examination of directions with the words, 'For in the explanations, those which are skillful and unskillful...,' he began the passage, 'they should be investigated in two ways...' Therein, 'they' refers to the directional phenomena. 'In two ways' means in two ways, thus: 'these are phenomena of defilement, these are phenomena of purification.' 'Should be investigated' means they should be seen from all sides fittingly; they should be looked at and examined as their respective directional aspects in accordance with the Dhamma; this is the meaning.

Yaṃ pakāraṃ sandhāya “duvidhā upaparikkhitabbā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ dasseti “lokavaṭṭānusārī ca lokavivaṭṭānusārī cā”ti. Tassattho – loko eva vaṭṭaṃ lokavaṭṭaṃ. Lokavaṭṭabhāvena anusarati pavattatīti lokavaṭṭānusārī, saṃkilesadhammoti attho. Lokassa, lokato vā vivaṭṭaṃ lokavivaṭṭaṃ, nibbānaṃ. Taṃ anusarati anulomanavasena gacchatīti lokavivaṭṭānusārī, vodānadhammoti attho. Tenevāha – “vaṭṭaṃ nāma saṃsāro, vivaṭṭaṃ nibbāna”nti.

He shows the manner referred to when it was said, 'should be investigated in two ways,' with the phrase 'that which follows the round of the world and that which follows the turning away from the world.' The meaning of this is as follows: the world itself is the round, hence 'the round of the world' (lokavaṭṭa). Because it proceeds in accordance with the state of the world as the round, it is 'that which follows the round of the world'; the meaning is a phenomenon of defilement. The turning away (vivaṭṭa) of the world, or from the world, is 'the turning away from the world' (lokavivaṭṭa), which is Nibbāna. Because it proceeds towards that in a conforming manner, it is 'that which follows the turning away from the world'; the meaning is a phenomenon of purification. For that very reason, he said: 'The round is saṃsāra, the turning away is Nibbāna.'

Taṃ [V 0.0319] kathaṃ daṭṭhabbanti taṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena daṭṭhabbanti ce? Upacayena. Yathā kataṃ kammaṃ phaladānasamatthaṃ hoti, tathā kataṃ upacitanti vuccati. Evaṃ upacitabhāve kammaṃ nāma hoti, vipākavaṭṭassa kāraṇaṃ hotīti attho. Sabbepi kilesā catūhi vipallāsehi niddisitabbā, dasannampi kilesānaṃ vipallāsahetubhāvato. Te kattha daṭṭhabbāti te pana vipallāsā kattha passitabbāti āha – “dasa vatthuke kilesapuñje”ti. Dasavidhakāraṇe kilesasamūheti attho. Tattha kilesāpi kilesavatthu, kilesānaṃ paccayadhammāpi kilesavatthu. Tesu kāraṇabhāvena purimasiddhā kilesā parato paresaṃ kilesānaṃ paccayabhāvato kilesāpi kilesavatthu. Ayonisomanasikāro, ayonisomanasikāraparikkhatā ca dhammā kilesuppattihetubhāvato kilesappaccayāpi kilesavatthūti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

If it is asked, 'How should that kamma be seen? In what manner should it be seen?', the answer is: by way of accumulation. In the way that kamma that has been done becomes capable of giving fruit, so what has been done is called 'accumulated'. Thus, in the state of being accumulated, it is indeed kamma, and the meaning is that it becomes a cause for the round of results. All defilements should be indicated by the four perversions, because the ten bases of defilements are a cause for perversions. When it is asked, 'Where should they be seen?'—that is, 'Where should those perversions be seen?'—he said, 'in the heap of defilements with ten bases.' The meaning is: in the mass of defilements that has ten kinds of causes. Therein, defilements themselves are a basis for defilements, and the states that are conditions for defilements are also a basis for defilements. Among them, because previously arisen defilements, by way of being a cause, are a condition for other, later defilements, the defilements themselves are also a basis for defilements. Because unwise attention and the states encompassed by unwise attention are a cause for the arising of defilements, the conditions for defilements are also a basis for defilements. Thus it should be understood.

Cattāro [M 0.0199] āhārāti ettha āhārasīsena tabbisayā kilesāpi adhippetā. Catasso viññāṇaṭṭhitiyoti etthāpi eseva nayo. “Paṭhame āhāre”tiādinā dasavatthuke kilesapuñje purimaṃ purimaṃ pacchimassa pacchimassa kāraṇanti dasseti. Tattha paṭhame āhāreti visayabhūte paṭhame āhāre paṭhamo vipallāso pavattatīti attho. Sesāhāresupi eseva nayo. Paṭhame vipallāseti paṭhame vipallāse appahīne sati paṭhamaṃ upādānaṃ pavattatīti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ niddeseyeva kathayissāma.

In the phrase 'four nutriments,' by the heading 'nutriment,' the defilements that have them as their object are also intended. In the phrase 'four stations of consciousness' also, this is the same principle. By the phrase beginning 'in the first nutriment,' he shows that in the heap of defilements with ten bases, each preceding one is a cause for each succeeding one. Therein, in the phrase 'in the first nutriment,' the meaning is that when the first nutriment becomes the object, the first perversion arises. In the remaining nutriments also, this is the same principle. In the phrase 'in the first perversion,' the meaning is that when the first perversion is not abandoned, the first clinging arises. In the remaining phrases also, this is the same principle. Whatever should be said here, that we will say in the Exposition itself.

83. Idāni dasavatthukaṃ kilesapuñjaṃ taṇhāvijjāvasena dve koṭṭhāse karonto “yo ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro”tiādimāha. Tattha kabaḷīkārāhāraṃ phassāhārañca aparijānantassa taṇhācaritassa yathākkamaṃ kāyavedanāsu tibbo chandarāgo hoti, iti upakkilesassa chandarāgassa hetubhāvato yo ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yo ca phasso āhāro, ime taṇhācaritassa puggalassa upakkilesāti vuttā. Tathā manosañcetanāhāraṃ viññāṇāhārañca aparijānanto diṭṭhicarito tesu attasaññī niccasaññī ca hotīti vuttanayeneva te diṭṭhicaritassa puggalassa upakkilesāti vuttā. Tathā purimakā dve vipallāsā purimakāni eva ca dve dveupādānayogaganthāsavaoghasallaviññāṇaṭṭhitiagatigamanāni taṇhāpadhānattā taṇhāsabhāvattā taṇhāvisayattā ca taṇhācaritassa upakkilesāti vuttā. Pacchimakāni pana tāni diṭṭhipadhānattā diṭṭhisabhāvattā diṭṭhivisayattā ca diṭṭhicaritassa upakkilesāti vuttāti daṭṭhabbā.

83. Now, making the heap of defilements with ten bases into two parts by way of craving and ignorance, he said the phrase beginning 'the nutriment of physical food...'. Therein, for a person of craving-temperament who does not fully comprehend the nutriment of physical food and the nutriment of contact, intense desire and lust arise respectively in the physical body and in feelings. Thus, because they are a cause for desire and lust, which is a defilement, 'the nutriment of physical food' and 'the nutriment of contact' are said to be a defilement for a person of craving-temperament. Similarly, a person of view-temperament who does not fully comprehend the nutriment of mental volition and the nutriment of consciousness has the perception of self and the perception of permanence in them. Therefore, in the way already stated, these are said to be a defilement for a person of view-temperament. Likewise, the first two perversions, and the first two of each of the clingings, yokes, ties, cankers, floods, darts, stations of consciousness, and wrong courses of action are said to be a defilement for one of craving-temperament because they are dominated by craving, have the nature of craving, and are the object of craving. But the latter ones are said to be a defilement for one of view-temperament because they are dominated by wrong view, have the nature of wrong view, and are the object of wrong view. Thus it should be understood.

84. Kabaḷīkāre āhāre “asubhe subha”nti vipallāsoti catūsu āhāresu kabaḷīkāre [V 0.0320] āhāre catūsu ca vipallāsesu “asubhe subha”nti vipallāso daṭṭhabbo kabaḷīkārāhārassa asubhasabhāvattā asubhasamuṭṭhānattā ca. Tathā phassāhārassa dukkhasabhāvattā dukkhapaccayattā ca visesato tattha “dukkhe sukha”nti vipallāso. Tathā yebhuyyena sattā viññāṇe niccasaññino, saṅkhāresu ca attasaññino, cetanāpadhānā ca saṅkhārāti vuttaṃ – “viññāṇe āhāre…pe… attāti vipallāso”ti. Paṭhame vipallāse ṭhito kāme upādiyatīti “asubhe subha”nti vipariyesaggāhī kilesakāmena vatthukāme daḷhaṃ gaṇhāti[M 0.0200]. Idaṃ vuccati kāmupādānanti yaṃ tathā kāmānaṃ gahaṇaṃ, idaṃ vuccati kāmupādānaṃ. “Dukkhe sukha”nti vipariyesaggāhī “sīlabbatehi anāgate bhavavisuddhīti taṃ nibbutisukha”nti daḷhaṃ gaṇhāti. “Anicce nicca”nti vipariyesaggāhī “sabbe bhavā niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammā”ti saṃsārābhinandiniṃ bhavadiṭṭhiṃ daḷhaṃ gaṇhāti. “Anattani attā”ti vipariyesaggāhī “asati attani kassidaṃ kammaphalaṃ, tasmā so karoti, so paṭisaṃvedetī”ti attadiṭṭhiṃ daḷhaṃ gaṇhātīti imamatthaṃ dasseti “dutiye vipallāse ṭhito”tiādinā.

84. Concerning the statement, 'In the nutriment of physical food, the perversion is “the attractive in the unattractive”': among the four nutriments, in the nutriment of physical food, and among the four perversions, the perversion that proceeds as 'the attractive in the unattractive' should be understood, because the nutriment of physical food has an unattractive nature and an unattractive origin. Similarly, because the nutriment of contact has the nature of suffering and is a condition for suffering, the perversion that proceeds as 'happiness in suffering' should be especially understood in that context. Likewise, since beings for the most part have the perception of permanence in consciousness and the perception of self in formations—and formations are dominated by volition—it was therefore said: 'in the nutriment of consciousness... the perversion of self.' Explaining 'One established in the first perversion clings to sensual pleasures': one who grasps pervertedly as 'the attractive in the unattractive' firmly seizes sensual objects with sensual desire that is a defilement. As for 'This is called clinging to sensual pleasures': that grasping of sensual objects in such a way is called clinging to sensual pleasures. One who grasps pervertedly as 'happiness in suffering' firmly seizes the view that 'through rites and vows, in the future there is purification of existence,' which is the happiness of extinguishment. One who grasps pervertedly as 'permanence in the impermanent' firmly seizes the view of existence that delights in saṃsāra: 'All states of existence are permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change.' One who grasps pervertedly as 'self in what is not-self' firmly seizes the view of self: 'If there is no self, whose is this fruit of kamma? Therefore, the one who acts is the one who experiences.' He shows this meaning by the phrase beginning 'one established in the second perversion...'

Ayaṃ vuccati kāmayogoti yena kāmarāgasaṅkhātena kāmupādānena vatthukāmehi saha satto saṃyojīyati, ayaṃ kāmarāgo “kāmayogo”ti vuccati. Ayaṃ vuccati bhavayogoti yato sīlabbatupādānasaṅkhātena bhavupādānena bhavena saha satto saṃyojīyati, ayaṃ bhavarāgo “bhavayogo”ti vuccati. Ayaṃ vuccati diṭṭhiyogoti yāya ahetukadiṭṭhiādisaṅkhātāya pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā, sakkāyadiṭṭhiādiavasiṭṭhadiṭṭhiyā ca satto dukkhena saha saṃyojīyati, ayaṃ pāpikā diṭṭhi “diṭṭhiyogo”ti vuccati. Ayaṃ vuccati avijjāyogoti yāya attavādupādānena sakalavaṭṭadukkhena ca saha satto saṃyojīyati, ayaṃ avijjā “avijjāyogo”ti vuccati.

This is called the yoke of sensual desire: by that clinging to sensual desire, which is designated as sensual lust, a being is bound together with sense objects; this sensual lust is called the 'yoke of sensual desire.' This is called the yoke of existence: since by the clinging to existence, which is designated as the clinging to precepts and vows, a being is bound together with existence, this lust for existence is called the 'yoke of existence.' This is called the yoke of views: by which evil view, designated as the view of no-cause and so on, and by the remaining views beginning with the personality-view, a being is bound together with suffering; this evil view is called the 'yoke of views.' This is called the yoke of ignorance: by which ignorance, and by the clinging to the doctrine of self, a being is bound together with the entire round of suffering; this ignorance is called the 'yoke of ignorance.'

Yasmā pana kāmayogādayo abhijjhākāyaganthādīnaṃ paccayā honti, tasmā “paṭhame yoge ṭhito abhijjhāya kāyaṃ ganthatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha abhijjhāya kāyaṃ ganthatīti parābhijjhāyanalakkhaṇāya abhijjhāya nāmakāyaṃ ganthati ghaṭṭetīti attho. Tathā bhavapatthanāya appahīnattā bhavadiṭṭhibhavarāgavasena āghātavatthūsu sattā cittāni padūsentīti āha – “dutiye yoge ṭhito byāpādena kāyaṃ ganthatī”ti. Tathā diṭṭhivasena avijjāvasena ca sīlabbatehi sujjhati, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti ca abhinivisatīti āha – “tatiye…pe… idaṃsaccābhinivesena kāyaṃ ganthatī”ti.

Since the yokes of sensual desire and so on are the causes of the bodily ties of covetousness and so on, it is therefore said: 'Established in the first yoke, one binds the body with covetousness,' and so on. Therein, 'binds the body with covetousness' means that one binds or strikes the mental body with covetousness, which has the characteristic of coveting others' possessions. Similarly, because the desire for existence has not been abandoned, beings, by way of the view of existence and lust for existence, defile their minds regarding grounds for animosity; thus, he said: 'Established in the second yoke, one binds the body with ill will.' Likewise, by way of views and by way of ignorance, one adheres to the belief that 'one is purified by precepts and vows,' and 'this alone is true, the other is empty'; thus, he said: 'Established in the third... and so on... one binds the body with the adherence that this is the truth.'

Tassāti [V 0.0321] tassa abhijjhādīhi samannāgatassa puggalassa. Evaṃ ganthitāti evaṃ abhijjhāyanādivasena nāmakāyaṃ ganthitvā ṭhitā. Āsavantīti [M 0.0201] āsavabhāvena pavattanti. Kuto ca vuccati āsavantīti kuto pana hetuto te kilesā āsavantīti āsavahetuṃ pucchati. Yasmā pana kilesā kusalappavattiṃ nivāretvā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhantā, maggena asamucchinnā eva vā āsavānaṃ uppattihetu honti, tasmā “anusayato vā pariyuṭṭhānato vā”ti vuttaṃ. Abhijjhākāyaganthena kāmāsavoti abhijjhākāyaganthena siddhena kāmarāgasabhāvattā kāmāsavo siddho hoti. Katthacideva visaye domanassito tappaṭipakkhe visaye tabbisayabahule ca bhave patthetīti āha – “byāpādakāyaganthena bhavāsavo”ti. Parāmāsakāyaganthena diṭṭhāsavoti sīlabbataparāmāsakāyaganthena siddhena taṃsabhāvattā aparāparaṃ vā diṭṭhiyo ganthentassa diṭṭhāsavo siddho hoti. Idaṃsaccābhinivesakāyaganthena avijjāsavoti “idameva saccaṃ moghamañña”nti abhinivisantassa ayonisomanasikārato anekehi akusalehi dhammehi saddhiṃ avijjāsavo uppajjati, sabbesaṃ vā akusaladhammānaṃ avijjāpubbaṅgamattā idaṃsaccābhinivesakāyaganthena siddhena tassa hetubhūto avijjāsavo siddho hoti.

'Of that' means of that person who is endowed with covetousness and so on. 'Thus bound' means that, having bound the mental body in this way by means of coveting and so on, they remain. 'They flow' means they proceed with the nature of cankers. 'And why are they said to flow?' asks for the cause of the cankers, meaning: 'For what reason do those defilements become cankers?' Because defilements, having prevented the occurrence of wholesome states, stand having overcome the mind, or, being not yet cut off by the path, are the cause for the arising of cankers, it is therefore said: 'from latency or from manifestation.' 'Through the bodily tie of covetousness, the canker of sensual desire': through the established bodily tie of covetousness, the canker of sensual desire is established due to its having the nature of sensual lust. One who is displeased with a certain object longs for an object that is its opposite and for an existence where such objects are abundant; thus, he said: 'through the bodily tie of ill will, the canker of becoming.' 'Through the bodily tie of misapprehension, the canker of views': through the established bodily tie of clinging to precepts and vows, the canker of views is established for one who binds to various views, due to its having that nature. 'Through the bodily tie of adherence that this is the truth, the canker of ignorance': for one who adheres to the belief that 'this alone is true, the other is empty,' the canker of ignorance arises together with many unwholesome states due to unwise attention. Or, because all unwholesome states have ignorance as their forerunner, through the established bodily tie of adherence that this is the truth, the canker of ignorance, which is its cause, is established.

Yasmā pana āsavā eva paribuddhā vaṭṭasmiṃ ohananti osādentīti “oghā”ti vuccanti, tasmā vuttaṃ – “tassa ime cattāro āsavā”tiādi.

Because the cankers themselves, having matured, cause beings to sink and be submerged in the round of existence, they are called 'floods.' Therefore, it is said: 'For him, these four cankers,' and so on.

Anusayasahagatāti anusayabhāvaṃ appaṭikkhipitvā gatā pavattā, anusayabhūtā vā. Ajjhāsayanti cittaṃ. Anupaviṭṭhāti ogāḷhā. Hadayaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhantīti cittassa abbhantarasaṅkhātaṃ hadayaṃ āhantvā tiṭṭhanti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 5) “abbhantaraṭṭhena hadaya”nti. Tena vuccanti sallāti yasmā ajjhāsayaṃ anupaviṭṭhā hadayaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhanti, tena vuccanti “sallā”ti. Pīḷājananaṃ duruddharaṇatā ca sallaṭṭho. “Eso me attā”ti gahaṇamukhena “esohamasmī”ti gahaṇaṃ hotīti diṭṭhiṃ nissāyapi mānaṃ jappentīti āha “diṭṭhoghena mānasallo”ti.

'Accompanied by latency' means they have proceeded without rejecting the state of latency, or they have become latent. 'They incline' means towards the mind. 'Entered into' means sunk into. 'They stand striking the heart' means they stand having struck the heart, which is called the interior of the mind. For so it is said in the Aṭṭhasālinī: '"heart" in the sense of interior.' Therefore, they are called 'darts': because, having entered the disposition, they stand striking the heart, they are called 'darts.' Causing affliction and being difficult to extract is the meaning of 'dart.' By means of grasping 'This is my self,' the grasping 'I am this' occurs; thus, relying even on view, one generates conceit. Therefore, he said: 'through the flood of views, the dart of conceit.'

Pariyādinnanti aññassa okāsaṃ adatvā samantato gahitaṃ. Catūsu dhammesu saṇṭhahatīti ārammaṇapaccayatāya ārammaṇabhūtesu catūsu [M 0.0202] dhammesu patiṭṭhahati. Tāni sarūpato dasseti “rūpe vedanāya saññāya saṅkhāresū”ti. Nandūpasecanenāti lobhasahagatassa sampayuttā nandī sahajātakoṭiyā[V 0.0322], itarassa upanissayakoṭiyā upasecananti nandūpasecanaṃ, tena nandūpasecanena. Kena pana taṃ nandūpasecananti āha – “rāgasallena nandūpasecanena viññāṇenā”ti.

'Taken possession of' means taken all around, without giving opportunity to another. 'It stands in four things' means it is established in four things that have become objects, by way of being an object-condition. He shows them in their own nature with the phrase: 'in form, in feeling, in perception, in formations.' 'By the sprinkling of delight' means: for consciousness accompanied by greed, the associated delight is a 'sprinkling' by way of co-nascence; for other consciousness, the delight is a 'sprinkling' by way of decisive-support condition. Thus, it is 'sprinkling of delight'. By that sprinkling of delight. But by what is it sprinkled with delight? He says: 'by consciousness sprinkled with delight through the dart of lust.'

Tattha rāgasallenāti rāgasallena hetubhūtena nandūpasecanena viññāṇenāti itthambhūtalakkhaṇe karaṇavacanaṃ. Rūpūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhitīti rūpameva ārammaṇakaraṇavasena upagantabbato, viññāṇassa patiṭṭhābhāvato ca rūpūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhiti. Tiṭṭhati etthāti ṭhiti. Pañcavokārabhavasmiñhi abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇaṃ rūpakkhandhaṃ nissāya tiṭṭhati. Dosasallenāti sahajātena dosasallena. Yadā vedanūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhiti vuccati, tadā upanissayakoṭiyāva nandiyā upasittaṃ viññāṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vedanāpi domanassavedanāva. Yadā ca upanissayapaccayabhūtena dosasallena vedanūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhiti vuccati, tadā sahajātakoṭiyā, upanissayakoṭiyā vā nandiyā upasittaṃ viññāṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vedanā pana tissopi tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ ārammaṇūpanissayabhāvato. Tattha paṭhamanayo domanassārammaṇassa abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇassa vasena vutto. Dutiyo sabbavedanārammaṇassa vasenāpi daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Therein, regarding 'by the dart of lust': the instrumental 'by the dart of lust', which is the cause, is used in the phrase 'by consciousness sprinkled with delight' in the sense of indicating a characteristic. 'The station of consciousness that resorts to form' is so called because form itself is to be resorted to by way of making it an object, and because it is a foothold for consciousness. It is a station because consciousness stands therein. For in the five-constituent existence, formative consciousness stands depending on the form aggregate. 'By the dart of hatred' means by the co-nascent dart of hatred. When 'the station of consciousness that resorts to feeling' is mentioned, then consciousness should be understood as sprinkled with delight only by way of decisive support. The feeling, too, is only painful mental feeling. And when 'the station of consciousness that resorts to feeling' is mentioned in connection with the dart of hatred that has become a decisive support condition, then consciousness should be understood as sprinkled with delight either by way of co-nascence or by way of decisive support. The feelings, however, can be all three, because the three feelings can be an object-support and a decisive support. Therein, the first method is stated by way of formative consciousness that has painful mental feeling as its object. The second should be understood by way of that which has all feelings as its object.

Mānasallenāti mānasallena sahajātena, upanissayabhūtena vā. Mohasallenāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Ettha ca anādimatisaṃsāre itthipurisā rūpābhirāmāti rāgasallavasena paṭhamā viññāṇaṭṭhiti yojitā. Sabbāyapi vedanāya dukkhapariyāyasabbhāvato dukkhāya ca doso anusetīti dosasallavasena dutiyā, saññāvasena “seyyohamasmī”ti maññanā hotīti mānasallavasena tatiyā, saṅkhāresu samūhaghanaṃ dubbinibbhoganti mohasallavasena catutthī viññāṇaṭṭhiti yojitāti daṭṭhabbā.

‘By the dart of conceit’ means by the dart of conceit that is co-nascent or that has become a decisive support. The same method applies also to ‘by the dart of delusion’. And herein, because in beginningless saṃsāra men and women delight in form, the first station of consciousness is connected by way of the dart of lust. Because all feeling has the nature of being a synonym for suffering, and because hatred lies latent in suffering, the second is connected by way of the dart of hatred. Because by way of perception the conceiving, “I am superior,” occurs, the third is connected by way of the dart of conceit. Because in formations the compact mass is difficult to penetrate, the fourth station of consciousness is connected by way of the dart of delusion. Thus it should be understood.

Upatthaddhanti olubbhārammaṇabhūtāhi viññāṇaṭṭhitīhi upatthambhitaṃ. Tañca kammanti yaṃ “cetanā cetasika”nti pubbe (netti. 82) vuttaṃ. Ime ca kilesāti ime ca dasavatthukā kilesā. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

‘Supported’ means supported by the stations of consciousness that have become supporting objects. And that kamma is what was previously stated as: “Volition, a mental factor.” And these defilements are these defilements with ten bases. The rest is easy to understand.

85. Idāni [M 0.0203] āhārādayo nayānaṃ saṃkilesapakkhe disābhāvena vavatthapetuṃ “imā catasso disā”tiādi āraddhaṃ, taṃ uttānameva. Puna kabaḷīkāro āhārotiādi āhārādīsuyeva yassa puggalassa upakkilesā, taṃ vibhajitvā dassetuṃ āraddhaṃ. Tattha dasannaṃ suttānanti ekadesesu samudāyavohārena vuttaṃ. Samudāyesu hi pavattā samaññā avayavesupi dissati[V 0.0323], “yathā paṭo daḍḍho, samuddo diṭṭho”ti ca. Eko atthoti ekassa atthassa nipphādanato vuttaṃ. Byañjanameva nānanti ettha byañjanaggahaṇena byañjanatthopi gahitoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Dasahipi suttapadehi savatthukā taṇhā vuttā. Taṇhā ca rāgacaritaṃ puggalaṃ khippaṃ dūsetīti āha – “ime rāgacaritassa puggalassa upakkilesā”ti. Yathā ca paṭhamadisābhāvena vuttadhammā rāgacaritassa upakkilesā, evaṃ dutiyadisābhāvena vuttadhammā dosacaritassa. Tatiyacatutthadisābhāvena vuttadhammā yathākkamaṃ diṭṭhicaritassa mandassa tikkhassa ca upakkilesā vuttā. Tesaṃ upakkilesabhāvo vuttanayānusārena veditabbo.

85. Now, in order to establish the methods concerning food and so on in the aspect of defilement by way of being directions, the passage beginning 'these four directions' is commenced; that is self-evident. Furthermore, beginning with 'physical food,' it is commenced to show by analysis which of these things, such as food, are defilements for which person. Herein, 'of the ten suttas' is stated using a collective designation for individual parts. For a designation that is applied to aggregates is also seen applied to their components, as in 'the cloth is burnt' or 'the ocean is seen.' 'One meaning' is stated because it accomplishes a single purpose. In the phrase 'only the wording is different,' it should be understood that by the term 'wording,' the meaning of the wording is also included. By all ten sutta passages, craving with its basis is stated. And since craving quickly corrupts a person of lustful temperament, it is said: 'These are the defilements for a person of lustful temperament.' And just as the things stated by way of the first direction are defilements for a person of lustful temperament, so the things stated by way of the second direction are defilements for a person of hateful temperament. The things stated by way of the third and fourth directions are stated as the defilements, respectively, for a person of speculative temperament who is dull and one who is sharp. Their nature as defilements should be understood according to the method already stated.

Āhāravipallāsādayo yadipi sabbehi tīhi vimokkhamukhehi pubbabhāge yathārahaṃ pariññeyyā pahātabbā ca. Yassa pana dukkhānupassanā purime āhāradvaye dukkhākārena bahulaṃ pavattati, tassa vasena yo ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yo ca phasso āhāro, ime appaṇihitena vimokkhamukhena pariññaṃ gacchantīti vuttaṃ. Esa nayo sesesu. Evañcetaṃ, na aññathā. Na hi ariyamaggānaṃ viya pahātabbesu vimokkhamukhānaṃ pariññeyyapahātabbesu koci niyamo sambhavati. Iti sabbe lokavaṭṭānusārino dhammā niyyanti, te lokā tīhi vimokkhamukhehīti nigamanaṃ. Tassattho – iti evaṃ vuttappakārā sabbe āhārādayo lokasaṅkhātavaṭṭānusārino dhammā te lokabhūtā vaṭṭato niyyanti aniccānupassanādīhi tīhi vimokkhamukhehīti.

Although distortions concerning food and so on are all to be fully understood and abandoned in the preliminary stage of insight by the three gateways to liberation as appropriate, it is nevertheless stated that for a person for whom contemplation of suffering occurs frequently in the aspect of suffering with regard to the first two foods, by his power, both physical food and food of contact come to be fully understood through the aimless gateway to liberation. This is the method for the rest. This is so, and not otherwise. For there is no fixed rule for the gateways to liberation regarding things to be fully understood and abandoned, as there is for the noble paths regarding things to be abandoned. 'Thus all things that follow the world's round are led out; those worlds are led out by the three gateways to liberation'—this is the conclusion. Its meaning is this: Thus all these various things beginning with food, which follow the round designated as 'the world'—these things that have become worldly are led out from the round by the three gateways to liberation, beginning with the contemplation of impermanence.

86. Evaṃ saṃkilesapakkhe disābhūtadhamme niddisitvā idāni vodānapakkhe disābhūtadhamme dassetuṃ “catasso paṭipadā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dibbabrahmaariyaāneñjavihāroti cattāro vihārā. Mānappahānaālayasamugghātaavijjāpahānabhavūpasamā cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā. Saccādhiṭṭhānādīni cattāri adhiṭṭhānāni. Chandasamādhibhāvanādayo catasso samādhibhāvanā. Indriyasaṃvaro tapasaṅkhāto puññadhammo [M 0.0204] bojjhaṅgabhāvanā sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggasaṅkhātaṃ nibbānañcāti cattāro sukhabhāgiyā dhammā veditabbāti.

86. Having thus indicated the phenomena that serve as directions in the aspect of defilement, now, to show the phenomena that serve as directions in the aspect of purification, the passage beginning 'four modes of practice' is stated. Therein, the divine, Brahma, noble, and imperturbable abodes are the four abodes. The abandonment of conceit, the uprooting of attachments, the abandonment of ignorance, and the stilling of becoming are the four amazing and wondrous phenomena. The resolutions beginning with the resolution of truth are the four resolutions. The developments of concentration beginning with that based on will are the four developments of concentration. Sense-restraint; the meritorious practice designated as austerity; the development of the factors of enlightenment; and Nibbāna, designated as the relinquishment of all substrates—these are to be understood as the four things partaking of happiness.

Paṭhamā paṭipadātiādi paṭipadāsatipaṭṭhānādīnaṃ abhedasandassanaṃ. Yadi evaṃ kasmā visuṃ gahaṇaṃ katanti? Dasavatthukassa kilesapuñjassa paṭipakkhabhāvadassanatthaṃ paṭipadādidasakaniddeso. Tathā hi vakkhati – “cattāro āhārā tesaṃ paṭipakkho catasso paṭipadā”tiādi [V 0.0324] (netti. 87). Kiñcāpi catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu “idaṃ nāma satipaṭṭhānaṃ imāya eva paṭipadāya ijjhatī”ti niyamo natthi, tathāpi paṭhamāya paṭipadāya paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ sambhavatīti sambhavavasena evaṃ vuttaṃ – “paṭhamā paṭipadā, paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhāna”nti. Yasmā pana āhāravipallāsādīnaṃ viya paṭipadāsatipaṭṭhānādīnaṃ atthato nānattaṃ natthi. Satipaṭṭhānāniyeva hi tathā tathā paṭipajjamānāni dukkhāpaṭipadādandhābhiññādināmakāni honti, tasmā yathā saṃkilesapakkhe “paṭhame āhāre paṭhamo vipallāso”tiādinā adhikaraṇabhedena vuttaṃ, evaṃ adhikaraṇabhedaṃ akatvā “paṭhamā paṭipadā, paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

The phrase 'the first practice,' etc., shows the non-difference of the practices, the foundations of mindfulness, and so on. If it is so, why is a separate mention made? The exposition of the decade beginning with the practices is for the purpose of showing the state of being the counterpart to the mass of defilements which has ten bases. For thus it will be said: 'The four nutriments; their counterpart is the four practices,' etc. Although among the four foundations of mindfulness there is no fixed rule that 'this particular foundation of mindfulness is accomplished only by this practice,' nevertheless, because the first foundation of mindfulness is possible through the first practice, it is stated thus by way of possibility: 'The first practice, the first foundation of mindfulness.' For, unlike the distortions of nutriment and so on, there is indeed no difference in essence for the practices, the foundations of mindfulness, and so on. For it is only the foundations of mindfulness, being practiced in such and such a way, that come to have names such as 'painful practice with slow direct knowledge,' etc. Therefore, just as in the aspect of defilement it was stated with a difference of locus, by the phrase 'in the first nutriment, the first distortion,' etc., so, without making a difference of locus, it was stated, 'The first practice, the first foundation of mindfulness,' etc. In the remaining cases, this is the same method.

Andhassa pabbatārohanaṃ viya kadācideva uppajjanakaṃ acchariyaṃ, accharāyoggaṃ acchariyanti porāṇā. Abhūtapubbaṃ bhūtanti abbhutaṃ. Ubhayampetaṃ vimhayāvahassa adhivacanaṃ. Na hi mānappahānādito aññaṃ durabhisambhavataraṃ vimhanīyañca upalabbhatīti adhitiṭṭhati etena, ettha vā adhiṭṭhānamattameva vā tanti adhiṭṭhānaṃ. Saccañca taṃ adhiṭṭhānañca, saccassa vā adhiṭṭhānaṃ, saccaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ etassāti vā saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Samādhi eva bhāvetabbatāya samādhibhāvanā. Sukhaṃ bhajatīti sukhabhāgiyo, sukhabhāgassa vā sukhakoṭṭhāsassa hitoti sukhabhāgiyo. Ekassapi sattassa asubhabhāvanādayo viya ekadese avattitvā anavasesapariyādānato natthi etissā pamāṇanti appamaññā.

Like the climbing of a mountain by a blind person, that which arises only sometimes is 'astonishing' (acchariyaṃ); 'that which is worthy of a finger-snap is astonishing,' thus say the ancients. 'What has not been before has come to be,' thus it is a 'marvel' (abbhutaṃ). Both of these are designations for that which brings astonishment. Indeed, other than the abandoning of conceit, etc., nothing more difficult to accomplish and more astonishing is found. 'By this, it is established (adhitiṭṭhati)'; or 'in this'; or 'it is mere establishment (adhiṭṭhānamattameva)'; thus it is 'determination' (adhiṭṭhānaṃ). It is both truth and determination; or it is the determination of truth; or for this, truth is its determination; thus it is 'determination of truth' (saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ). In the remaining cases, this is the same method. Concentration itself, because it is to be developed, is the 'development of concentration'. 'It partakes of happiness (sukhaṃ bhajati),' thus it is 'partaking of happiness' (sukhabhāgiyo); or, 'it is beneficial (hito) for a share of happiness (sukhabhāgassa), for a portion of happiness,' thus it is 'partaking of happiness'. Unlike the development of foulness and so on, it does not occur in a single part, and because it takes in even a single being without remainder, 'for this there is no measure (pamāṇaṃ),' thus it is 'immeasurable' (appamaññā).

Paṭhamā paṭipadā bhāvitā bahulīkatā paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ paripūretīti paṭhamāya paṭipadāya bhāvanābahulīkāro paṭhamassa satipaṭṭhānassa bhāvanāpāripūrīti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Yathā hi ariyamagge bhāvite satipaṭṭhānādayo bodhipakkhiyadhammā sabbepi bhāvitā eva honti, evaṃsampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Regarding the text 'The first practice, when developed and frequently practiced, fulfills the first foundation of mindfulness,' the meaning is this: the development and frequent practice of the first practice is the fulfillment of the development of the first foundation of mindfulness. In the remaining passages, too, this is the same method. For just as when the noble path is developed, all the states on the side of enlightenment, beginning with the foundations of mindfulness, are indeed developed, so this accomplishment should be understood.

Kāyānupassanāya [M 0.0205] kāmarāgassa ujuvipaccanīkabhāvato “paṭhamo satipaṭṭhāno bhāvito bahulīkato kāmapaṭipakkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ paripūretī”ti vuttaṃ. Tathā pītipaṭisaṃvedanādivasena pavattamānaṃ dutiyaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, sappītikassa dutiyajjhānassa cittassa abhippamodanavasena pavattamānaṃ tatiyaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ ukkaṃsagatasukhassa tatiyajjhānassa aniccavirāgādivasena pavattiyā saṅkhāresu upekkhakaṃ catutthaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvato catutthajjhānassa pāripūriyā saṃvattati.

Because contemplation of the body is the direct opposite of sensual lust, it is said: 'The first foundation of mindfulness, when developed and frequently practiced, fulfills the first jhāna, which is the counterpart to sensuality.' Similarly, the second foundation of mindfulness, which proceeds by way of experiencing joy and so on, conduces to the fulfillment of the second jhāna, which is accompanied by joy; the third foundation of mindfulness, which proceeds by way of gladdening the mind, conduces to the fulfillment of the third jhāna, which has sublime happiness; and the fourth foundation of mindfulness, which is equanimous towards formations due to proceeding by way of impermanence, dispassion, and so on, conduces to the fulfillment of the fourth jhāna because of the state of purity of mindfulness with equanimity.

Yasmā [V 0.0325] pana rūpāvacarapaṭhamajjhānaṃ rūpāvacarasamāpattīnaṃ, dutiyajjhānaṃ byāpādavitakkādidūrībhāvena brahmavihārānaṃ, tatiyajjhānaṃ pītivirāgena sukhena vipassanāya adhiṭṭhānabhūtaṃ ariyavihārānaṃ, catutthajjhānaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiāneñjappattaṃ āneñjavihārānaṃ visesato paccayo hoti, tasmā “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ paṭhamaṃ vihāraṃ paripūretī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Iti yo yassa visesapaccayo, so taṃ paripūretīti vuttoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Because the first form-sphere jhāna is a special condition for the form-sphere attainments; the second jhāna, by being far from thoughts such as ill will, is a special condition for the divine abodes; the third jhāna, which through the fading of joy and by means of happiness is a foundation for insight, is a special condition for the noble abodes; and the fourth jhāna, which has attained imperturbability through the purity of mindfulness with equanimity, is a special condition for the imperturbable abodes; therefore, it was stated: 'The first jhāna, when developed and frequently practiced, fulfills the first abode,' etc. Thus, it should be understood that it is said: 'Whatever state is a special condition for another state, that state fulfills that other state.'

87. Idāni paṭipadādayo vodānapakkhe disābhāvena vavatthapetuṃ “tattha imā catasso disā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Taṃ suviññeyyameva. Puna “paṭhamā paṭipadā”tiādi paṭipadācatukkādīsu yena yassa puggalassa vodānaṃ, taṃ vibhajitvā dassetuṃ āraddhaṃ. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva. Yadipi tīsu vimokkhamukhesu “idaṃ nāma vimokkhamukhaṃ imāya eva paṭipadāya ijjhatī”ti niyamo natthi. Yesaṃ pana puggalānaṃ purimāhi dvīhi paṭipadāhi appaṇihitena vimokkhamukhena ariyamaggādhigamo. Tathā yassa tatiyāya paṭipadāya suññatavimokkhamukhena, yassa ca catutthāya paṭipadāya animittavimokkhamukhena ariyamaggādhigamo, tesaṃ puggalānaṃ vasena ayaṃ paṭipadāvimokkhamukhasaṃsandanā. Satipaṭṭhānādīhi vimokkhamukhasaṃsandanāyapi eseva nayo.

87. Now, in order to establish the practices and so on as directions in the aspect of purification, it was stated: 'Therein, these are the four directions,' etc. That is easy to understand. Again, beginning with 'the first practice,' etc., it is undertaken to show by analyzing for which person purification occurs by which means among the tetrads of practice and so on. That is the same method as stated previously. Although among the three gateways to liberation there is no fixed rule that 'this particular gateway to liberation is accomplished only by this practice,' nevertheless, for those persons for whom there is attainment of the noble path through the desireless gateway to liberation by means of the first two practices; and similarly, for the person for whom there is attainment of the noble path through the emptiness gateway to liberation by means of the third practice; and for the person for whom there is attainment of the noble path through the signless gateway to liberation by means of the fourth practice—by way of those persons, this correlation of the practices and the gateways to liberation occurs. In the correlation of the gateways to liberation with the foundations of mindfulness and so on, this is the same method.

Tesaṃ vikkīḷitanti tesaṃ asantāsanajavaparakkamādivisesayogena sīhānaṃ buddhānaṃ paccekabuddhānaṃ buddhasāvakānañca vikkīḷitaṃ viharaṇaṃ. Yadidaṃ āhārādikilesavatthusamatikkamanamukhena saparasantāne paṭipadādisampādanā. Idāni āhārādīnaṃ paṭipadādīhi yena samatikkamanaṃ, taṃ nesaṃ paṭipakkhabhāvaṃ dassento “cattāro āhārā tesaṃ paṭipakkho catasso [M 0.0206] paṭipadā”tiādimāha. Tattha tesaṃ paṭipakkhabhāvo pahātabbabhāvo pahāyakabhāvo ca āhāraviññāṇaṭṭhitīnañcettha pahātabbabhāvo tappaṭibandhachandarāgavasena daṭṭhabbo. Tattha “vikkīḷitaṃ bhāvanā sacchikiriyā cā”tiādi tassāyaṃ saṅkhepattho – tesaṃ vikkīḷitanti ettha yadetaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ nāma bhāvetabbānaṃ bodhipakkhiyadhammānaṃ bhāvanā, sacchikātabbānaṃ phalanibbānānaṃ sacchikiriyā ca. Tathā pahātabbassa dasavatthukassa kilesapuñjassa tadaṅgādivasena pahānaṃ byantīkiriyā anavasesananti. Idāni taṃ saṅkhepena dassento “indriyādhiṭṭhānaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ vipariyāsānadhiṭṭhāna”nti āha.

Their sport (tesaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ): This is the sport, the dwelling, of those who are lions—the Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and disciples of the Buddha—due to their possession of special qualities such as fearlessness, swiftness, and vigor. That is to say, it is the accomplishment of the practices and so on in one's own and others' continuums by means of transcending the grounds of defilements such as nutriment. Now, showing their state of being an antidote, by which there is the transcending of nutriment and the like through the practices and the like, he says, 'The four nutriments, their antidote is the four practices,' and so on. Herein, their state of being an antidote is the state of being what is to be abandoned and the state of being what abandons. And here, the state of being what is to be abandoned of the nutriments and the stations of consciousness should be understood by way of the desire and lust connected with them. Herein, of the text 'sport is development and realization,' etc., this is the concise meaning: in the phrase 'their sport,' that which is called sport is the development of the factors of enlightenment that are to be developed, and the realization of the fruits and Nibbāna that are to be realized. Likewise, it is the abandoning, eradication, and complete removal of the heap of defilements with ten bases, by way of its parts and so forth. Now, showing that concisely, he says, 'The establishment of the faculties is sport, the non-establishment of distortions.'

Indriyādhiṭṭhānanti indriyānaṃ pavattanaṃ bhāvanā sacchikiriyā ca. Vipariyāsānadhiṭṭhānanti vipallāsānaṃ apavattanaṃ pahānaṃ anuppādanaṃ. Indriyāni saddhammagocaroti indriyāni cettha saddhammassa [V 0.0326] gocarabhūtāni pavattihetūti adhippetāni saddhindriyādīnīti attho. Vipariyāsā kilesagocaroti vipallāsā saṃkilesapakkhassa pavattiṭṭhānaṃ pavattihetūti. Ayaṃ vuccati sīhavikkīḷitassa nayassa bhūmīti yāyaṃ “cattāro āhārā”tiādinā saṃkilesapakkhe dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ, “catasso paṭipadā”tiādinā vodānapakkhepi dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ taṇhācaritādīnaṃ upakkilesavodānavibhāvanāmukhena niddhāraṇā, ayaṃ sīhavikkīḷitassa nayassa bhūmi nāma.

Establishment of the faculties (indriyādhiṭṭhāna) means the arising of the faculties, that is, development and realization. Non-establishment of distortions (vipariyāsānadhiṭṭhāna) means the non-arising, abandoning, and non-production of the distortions. The faculties are the domain of the True Dhamma (indriyāni saddhammagocaro): Here, the faculties, such as the faculty of faith and so on, are intended as the domain of the True Dhamma and the cause of its arising; this is the meaning. Distortions are the domain of defilements (vipariyāsā kilesagocaro): The distortions are the place of arising and the cause of arising for the side of defilement. This is called the ground of the lion's sport method (ayaṃ vuccati sīhavikkīḷitassa nayassa bhūmi): The determination of the ten sets of four on the side of defilement, beginning with 'the four nutriments,' and the ten sets of four on the side of purification, beginning with 'the four practices,' by means of clarifying the corruptions and purifications of those with craving-based temperaments and so on—this is called the ground of the lion's sport method.

88. Idāni ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalattayavasena tipukkhalanayassa bhūmiṃ vibhāvetukāmo yasmā pana nayānaṃ aññamaññānuppavesassa icchitattā sīhavikkīḷitanayato tipukkhalanayo niggacchati, tasmā paṭipadāvibhāgato cattāro puggale sīhavikkīḷitanayassa bhūmiṃ niddisitvā tato eva ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalattaye niddhāretuṃ “tattha ye dukkhāya paṭipadāyā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha ime dve puggalāti ime purimānaṃ dvinnaṃ paṭipadānaṃ vasena dve puggalā. Esa nayo itaratthāpi. Puna “tattha ye dukkhāya paṭipadāyā”tiādi yathāvuttapuggalacatukkato ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalattayaṃ niddhāretuṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha yo sādhāraṇāyāti dukkhāpaṭipadāya khippābhiññāya, sukhāpaṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya ca niyyātīti sambandho. Kathaṃ pana paṭipadādvayaṃ ekassa sambhavatīti? Nayidamevaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ekassa puggalassa ekasmiṃ dve paṭipadā sambhavantīti. Yathāvuttāsu pana dvīsu [M 0.0207] paṭipadāsu yo yāya kāyaci niyyāti, ayaṃ vipañcitaññūti ayamettha adhippāyo. Yasmā pana aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 350) paṭipadā calati na calatīti vicāraṇāyaṃ “calatī”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā ekassapi puggalassa jhānantaramaggantaresu paṭipadābhedo icchitovāti.

88. Now, wishing to clarify the ground of the method of three individuals (tipukkhalanaya) by way of the triad of individuals beginning with the ugghaṭitaññu; and since, because the interpenetration of the methods is desired, the method of three individuals emerges from the lion's sport method (sīhavikkīḷitanaya); therefore, having indicated the four individuals by way of the division of paths, and the ground of the lion's sport method, the passage beginning, 'Therein, those with the painful practice,' was undertaken in order to determine from just that group the triad of individuals beginning with the ugghaṭitaññu. Herein, 'these two individuals' means these two individuals by way of the first two practices. This is the method in the other case as well. Again, the passage beginning, 'Therein, those with the painful practice,' was stated to determine the triad of individuals beginning with the ugghaṭitaññu from the aforementioned fourfold group of individuals. Therein, 'one who is common' (yo sādhāraṇāya) is to be connected thus: 'is liberated (niyyāti) by the painful practice with quick direct knowledge, and by the pleasant practice with slow direct knowledge.' But how can two practices be possible for one person? It should not be seen thus: that two practices are possible for one individual at a single moment. Rather, among the two aforementioned practices, whoever is liberated by whichever of them, that one is a person of expanded wisdom (vipañcitaññū); this is the intention here. And since in the Aṭṭhasālinī, in the investigation of whether the practice fluctuates or not, it is stated that 'it fluctuates,' therefore, it should be understood that even for a single individual, a difference in practice between different jhānas and different paths is desired.

“Tattha bhagavā”tiādinā desanāvibhāgehipi tameva puggalavibhāgaṃ vibhāveti. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva. Tattha adhicittanti adhicittasikkhañcāti ca-saddo luttaniddiṭṭho. Tena adhicittasikkhañca adhipaññāsikkhañca vipañcitaññussa paññapetīti attho. Adhisīlanti etthāpi eseva nayo. Adhisīlasikkhaṃ adhicittasikkhaṃ adhipaññāsikkhañcāti yojetabbaṃ.

By the passage beginning, 'Therein, the Blessed One,' he also clarifies that same division of individuals by means of the divisions of the teaching. That is in the same manner as stated previously. Therein, 'higher mind' (adhicittaṃ) means 'and the training in higher mind'; the particle 'ca' is indicated as elided. By that, the meaning is that he prescribes the training in higher mind and the training in higher wisdom for the person of expanded wisdom (vipañcitaññu). In 'higher virtue' (adhisīlaṃ) as well, this is the same method. It should be connected as: the training in higher virtue, the training in higher mind, and the training in higher wisdom.

Cattāri hutvā tīṇi bhavantīti liṅgavipallāsena vuttaṃ, cattāro puggalā hutvā tayo puggalā hontīti attho.

The statement, 'Having been four, they become three,' is stated with a change of gender. The meaning is: having been four individuals, they become three individuals.

Ayaṃ [V 0.0327] saṃkilesoti ayaṃ akusalamūlādidvādasattikasaṅgaho saṃkilissati etenāti saṃkilesoti katvā. Idaṃ vodānanti etthāpi eseva nayo.

This is defilement (ayaṃ saṃkileso): This collection of twelve sets beginning with the unwholesome roots is called 'defilement' (saṃkileso) because 'one is defiled by this' (saṃkilissati etena). In 'this is purification' (idaṃ vodānaṃ) as well, this is the same method.

Tīṇi hutvā dve bhavantīti nandiyāvaṭṭanayassa disābhūtadhammadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenevāha – “taṇhā ca avijjā cā”tiādi, taṃ sabbaṃ suviññeyyameva.

The statement, 'Having been three, they become two,' was stated for the purpose of showing the phenomena that are the cause for the nandiyāvaṭṭa method. Therefore, he said, 'Craving and ignorance,' and so on. All of that is very easy to understand.

Kasmā panettha nayānaṃ uddesānukkamena niddeso na katoti? Nayānaṃ nayehi sambhavadassanatthaṃ. Paṭhamanayato hi puggalādhiṭṭhānavasena tatiyanayassa, tatiyanayato ca dutiyanayassa sambhavoti imassa visesassa dassanatthaṃ paṭhamanayānantaraṃ tatiyanayo, tatiyanayānantarañca dutiyanayo niddiṭṭho. Dhammādhiṭṭhānavasena pana tatiyanayato dutiyanayo, dutiyanayato paṭhamanayopi sambhavatīti imassa visesassa dassanatthaṃ ante “taṇhā ca avijjā cā”tiādinā paṭhamanayassa bhūmi dassitā. Teneva hi “cattāri hutvā tīṇi bhavanti, tīṇi hutvā dve bhavantī”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ “dve hutvā cattāri bhavanti, dve hutvā tīṇi bhavanti, tīṇi hutvā cattāri bhavantī”ti ayampi nayo vattabbo siyāti? Saccametaṃ, ayaṃ pana nayo atthato dassito evāti [M 0.0208] katvā na vutto. Yasmā tiṇṇaṃ atthanayānaṃ aññamaññaṃ anuppaveso icchito, sati ca anuppavese tato viniggamopi sambhavati evāti. Ayañca attho peṭakopadesena vibhāvetabbo.

But why is the exposition here not made according to the order of enumeration of the methods? To show the arising of the methods from the methods. For, from the first method, by way of the individual as basis, the third method arises; and from the third method, the second method arises. To show this distinction, the third method is indicated after the first method, and the second method is indicated after the third method. By way of phenomena as basis, however, the second method arises from the third, and the first method also arises from the second. To show this distinction, the ground of the first method is shown at the end with 'craving and ignorance,' etc. Indeed, for that very reason, it is said: 'Having been four, they become three; having been three, they become two.' If so, should this method also be stated: 'Having been two, they become four; having been two, they become three; having been three, they become four'? This is true, but this method, having been shown in meaning, is thus not stated. Because the mutual interpenetration of the three methods of meaning is desired, and when there is interpenetration, emergence from that is also indeed possible. And this meaning should be clarified by means of the Peṭakopadesa.

Tatthāyaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya vibhāvanā – cattāro puggalā taṇhācarito duvidho mudindriyo tikkhindriyo ca. Tathā diṭṭhicaritoti. Tattha taṇhācarito mudindriyo dukkhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya niyyāti, tikkhindriyo dukkhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya niyyāti, diṭṭhicarito pana mudindriyo sukhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya niyyāti, tikkhindriyo sukhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya niyyāti. Iti imāsu paṭipadāsu yathārahaṃ ṭhitehi taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritehi cattāro āhārā tappaṭibandhachandarāgappahānena pahātabbā. Cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bhāvetvā cattāro vipallāsā daṭṭhabbāti sabbo yathāvuttanayo anugantabbo.

Herein is the explanation beginning from the outset—there are four individuals: the craving-natured, who is twofold as one with dull faculties and one with keen faculties; and similarly, the view-natured. Among them, a craving-natured individual with dull faculties is liberated by the painful path with slow direct knowledge, while one with keen faculties is liberated by the painful path with quick direct knowledge. A view-natured individual with dull faculties, on the other hand, is liberated by the pleasant path with slow direct knowledge, while one with keen faculties is liberated by the pleasant path with quick direct knowledge. Thus, by those of craving-nature and view-nature who are established in these paths as is appropriate, the four nutriments should be abandoned by the abandoning of the desire and lust connected with them. Having developed the four foundations of mindfulness, the four perversions should be seen—the entire method as stated should be followed.

Tatthāyaṃ pāḷi – tattha ye diṭṭhicaritā sattā, te kāmesu dosadiṭṭhī, na ca ye kāmesu anusayā samūhatā, te attakilamathānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti. Tesaṃ satthā vā dhammaṃ deseti aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī “kāmehi natthi attho”ti, te ca pubbeyeva kāmehi anatthikā[V 0.0328], iti kāme appakasirena paṭinissajjanti, te cetasikena dukkhena anajjhositā. Tena vuccati “sukhā paṭipadā”ti. Ye pana taṇhācaritā sattā, te kāmesu ajjhositā, tesaṃ satthā vā dhammaṃ deseti aññataro vā bhikkhu “kāmehi natthi attho”ti, te piyarūpaṃ dukkhena paṭinissajjanti. Tena vuccati “dukkhā paṭipadā”ti. Iti ime sabbe sattā dvīsu paṭipadāsu samosaraṇaṃ gacchanti dukkhāyañca sukhāyañca.

Herein is the Pāḷi: Among them, those beings who are of view-nature are accustomed to seeing the fault in sensual pleasures, and their latent tendencies toward sensual pleasures are not eradicated; they dwell devoted to the practice of self-mortification. To them, the Teacher or another respected spiritual companion teaches the Dhamma, saying, 'There is no benefit in sensual pleasures.' Since they were already disinclined towards sensual pleasures beforehand, they relinquish them with little trouble and are not overcome by mental suffering. Therefore, it is called 'the pleasant path.' But those beings who are of craving-nature are attached to sensual pleasures. To them, the Teacher or another bhikkhu teaches the Dhamma, saying, 'There is no benefit in sensual pleasures.' They relinquish what is dear with difficulty. Therefore, it is called 'the painful path.' Thus, all these beings converge upon the two paths—the painful and the pleasant.

Tattha ye diṭṭhicaritā sattā, te dvidhā tikkhindriyā ca mudindriyā ca. Tattha ye diṭṭhicaritā sattā tikkhindriyā, te sukhena paṭinissajjanti, khippañca abhisamenti. Tena vuccati – “sukhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā”ti. Tattha ye diṭṭhicaritā sattā mudindriyā paṭhamaṃ tikkhindriyaṃ upādāya dandhataraṃ abhisamenti, te sukhena paṭinissajjanti, dandhañca abhisamenti. Tena vuccati – “sukhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā”ti. Tattha taṇhācaritā sattā duvidhā tikkhindriyā ca mudindriyā [M 0.0209] ca. Tattha ye taṇhācaritā sattā tikkhindriyā, te dukkhena paṭinissajjanti, khippañca abhisamenti. Tena vuccati – “dukkhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā”ti. Tattha ye taṇhācaritā sattā mudindriyā paṭhamaṃ tikkhindriyaṃ upādāya dandhataraṃ abhisamenti, te dukkhena paṭinissajjanti, dandhañca abhisamenti. Tena vuccati – “dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā”ti. Imā catasso paṭipadāyo apañcamā achaṭṭhā. Ye hi keci nibbutā nibbāyanti nibbāyissanti vā imāhi catūhi paṭipadāhi anaññāhi, ayaṃ paṭipadā catukkamaggena kilese niddisati. Yā catukkamaggena ariyadhammesu niddisitabbā, ayaṃ vuccati sīhavikkīḷito nāma nayo.

Therein, beings of view-nature are of two kinds: those with keen faculties and those with dull faculties. Among them, beings of view-nature with keen faculties relinquish with ease and quickly comprehend. Therefore, it is said: 'The pleasant path with quick direct knowledge.' Therein, beings of view-nature with dull faculties, in comparison to the one with keen faculties, comprehend more slowly; they relinquish with ease but comprehend slowly. Therefore, it is said: 'The pleasant path with slow direct knowledge.' Therein, beings of craving-nature are of two kinds: those with keen faculties and those with dull faculties. Among them, beings of craving-nature with keen faculties relinquish with difficulty and quickly comprehend. Therefore, it is said: 'The painful path with quick direct knowledge.' Therein, beings of craving-nature with dull faculties, in comparison to the one with keen faculties, comprehend more slowly; they relinquish with difficulty and comprehend slowly. Therefore, it is said: 'The painful path with slow direct knowledge.' These four paths are not a fifth, nor a sixth. For all who have been extinguished, are being extinguished, or will be extinguished, it is by these four paths and no others. This path indicates the defilements by means of the fourfold way. That which is to be indicated in the noble dhammas by means of the fourfold way is called the method named 'the lion's sport'.

Tatrime cattāro āhārā, cattāro vipallāsā upādānā yogā ganthā āsavā oghā sallā viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo agatigamanānīti evaṃ imāni sabbāni dasa padāni. Ayaṃ suttassa saṃsandanā.

Therein are these: the four nutriments, the four perversions, the clingings, the yokes, the bodily ties, the taints, the floods, the darts, the stations of consciousness, and the wrong courses—thus all these are ten terms. This is the linking of the teaching.

Cattāro āhārā, tattha yo ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yo ca phasso āhāro, ime taṇhācaritena pahātabbā. Tattha yo ca manosañcetanāhāro, yo ca viññāṇāhāro, ime diṭṭhicaritena pahātabbā.

There are four nutriments. Among them, the nutriment of physical food and the nutriment of contact are to be abandoned by one of craving-nature. The nutriment of mental volition and the nutriment of consciousness are to be abandoned by one of view-nature.

Tattha paṭhamo āhāro paṭhamo vipallāso, dutiyo āhāro dutiyo vipallāso, tatiyo āhāro [V 0.0329] tatiyo vipallāso, catuttho āhāro catuttho vipallāso, ime cattāro vipallāsā apañcamā achaṭṭhā. Idañca pamāṇā cattāro āhārā.

Therein, the first nutriment is the first perversion, the second nutriment is the second perversion, the third nutriment is the third perversion, and the fourth nutriment is the fourth perversion. These four perversions are not a fifth, nor a sixth. And the measure for this is the four nutriments.

Tattha paṭhame vipallāse ṭhito kāme upādiyati, idaṃ kāmupādānaṃ. Dutiye vipallāse ṭhito anāgataṃ bhavaṃ upādiyati, idaṃ sīlabbatupādānaṃ. Tatiye vipallāse ṭhito viparītadiṭṭhiṃ upādiyati, idaṃ diṭṭhupādānaṃ. Catutthe vipallāse ṭhito khandhe attato upādiyati, idaṃ attavādupādānaṃ.

Therein, one established in the first perversion clings to sensual pleasures—this is the clinging to sensual pleasures. One established in the second perversion clings to future existence—this is the clinging to precepts and practices. One established in the third perversion clings to a perverted view—this is the clinging to views. One established in the fourth perversion clings to the aggregates as self—this is the clinging to a doctrine of self.

Tattha kāmupādāne ṭhito kāme abhijjhāya ganthati, ayaṃ abhijjhākāyagantho. Sīlabbatupādāne ṭhito byāpādaṃ ganthati, ayaṃ byāpādakāyagantho. Diṭṭhupādāne ṭhito parāmāsaṃ ganthati, ayaṃ parāmāsakāyagantho. Attavādupādāne ṭhito papañcento ganthati, ayaṃ idaṃsaccābhinivesakāyagantho.

Therein, one established in clinging to sensual pleasures binds sensual pleasures with covetousness—this is the bodily tie of covetousness. One established in clinging to precepts and practices binds ill will—this is the bodily tie of ill will. One established in clinging to views binds adherence—this is the bodily tie of adherence. One established in clinging to a doctrine of self, proliferating, binds—this is the bodily tie of insistence that 'this alone is the truth'.

Tassa [M 0.0210] ganthaganthitā kilesā āsavanti. Kiṃ pana vuccati āsavantīti? Vippaṭisārā. Ye vippaṭisārā, te anusayā. Tattha abhijjhākāyaganthena kāmāsavo, byāpādakāyaganthena bhavāsavo, parāmāsakāyaganthena diṭṭhāsavo, idaṃsaccābhinivesakāyaganthena avijjāsavo.

For that person, the defilements bound by the ties flow out as taints. What, then, is said to flow out? Remorse. Those remorses are the underlying tendencies. Therein, through the bodily tie of covetousness there is the taint of sensuality; through the bodily tie of ill will there is the taint of existence; through the bodily tie of adherence there is the taint of views; through the bodily tie of insistence that 'this alone is the truth' there is the taint of ignorance.

Te cattāro āsavā vepullaṃ gatā oghā honti, tena vuccanti “oghā”ti. Tattha kāmāsavo kāmogho, bhavāsavo bhavogho, avijjāsavo avijjogho, diṭṭhāsavo diṭṭhogho.

Those four taints, having become extensive, become floods; therefore, they are called 'floods.' Therein, the taint of sensuality is the flood of sensuality, the taint of existence is the flood of existence, the taint of ignorance is the flood of ignorance, and the taint of views is the flood of views.

Te cattāro oghā āsayamanupaviṭṭhā anusayasahagatā vuccanti sallāti hadayamāhacca tiṭṭhanti. Tattha kāmogho rāgasallaṃ, bhavogho dosasallaṃ, avijjogho mohasallaṃ, diṭṭhogho diṭṭhisallaṃ.

Those four floods, having entered the disposition and being accompanied by underlying tendencies, are called 'darts'; having struck the heart, they remain. Therein, the flood of sensuality is the dart of lust, the flood of existence is the dart of aversion, the flood of ignorance is the dart of delusion, and the flood of views is the dart of views.

Imehi catūhi sallehi pariyādinnaṃ viññāṇaṃ catūsu dhammesu tiṭṭhati rūpe vedanāya saññāya saṅkhāresu. Imā catasso viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo. Tattha rāgasallena nandūpasecanaṃ rūpūpagaṃ viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhati. Dosasallena vedanūpagaṃ. Mohasallena saññūpagaṃ. Diṭṭhisallena nandūpasecanaṃ saṅkhārūpagaṃ viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhati.

Consciousness, overcome by these four darts, is established in four phenomena: in form, in feeling, in perception, and in formations. These are the four stations of consciousness. Therein, by the dart of lust, consciousness that is moistened by delight and has approached form is established. By the dart of aversion, consciousness that has approached feeling is established. By the dart of delusion, consciousness that has approached perception is established. By the dart of views, consciousness that is moistened by delight and has approached formations is established.

Catūhi [V 0.0330] viññāṇaṭṭhitīhi catubbidhaṃ agatiṃ gacchanti chandā dosā bhayā mohā. Rāgena chandā agatiṃ gacchati, dosena dosā agatiṃ gacchati, mohena mohā agatiṃ gacchati, diṭṭhiyā bhayā agatiṃ gacchati, iti imāni ca kammāni ime ca kilesā ayaṃ saṃsārahetu.

By means of the four stations of consciousness, they go to the four kinds of wrong courses: from desire, from aversion, from fear, and from delusion. Due to lust, one goes to a wrong course from desire. Due to aversion, one goes to a wrong course from aversion. Due to delusion, one goes to a wrong course from delusion. Due to views, one goes to a wrong course from fear. Thus, these actions and these defilements are the cause of saṃsāra.

Tatthimā catasso disā kabaḷīkāro āhāro “asubhe subha”nti vipallāso kāmupādānaṃ kāmayogo abhijjhākāyagantho kāmāsavo kāmogho rāgasallaṃ rūpūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhiti chandā agatigamanaṃ, ayaṃ paṭhamā disā.

Therein are these four directions: physical food; the perversion of perceiving 'the pleasant' in the unpleasant; the clinging to sensual pleasures; the yoke of sensuality; the bodily tie of covetousness; the taint of sensuality; the flood of sensuality; the dart of lust; the station of consciousness that has approached form; and going to a wrong course from desire—this is the first direction.

Phasso āhāro “dukkhe sukha”nti vipallāso sīlabbatupādānaṃ bhavayogo byāpādakāyagantho bhavāsavo bhavogho dosasallaṃ vedanūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhiti dosā agatigamanaṃ, ayaṃ dutiyā disā.

Contact as nutriment; the perversion of perceiving 'happiness' in suffering; the clinging to precepts and practices; the yoke of existence; the bodily tie of ill will; the taint of existence; the flood of existence; the dart of aversion; the station of consciousness that has approached feeling; and going to a wrong course from aversion—this is the second direction.

Manosañcetanāhāro “anattani attā”ti vipallāso diṭṭhupādānaṃ diṭṭhiyogo parāmāsakāyagantho diṭṭhāsavo diṭṭhogho diṭṭhisallaṃ saññūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhiti bhayā agatigamanaṃ, ayaṃ tatiyā disā.

Mental volition as nutriment; the perversion of perceiving 'self' in what is not-self; the clinging to views; the yoke of views; the bodily tie of adherence; the taint of views; the flood of views; the dart of views; the station of consciousness that has approached perception; and going to a wrong course from fear—this is the third direction.

Viññāṇāhāro [M 0.0211] “anicce nicca”nti vipallāso attavādupādānaṃ avijjāyogo idaṃsaccābhinivesokāyagantho avijjāsavo avijjogho mohasallaṃ saṅkhārūpagā viññāṇaṭṭhiti mohā agatigamanaṃ, ayaṃ catutthī disā. Iti imesaṃ dasannaṃ suttānaṃ paṭhamena padena paṭhamāya disāya ālokanaṃ, dutiyena padena dutiyāya disāya, tatiyena padena tatiyāya disāya, catutthena padena catutthiyā disāya ālokanaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati disā ālokanā. Iminā nayena sabbe kilesā catūsu padesu pakkhipitabbā. Ayaṃ akusalapakkho.

Consciousness as nutriment; the perversion of perceiving 'permanence' in the impermanent; the clinging to a doctrine of self; the yoke of ignorance; the bodily tie of insistence that 'this alone is the truth'; the taint of ignorance; the flood of ignorance; the dart of delusion; the station of consciousness that has approached formations; and going to a wrong course from delusion—this is the fourth direction. Thus, of these ten terms, by the first phrase there is the illumination of the first direction; by the second phrase, of the second direction; by the third phrase, of the third direction; and by the fourth phrase, there is the illumination of the fourth direction. This is called the illumination of the directions. By this method, all defilements should be included in the four phrases. This is the unwholesome side.
