Catasso paṭipadā, cattāri jhānāni, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro vihārā dibbo brahmā ariyo āneñjo, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, cattāro adhiṭṭhānā, cattāro samādhayo chandasamādhi vīriyasamādhi cittasamādhi vīmaṃsāsamādhi, cattāro dhammā sukhabhāgiyā nāññatra bojjhaṅgā nāññatra tapasā nāññatra indriyasaṃvarā nāññatra sabbanissaggā, cattāri appamāṇāni.

The four practices, the four jhānas, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four abodes—divine, brahmā, noble, and imperturbable; the four right strivings, the four amazing and wondrous qualities, the four determinations, the four concentrations—concentration due to desire, concentration due to energy, concentration due to mind, and concentration due to investigation; the four qualities partaking of happiness—not apart from the factors of enlightenment, not apart from austere practice, not apart from restraint of the faculties, not apart from total relinquishment; the four immeasurables.

Tattha [V 0.0331] dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā bhāviyamānā bahulīkariyamānā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ paripūreti, paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ paripūreti, paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ vihāraṃ paripūreti, paṭhamo vihāro paripuṇṇo paṭhamaṃ sammappadhānaṃ paripūreti, paṭhamaṃ sammappadhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ acchariyaṃ abbhutaṃ dhammaṃ paripūreti, paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo paripuṇṇo paṭhamaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ paripūreti, paṭhamaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ chandasamādhiṃ paripūreti, chandasamādhi paripuṇṇo indriyasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, indriyasaṃvaro paripuṇṇo paṭhamaṃ appamāṇaṃ paripūreti. Evaṃ yāva sabbanissaggā catutthaṃ appamāṇaṃ paripūreti.

Therein, the painful practice with slow direct knowledge, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the first jhāna; the first jhāna, when fulfilled, fulfills the first foundation of mindfulness; the first foundation of mindfulness, when fulfilled, fulfills the first abode; the first abode, when fulfilled, fulfills the first right striving; the first right striving, when fulfilled, fulfills the first amazing and wondrous quality; the first amazing and wondrous quality, when fulfilled, fulfills the first determination; the first determination, when fulfilled, fulfills concentration due to desire; concentration due to desire, when fulfilled, fulfills restraint of the faculties; restraint of the faculties, when fulfilled, fulfills the first immeasurable. In this way, up to total relinquishment, it fulfills the fourth immeasurable.

Tattha paṭhamā ca paṭipadā paṭhamañca jhānaṃ paṭhamañca satipaṭṭhānaṃ dibbo ca vihāro paṭhamañca sammappadhānaṃ paṭhamo ca acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saccādhiṭṭhānañca chandasamādhi ca indriyasaṃvaro ca mettā ca appamāṇaṃ. Ayaṃ paṭhamā disā.

Therein, the first practice, the first jhāna, the first foundation of mindfulness, the divine abiding, the first right striving, the first amazing and wondrous quality, the determination of truth, concentration due to desire, restraint of the faculties, and the immeasurable of loving-kindness—this is the first direction.

Dutiyā ca paṭipadā khippābhiññā dutiyañca jhānaṃ dutiyañca satipaṭṭhānaṃ brahmā ca vihāro dutiyañca sammappadhānaṃ dutiyo ca acchariyo abbhuto dhammo cāgādhiṭṭhānañca [M 0.0212] cittasamādhi ca tapo ca karuṇā ca appamāṇaṃ. Ayaṃ dutiyā disā.

The second practice with quick direct knowledge, the second jhāna, the second foundation of mindfulness, the Brahmā abiding, the second right striving, the second amazing and wondrous quality, the determination of relinquishment, concentration of mind, austerity, and the immeasurable of compassion—this is the second direction.

Tatiyā ca paṭipadā dandhābhiññā tatiyañca jhānaṃ tatiyañca satipaṭṭhānaṃ ariyo ca vihāro tatiyañca sammappadhānaṃ tatiyo ca acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saccādhiṭṭhānañca vīriyasamādhi ca bojjhaṅgā ca muditā ca appamāṇaṃ. Ayaṃ tatiyā disā.

The third practice with slow direct knowledge, the third jhāna, the third foundation of mindfulness, the noble abiding, the third right striving, the third amazing and wondrous quality, the determination of truth, concentration of energy, the factors of enlightenment, and the immeasurable of appreciative joy—this is the third direction.

Catutthī ca paṭipadā khippābhiññā catutthañca jhānaṃ catutthañca satipaṭṭhānaṃ āneñjo ca vihāro catutthañca sammappadhānaṃ catuttho ca acchariyo abbhuto dhammo upasamādhiṭṭhānañca vīmaṃsāsamādhi ca sabbanissaggo ca upekkhā ca appamāṇaṃ. Ayaṃ catutthī disā. Imāsaṃ catunnaṃ disānaṃ yā ālokanā, ayaṃ vuccati disālocano nāma nayo.

The fourth practice with quick direct knowledge, the fourth jhāna, the fourth foundation of mindfulness, the imperturbable abiding, the fourth right striving, the fourth amazing and wondrous quality, the determination of peace, concentration of investigation, total relinquishment, and the immeasurable of equanimity—this is the fourth direction. The viewing of these four directions is called the method of surveying the directions.

Tatthāyaṃ yojanā – cattāro ca āhārā, catasso ca paṭipadā, cattāro ca vipallāsā, cattāro ca satipaṭṭhānā, cattāri ca upādānāni, cattāri ca jhānāni, cattāro ca yogā, cattāro ca vihārā, cattāro ca ganthā, cattāro ca sammappadhānā, cattāro ca āsavā, cattāro ca acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, cattāro ca oghā, cattāri ca adhiṭṭhānāni, cattāri ca [V 0.0332] sallāni, cattāro ca samādhayo, catasso ca viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo, cattāro ca sukhabhāgiyā dhammā, cattāri ca agatigamanāni cattāri ca appamāṇāni. Iti kusalākusalānaṃ pakkhapaṭipakkhavasena yojanā. Ayaṃ sīhavikkīḷite disālocano nayo.

Herein is the connection: the four kinds of nutriment, the four kinds of practice, the four distortions, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four kinds of clinging, the four jhānas, the four yokes, the four abidings, the four bonds, the four right strivings, the four taints, the four amazing and wondrous qualities, the four floods, the four determinations, the four darts, the four concentrations, the four stations of consciousness, the four qualities that partake of happiness, the four wrong courses, and the four immeasurables. Thus is the connection of the wholesome and unwholesome by way of faction and counter-faction. This is the method of surveying the directions in the Lion's Play.

Tassa cattāri sāmaññaphalāni pariyosānaṃ, tattha paṭhamāya disāya sotāpattiphalaṃ pariyosānaṃ, dutiyāya sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, tatiyāya anāgāmiphalaṃ, catutthiyā arahattaphalaṃ pariyosānanti.

Its culmination is the four fruits of recluseship. Therein, for the first direction, the culmination is the fruit of stream-entry; for the second, the fruit of once-returning; for the third, the fruit of non-returning; for the fourth, the fruit of arahantship.

Tattha katamo tipukkhalanayo? Paṭipadāvibhāgena catūsu puggalesu yo sukhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya niyyāti, ayaṃ ugghaṭitaññū. Yo sukhāya vā paṭipadāya, dandhābhiññāya, dukkhāya vā paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya niyyāti, ayaṃ vipañcitaññū. Yo dukkhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya niyyāti, ayaṃ neyyo. Iti cattāro hutvā tayo honti. Tattha ugghaṭitaññussa samathapubbaṅgamā vipassanā sappāyā[M 0.0213]. Neyyassa vipassanāpubbaṅgamo samatho, vipañcitaññussa samathavipassanā yuganaddhā. Ugghaṭitaññussa mudukā desanā, neyyassa tikkhā desanā, vipañcitaññussa tikkhamudukā desanā.

Herein, what is the threefold method concerning individuals? By way of the distinction of practices, among the four individuals, one who is liberated by a pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge—this is the one of quick understanding. One who is liberated either by a pleasant practice with slow direct knowledge or by a painful practice with quick direct knowledge—this is the one who understands through elaboration. One who is liberated by a painful practice with slow direct knowledge—this is the one to be guided. Thus, being four, they become three. Therein, for the one of quick understanding, insight preceded by tranquility is suitable. For the one to be guided, tranquility preceded by insight is suitable. For the one who understands through elaboration, tranquility and insight yoked together are suitable. For the one of quick understanding, a gentle teaching is suitable. For the one to be guided, a sharp teaching is suitable. For the one who understands through elaboration, a sharp and gentle teaching is suitable.

Ugghaṭitaññussa adhipaññāsikkhā, vipañcitaññussa adhicittasikkhā ca adhipaññāsikkhā ca, neyyassa adhisīlasikkhā ca adhicittasikkhā ca adhipaññāsikkhā ca. Iti imesaṃ puggalānaṃ catūhi paṭipadāhi niyyānaṃ.

For the one of quick understanding, the higher training in wisdom is suitable. For the one who understands through elaboration, the higher training in mind and the higher training in wisdom are suitable. For the one to be guided, the higher training in virtue, the higher training in mind, and the higher training in wisdom are suitable. Thus, for these individuals, liberation is through the four practices.

Tatthāyaṃ saṃkilesapakkho, tīṇi akusalamūlāni, tayo phassā, tisso vedanā, tayo upavicārā, tayo kilesā, tayo vitakkā, tayo pariḷāhā, tīṇi saṅkhatalakkhaṇāni, tisso dukkhatā.

Herein is the faction of defilement: the three unwholesome roots, the three contacts, the three feelings, the three close examinations, the three defilements, the three thoughts, the three fevers, the three characteristics of the conditioned, and the three kinds of suffering.

Tīṇi akusalamūlānīti lobho akusalamūlaṃ, doso akusalamūlaṃ, moho akusalamūlaṃ. Tayo phassāti sukhavedanīyo phasso, dukkhavedanīyo phasso, adukkhamasukhavedanīyo phasso. Tisso vedanāti sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Tayo upavicārāti somanassūpavicāro, domanassūpavicāro, upekkhūpavicāro. Tayo kilesāti lobho, doso, moho. Tayo vitakkāti kāmavitakko, byāpādavitakko, vihiṃsāvitakko. Tayo pariḷāhāti [V 0.0333] rāgajo, dosajo, mohajo. Tīṇi saṅkhatalakkhaṇānīti uppādo, ṭhiti, vayo. Tisso dukkhatāti dukkhadukkhatā, vipariṇāmadukkhatā, saṅkhāradukkhatā.

The three unwholesome roots are: greed as an unwholesome root, hatred as an unwholesome root, and delusion as an unwholesome root. The three contacts are: contact felt as pleasant, contact felt as painful, and contact felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant. The three feelings are: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The three close examinations are: close examination with joy, close examination with displeasure, and close examination with equanimity. The three defilements are: greed, hatred, and delusion. The three thoughts are: sensual thought, thought of ill will, and thought of harming. The three fevers are: that born of lust, that born of hatred, and that born of delusion. The three characteristics of the conditioned are: arising, presence, and passing away. The three kinds of suffering are: suffering as pain, suffering due to change, and suffering due to conditioned formations.

Tattha lobho akusalamūlaṃ manāpikena ārammaṇena samuṭṭhahati. Tadeva manāpikārammaṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhavedanīyo phasso, sukhavedanīyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhā vedanā, sukhaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati somanassūpavicāro, somanassūpavicāraṃ paṭicca uppajjati rāgo, rāgaṃ paṭicca uppajjati kāmavitakko, kāmavitakkaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rāgajo pariḷāho, rāgajaṃ pariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati uppādo saṅkhatalakkhaṇaṃ, uppādaṃ saṅkhatalakkhaṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vipariṇāmadukkhatā.

Therein, greed, an unwholesome root, arises from a pleasing object. Dependent on that very pleasing object, contact felt as pleasant arises. Dependent on contact felt as pleasant, pleasant feeling arises. Dependent on pleasant feeling, the approach which has joy as its resort arises. Dependent on the approach which has joy as its resort, lust arises. Dependent on lust, sensual thought arises. Dependent on sensual thought, the fever born of lust arises. Dependent on the fever born of lust, the characteristic of the conditioned, which is arising, arises. Dependent on the characteristic of the conditioned, which is arising, suffering due to change arises.

Doso akusalamūlaṃ amanāpikena ārammaṇena samuṭṭhahati. Tadeva amanāpikārammaṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dukkhavedanīyo phasso, dukkhavedanīyaṃ [M 0.0214] phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dukkhā vedanā, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati domanassūpavicāro, domanassūpavicāraṃ paṭicca uppajjati doso, dosaṃ paṭicca uppajjati byāpādavitakko, byāpādavitakkaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dosajo pariḷāho, dosajaṃ pariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ saṅkhatalakkhaṇaṃ, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ saṅkhatalakkhaṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dukkhadukkhatā.

Hatred, an unwholesome root, arises from a disagreeable object. Dependent on that very disagreeable object, contact productive of painful feeling arises. Dependent on contact productive of painful feeling, painful feeling arises. Dependent on painful feeling, the approach which has displeasure as its resort arises. Dependent on the approach which has displeasure as its resort, hatred arises. Dependent on hatred, thought of ill will arises. Dependent on thought of ill will, the distress born of hatred arises. Dependent on the distress born of hatred, the characteristic of the conditioned, which is the alteration of what is present, arises. Dependent on the characteristic of the conditioned, which is the alteration of what is present, the suffering of pain arises.

Moho akusalamūlaṃ upekkhāṭhāniyaṃ ārammaṇena samuṭṭhahati. Tadeva upekkhāṭhāniyaṃ ārammaṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati adukkhamasukhavedanīyo phasso, adukkhamasukhavedanīyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati adukkhamasukhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati upekkhūpavicāro, upekkhūpavicāraṃ paṭicca uppajjati moho, mohaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vihiṃsāvitakko, vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ paṭicca uppajjati mohajo pariḷāho, mohajaṃ pariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vayo saṅkhatalakkhaṇaṃ, vayaṃ saṅkhatalakkhaṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkhāradukkhatā. Iti ayaṃ tīhi ākārehi kilesānaṃ niddeso. Yo koci akusalapakkho, sabbo so tīsu akusalamūlesu samosaratīti.

Delusion, an unwholesome root, arises from an object that is a basis for equanimity. Dependent on that very object that is a basis for equanimity, contact productive of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises. Dependent on contact productive of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises. Dependent on neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, the approach which has equanimity as its resort arises. Dependent on the approach which has equanimity as its resort, delusion arises. Dependent on delusion, thought of violence arises. Dependent on thought of violence, the distress born of delusion arises. Dependent on the distress born of delusion, the characteristic of the conditioned, which is passing away, arises. Dependent on the characteristic of the conditioned, which is passing away, the suffering due to formations arises. Thus, this is the exposition of the defilements in three aspects. Whatever belongs to the unwholesome side, all of that is included in these three unwholesome roots.

Tattha katamo kusalapakkho? Tīṇi kusalamūlāni alobho, adoso, amoho. Tisso paññā sutamayī, cintāmayī, bhāvanāmayī. Tayo samādhī savitakkasavicāro, avitakkavicāramatto, avitakkaavicāro. Tisso sikkhā adhisīlasikkhā, adhicittasikkhā[V 0.0334], adhipaññāsikkhā. Tīṇi nimittāni samathanimittaṃ, paggahanimittaṃ, upekkhānimittaṃ. Tayo vitakkā nekkhammavitakko, abyāpādavitakko, avihiṃsāvitakko. Tīṇi indriyāni anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ. Tayo upavicārā nekkhammūpavicāro, abyāpādūpavicāro, avihiṃsūpavicāro tisso esanā kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā. Tayo khandhā sīlakkhandho, samādhikkhandho, paññākkhandho.

Herein, what is the wholesome side? Three wholesome roots: non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion. Three kinds of wisdom: wisdom based on learning, wisdom based on reflection, and wisdom based on development. Three kinds of concentration: concentration with initial and sustained thought, concentration without initial thought and with sustained thought only, and concentration without initial and sustained thought. Three trainings: the higher training in virtue, the higher training in mind, and the higher training in wisdom. Three signs: the sign of serenity, the sign of exertion, and the sign of equanimity. Three thoughts: the thought of renunciation, the thought of non-ill will, and the thought of non-harming. Three faculties: the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown,' the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge. Three approaches: the approach of renunciation, the approach of non-ill will, and the approach of non-harming. Three quests: the quest for sensual pleasures, the quest for existence, and the quest for the holy life. Three aggregates: the aggregate of virtue, the aggregate of concentration, and the aggregate of wisdom.

Tattha alobho kusalamūlaṃ sutamayipaññaṃ paripūreti. Sutamayi paññā paripuṇṇā savitakkasavicāraṃ samādhiṃ paripūreti, savitakkasavicāro samādhi paripuṇṇo adhisīlasikkhaṃ paripūreti, adhisīlasikkhā paripuṇṇā [M 0.0215] samathanimittaṃ paripūreti, samathanimittaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ nekkhammavitakkaṃ paripūreti, nekkhammavitakko paripuṇṇo anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ paripūreti, anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ nekkhammasitūpavicāraṃ paripūreti, nekkhammūpavicāraṃ paripuṇṇo kāmesanaṃ pajahati. Kāmesanappahānaṃ sīlakkhandhaṃ paripūreti.

Herein, non-greed, the wholesome root, fulfills wisdom based on learning. Wisdom based on learning, when fulfilled, fulfills concentration with initial and sustained thought. Concentration with initial and sustained thought, when fulfilled, fulfills the higher training in virtue. The higher training in virtue, when fulfilled, fulfills the sign of serenity. The sign of serenity, when fulfilled, fulfills the thought of renunciation. The thought of renunciation, when fulfilled, fulfills the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown.' The faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown,' when fulfilled, fulfills the approach based on renunciation. The approach of renunciation, when fulfilled, abandons the quest for sensual pleasures. The abandonment of the quest for sensual pleasures fulfills the aggregate of virtue.

Adoso kusalamūlaṃ cintāmayipaññaṃ paripūreti, cintāmayipaññā paripuṇṇā avitakkavicāramattaṃ samādhiṃ paripūreti, avitakkavicāramatto samādhi paripuṇṇo adhicittasikkhaṃ paripūreti, adhicittasikkhā paripuṇṇā upekkhānimittaṃ paripūreti, upekkhānimittaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ abyāpādavitakkaṃ paripūreti, abyāpādavitakko paripuṇṇo aññindriyaṃ paripūreti, aññindriyaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ abyāpādūpavicāraṃ paripūreti, abyāpādūpavicāro paripuṇṇo bhavesanaṃ pajahati, bhavesanappahānaṃ samādhikkhandhaṃ paripūreti.

Non-hatred, the wholesome root, fulfills wisdom based on reflection. Wisdom based on reflection, when fulfilled, fulfills concentration without initial thought and with sustained thought only. Concentration without initial thought and with sustained thought only, when fulfilled, fulfills the higher training in mind. The higher training in mind, when fulfilled, fulfills the sign of equanimity. The sign of equanimity, when fulfilled, fulfills the thought of non-ill will. The thought of non-ill will, when fulfilled, fulfills the faculty of final knowledge. The faculty of final knowledge, when fulfilled, fulfills the approach of non-ill will. The approach of non-ill will, when fulfilled, abandons the quest for existence. The abandonment of the quest for existence fulfills the aggregate of concentration.

Amoho kusalamūlaṃ bhāvanāmayipaññaṃ paripūreti, bhāvanāmayipaññā paripuṇṇā avitakkaavicāraṃ samādhiṃ paripūreti, avitakkaavicāro samādhi paripuṇṇo adhipaññāsikkhaṃ paripūreti, adhipaññāsikkhā paripuṇṇā paggahanimittaṃ paripūreti, paggahanimittaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ avihiṃsāvitakkaṃ paripūreti, avihiṃsāvitakko paripuṇṇo aññātāvindriyaṃ paripūreti, aññātāvindriyaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ avihiṃsūpavicāraṃ paripūreti, avihiṃsūpavicāro paripuṇṇo brahmacariyesanaṃ paripūreti, brahmacariyesanā paripuṇṇā paññākkhandhaṃ paripūreti.

Non-delusion, the wholesome root, fulfills wisdom based on development. Wisdom based on development, when fulfilled, fulfills concentration without initial and sustained thought. Concentration without initial and sustained thought, when fulfilled, fulfills the higher training in wisdom. The higher training in wisdom, when fulfilled, fulfills the sign of exertion. The sign of exertion, when fulfilled, fulfills the thought of non-harming. The thought of non-harming, when fulfilled, fulfills the faculty of one who has final knowledge. The faculty of one who has final knowledge, when fulfilled, fulfills the approach of non-harming. The approach of non-harming, when fulfilled, fulfills the quest for the holy life. The quest for the holy life, when fulfilled, fulfills the aggregate of wisdom.

Iti ime tayo dhammā akusalapakkhikā kusalapakkhikā ca tikaniddesehi niddiṭṭhā tipukkhalanayassa [V 0.0335] disā nāma. Tassa pariyosānaṃ tayo vimokkhā appaṇihito suññato animitto, ayaṃ tipukkhalo nāma dutiyo nayo.

Thus, these threefold states, pertaining to the unwholesome side and the wholesome side, having been set forth by the expositions of triads, are called the directions of the method of the three persons. Its conclusion is the three liberations: the desireless, the empty, and the signless. This is the second method, called the method of the three persons.

Tattha ye ime tayo puggalā ugghaṭitaññū vipañcitaññū neyyoti imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ dve puggalā sukhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya, sukhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya ca niyyanti, dveyeva puggalā dukkhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya, dukkhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya ca niyyanti, ime cattāro. Te visesena dve honti diṭṭhicarito ca taṇhācarito ca. Ime [M 0.0216] cattāro hutvā tayo honti, tayo hutvā dve honti. Imesaṃ dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ ayaṃ saṃkileso – avijjā ca taṇhā ca ahirīkañca anottappañca asati ca asampajaññañca nīvaraṇāni ca saṃyojanāni ca ajjhosānañca abhiniveso ca ahaṃkāro ca mamaṃkāro ca assaddhiyañca dovacassatā ca kosajjañca ayonisomanasikāro ca vicikicchā ca avijjā ca asaddhammassavanañca asamāpatti ca.

Herein, among these three types of individuals—the one who understands by direct intuition, the one who understands by detailed explanation, and the one who needs guidance—two individuals are led out by way of pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge, and by way of pleasant practice with slow direct knowledge. Two individuals are led out by way of painful practice with quick direct knowledge, and by way of painful practice with slow direct knowledge. These are four. They are specifically two: one whose conduct is views and one whose conduct is craving. These four become three, and these three become two. For these two individuals, this is the defilement: ignorance and craving, shamelessness and lack of moral dread, lack of mindfulness and lack of clear comprehension, the hindrances and the fetters, clinging and obsession, conceit ('I-making') and possessiveness ('my-making'), lack of faith and intractability, laziness and unwise consideration, doubt, ignorance, not listening to the true Dhamma, and non-attainment.

Tattha avijjā ca ahirīkañca asati ca nīvaraṇāni ca ajjhosānañca ahaṃkāro ca assaddhiyañca kosajjañca vicikicchā ca asaddhammassavanañca, ayaṃ ekā disā.

Therein, ignorance, shamelessness, lack of mindfulness, the hindrances, clinging, conceit ('I-making'), lack of faith, laziness, doubt, and not listening to the true Dhamma—this is one direction.

Taṇhā ca anottappañca asampajaññañca saṃyojanāni ca abhiniveso ca mamaṃkāro ca dovacassatā ca ayonisomanasikāro ca avijjā ca asamāpatti ca, ayaṃ dutiyā disā. Dasannaṃ dukānaṃ dasa padāni paṭhamā disāti kātabbāni. Saṃkhittena atthaṃ ñāpenti paṭipakkhe kaṇhapakkhassa dasannaṃ dukānaṃ dasa padāni dutiyakāni, ayaṃ dutiyā disā.

Craving, lack of moral dread, lack of clear comprehension, the fetters, obsession, possessiveness ('my-making'), intractability, unwise consideration, ignorance, and non-attainment—this is the second direction. Of the ten pairs, the ten terms are to be made the first direction. The second ten terms of the ten pairs, which make known the meaning of the dark side by way of its opposite, are the second direction.

Tattha katamo kusalapakkho? Samatho ca vipassanā ca vijjā ca caraṇañca sati ca sampajaññañca hirī ca ottappañca ahaṃkārappahānañca mamaṃkārappahānañca sammāvāyāmo ca yonisomanasikāro ca sammāsati ca sammāsamādhi ca paññā ca nibbidā ca samāpatti ca saddhammassavanañca somanassañca dhammānudhammapaṭipatti ca.

Herein, what is the wholesome side? Tranquility and insight, knowledge and conduct, mindfulness and clear comprehension, moral shame and moral dread, the abandoning of conceit ('I-making') and the abandoning of possessiveness ('my-making'), right effort and wise consideration, right mindfulness and right concentration, wisdom and disenchantment, attainment, listening to the true Dhamma, joy, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma.

Dasannaṃ dukānaṃ samathādīni somanassapariyosānāni paṭhamāni dasa padāni paṭhamā disā, vipassanādīni dhammānudhammapaṭipattipariyosānāni dutiyāni dasa padāni dutiyā disā. Iti akusalapakkhe kusalapakkhe ca nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa catasso disā.

Of the ten pairs, the first ten terms, beginning with tranquility and culminating in joy, are the first direction. The second ten terms, beginning with insight and culminating in practice in accordance with the Dhamma, are the second direction. Thus, in the unwholesome side and the wholesome side, there are four directions of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method.

Tāsu [V 0.0336] kusalapakkhe samathādīhi akusalapakkhe taṇhādayo pahānaṃ gacchanti, tesaṃ pahānā rāgavirāgā cetovimutti, kusalapakkhe vipassanādīhi akusalapakkhe avijjādayo pahānaṃ gacchanti, tesaṃ pahānā avijjāvirāgā paññāvimutti. Iti imā dve vimuttiyo nandiyāvaṭṭanaye pariyosānaṃ.

Among these, on the wholesome side, through tranquility and so forth, craving and the like on the unwholesome side are abandoned. Through their abandonment, with the fading away of lust, there is liberation of mind. On the wholesome side, through insight and so forth, ignorance and the like on the unwholesome side are abandoned. Through their abandonment, with the fading away of ignorance, there is liberation by wisdom. Thus, these two liberations are the culmination in the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method.

Tattha [M 0.0217] taṇhā avijjā samatho vipassanāti cattāri padāni, tesu aṭṭhārasa mūlapadāni samosaranti. Kathaṃ? Samatho ca alobho ca adoso ca asubhasaññā ca dukkhasaññā cāti imāni pañca padāni samathaṃ bhajanti, vipassanā ca amoho ca aniccasaññā ca anattasaññā cāti imāni cattāri padāni vipassanaṃ bhajanti. Evaṃ nava padāni kusalāni dvīsu padesu samosaranti. Taṇhā ca lobho ca doso ca subhasaññā ca sukhasaññā cāti imāni pañca padāni taṇhaṃ bhajanti, avijjā ca moho ca niccasaññā ca attasaññā cāti imāni cattāri padāni avijjaṃ bhajanti. Evaṃ nava padāni akusalāni dvīsu padesu samosaranti. Iti tipukkhalo ca sīhavikkīḷito ca nandiyāvaṭṭanayaṃ anuppavisanti.

Herein, craving, ignorance, tranquility, and insight are the four terms. In them, eighteen root terms converge. How? Tranquility, non-greed, non-hatred, perception of foulness, and perception of suffering—these five terms pertain to tranquility. Insight, non-delusion, perception of impermanence, and perception of not-self—these four terms pertain to insight. Thus, nine wholesome terms converge in these two terms. Craving, greed, hatred, perception of beauty, and perception of pleasure—these five terms pertain to craving. Ignorance, delusion, perception of permanence, and perception of self—these four terms pertain to ignorance. Thus, nine unwholesome terms converge in these two terms. Thus, the Tipukkhala and the Sīhavikkīḷita enter into the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method.

Kathaṃ tipukkhale naye itare dve nayā anuppavisanti? Vipassanā ca amoho ca aniccasaññā ca anattasaññā cāti imāni cattāri padāni amoho, samatho ca alobho ca asubhasaññā ca dukkhasaññā cāti imāni cattāri padāni alobho, adoso adoso eva. Evaṃ nava padāni kusalāni tīsu padesu samosaranti. Taṇhā ca lobho ca subhasaññā ca sukhasaññā cāti imāni cattāri padāni lobho, avijjā ca moho ca niccasaññā ca attasaññā cāti imāni cattāri padāni moho, doso doso eva. Evaṃ nava padāni akusalāni tīsu padesu samosaranti. Iti tipukkhale naye itare dve nayā anuppavisanti.

How do the other two methods enter into the Tipukkhala method? Insight, non-delusion, perception of impermanence, and perception of not-self—these four terms are non-delusion. Tranquility, non-greed, perception of foulness, and perception of suffering—these four terms are non-greed. Non-hatred is just non-hatred. Thus, nine wholesome terms converge in these three terms. Craving, greed, perception of beauty, and perception of pleasure—these four terms are greed. Ignorance, delusion, perception of permanence, and perception of self—these four terms are delusion. Hatred is just hatred. Thus, nine unwholesome terms converge in these three terms. In this way, the other two methods enter into the Tipukkhala method.

Kathaṃ catūsu padesu aṭṭhārasa mūlapadāni samosaranti? Taṇhā ca subhasaññā ca, ayaṃ paṭhamo vipallāso. Lobho ca sukhasaññā ca, ayaṃ dutiyo vipallāso. Avijjā ca niccasaññā ca, ayaṃ tatiyo vipallāso. Moho ca attasaññā ca, ayaṃ catuttho vipallāso. Iti nava padāni akusalāni catūsu padesu samosaranti. Samatho ca asubhasaññā ca paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, alobho ca dukkhasaññā ca dutiyaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, vipassanā ca aniccasaññā ca tatiyaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, amoho ca anattasaññā ca catutthaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ. Iti nava padāni kusalāni catūsu padesu samosaranti. Evaṃ sīhavikkīḷitanaye [V 0.0337] itare dve nayā anuppavisanti. Tiṇṇañhi nayānaṃ yā bhūmiyo gocaro, so ekekaṃ nayaṃ [M 0.0218] anuppavisati. Tasmā ekekassa nayassa akusale vā dhamme viññāte kusale vā paṭipakkho anvesitabbo. Paṭipakkhaṃ anvesitvā so nayo niddisitabbo. Tamhi naye niddiṭṭhe yathā ekamhi naye itaresaṃ nayānaṃ mūlapadāni anuppaviṭṭhāni, tato tato nīharitvā niddisitabbāni. Ekekasmiñhi naye aṭṭhārasa mūlapadāni anuppaviṭṭhāni.

How do the eighteen root terms converge in the four terms? Craving and the perception of beauty are the first distortion. Greed and the perception of pleasure are the second distortion. Ignorance and the perception of permanence are the third distortion. Delusion and the perception of self are the fourth distortion. Thus, the nine unwholesome terms converge in the four terms. Serenity and the perception of foulness are the first foundation of mindfulness. Non-greed and the perception of suffering are the second foundation of mindfulness. Insight and the perception of impermanence are the third foundation of mindfulness. Non-delusion and the perception of not-self are the fourth foundation of mindfulness. Thus, the nine wholesome terms converge in the four terms. In this way, the other two methods enter into the Lion's Play method. Indeed, whatever are the domains and range of the three methods, that enters into each particular method. Therefore, for each method, when an unwholesome phenomenon is discerned, its wholesome opposite should be sought; and when a wholesome phenomenon is discerned, its unwholesome opposite should be sought. Having sought out the opposite, that method should be designated. When that method is designated, just as the root terms of the other methods have entered into one method, so they should be extracted from each respective method and designated. Indeed, in each method, the eighteen root terms have entered.

Tattha ekekasmiṃ dhamme viññāte sabbe dhammā viññātā honti. Imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ nayānaṃ sīhavikkīḷitassa nayassa cattāri phalāni pariyosānaṃ paṭhamāya disāya paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ, dutiyāya disāya dutiyaṃ phalaṃ, tatiyāya disāya tatiyaṃ phalaṃ, catutthāya disāya catutthaṃ phalaṃ pariyosānaṃ.

In each of those methods, when a single phenomenon is discerned, all phenomena are discerned. Of these three methods, for the Lion's Play method, the four fruits are the culmination. For the first direction, the first fruit is the culmination; for the second direction, the second fruit is the culmination; for the third direction, the third fruit is the culmination; for the fourth direction, the fourth fruit is the culmination.

Tipukkhalassa nayassa tayo vimokkhā pariyosānaṃ paṭhamāya disāya appaṇihito, dutiyāya suññato, tatiyāya animitto vimokkho pariyosānaṃ.

For the Tipukkhala method, the three liberations are the culmination. For the first direction, the aimless liberation is the culmination; for the second direction, the empty liberation is the culmination; for the third direction, the signless liberation is the culmination.

Nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa dve vimuttiyo pariyosānaṃ paṭhamāya disāya taṇhāvirāgā cetovimutti, dutiyāya disāya avijjāvirāgā paññāvimutti pariyosānaṃ. Imesu tīsu nayesu yā aṭṭhārasannaṃ padānaṃ ālocanā, ayaṃ disālocano nayo. Yā āloketvā kusalapakkhe akusalapakkhe ca “ayaṃ dhammo imaṃ dhammaṃ bhajatī”ti jānantena sammā yojanā, ayaṃ aṅkuso nayoti ime pañca nayā.

For the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method, the two liberations are the culmination. For the first direction, the liberation of mind through dispassion for craving is the culmination; for the second direction, the liberation by wisdom through dispassion for ignorance is the culmination. In these three methods, whatever is the examination of the eighteen terms, this is the directional examination method. Whatever is the proper application by one who knows—having examined both the wholesome and unwholesome sides—that 'This phenomenon pertains to that phenomenon,' this is the goad method. Thus, these are the five methods.

Nayasamuṭṭhānavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the section on the origination of methods is concluded.

Sāsanapaṭṭhānavāravaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Section on the Establishment of the Teaching

89. Evaṃ sabbathā nayasamuṭṭhānaṃ vibhajitvā idāni sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ vibhajanto yasmā saṅgahavārādīsu mūlapadeheva paṭṭhānaṃ saṅgahetvā sarūpato na dassitaṃ, tasmā yathā mūlapadehi paṭṭhānaṃ niddhāretabbaṃ, evaṃ paṭṭhānatopi mūlapadāni niddhāretabbānīti dassanatthaṃ “aṭṭhārasa mūlapadā kuhiṃ daṭṭhabbā? Sāsanapaṭṭhāne”ti āha. Mūlapadasāsanapaṭṭhānānañhi aññamaññasaṅgaho pubbe dassito evāti. Atha sāsanapaṭṭhānanti ko vacanattho? Sāsanassa paṭṭhānanti sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ[V 0.0338], sāsanaṃ [M 0.0219] desanā, tassā veneyyajjhāsayānurūpaṃ tesaṃ hitasukhanipphādanatthaṃ pakārehi ṭhānaṃ pavatti sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ. Idha pana tassa tathābhāvadīpanaṃ “sāsanapaṭṭhāna”nti veditabbaṃ. Atha vā sāsanaṃ adhisīlasikkhādayo. Tesaṃ pavattanupāyabhāvato patiṭṭhahanti etehīti paṭṭhānāni, saṃkilesādidhammā. Tesaṃ pavedanato tadupacārena suttāni paṭṭhānāni. Tesaṃ pana samūhabhāvato ayaṃ pakaraṇappadeso paṭṭhānaṃ nāma.

89. Having thus analyzed the origin of methods in all aspects, now, while analyzing the establishment of the teaching, because in the sections such as the Saṅgaha-vāra, the establishment was only included with the root terms without being shown in its own form, therefore, to show that just as the establishment should be determined from the root terms, so too the root terms should be determined from the establishment, it is said: 'Where are the eighteen root terms to be seen? In the establishment of the teaching.' For indeed, the mutual inclusion of the root terms and the establishment of the teaching was previously shown. Now, what is the meaning of the term 'establishment of the teaching'? 'The establishment of the teaching' (sāsanassa paṭṭhānaṃ) is 'sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ'. The teaching (sāsana) is the instruction (desanā); its establishment (paṭṭhāna) is its standing or occurrence in various ways, in accordance with the disposition of the disciples, for the purpose of accomplishing their welfare and happiness. Here, however, the demonstration of its nature as such should be known as 'the establishment of the teaching'. Alternatively, the teaching (sāsana) consists of the higher training in virtue and so on. Because they are the means for their occurrence, and because the trainings are established by these, the defilements and other phenomena are called 'establishments' (paṭṭhānāni). Because they make them known, the suttas are metaphorically called 'establishments' (paṭṭhānāni). Moreover, because this section of the treatise is a collection of these, it is called the 'establishment' (paṭṭhāna).

Aparo nayo – kenaṭṭhena paṭṭhānaṃ? Paṭṭhitaṭṭhena gamanaṭṭhenāti attho. “Ye te goṭṭhā paṭṭhitagāvo”ti (ma. ni. 1.156) āgataṭṭhānasmiñhi yena paṭṭhānena te “goṭṭhā paṭṭhitagāvo”ti vuttā, taṃ atthato gamanaṃ hoti. Iti nātivitthāritanayesu hāranayesu anissaṅgagamanassa desanāñāṇassa saṃkilesabhāgiyādilokiyādibhedesu tadubhayavomissakabhedesu ca vitthāritanayalābhato nissaṅgavasena pavattagamanattā te saṃkilesabhāgiyādayo lokiyādayo ca visuṃ visuṃ vomissā ca adhikaraṇavasena paṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Tesaṃ pakāsanato ayaṃ pakaraṇappadeso paṭṭhānanti veditabbaṃ.

Another method: by what meaning is it a 'paṭṭhāna'? The meaning is: by the meaning of having proceeded, by the meaning of going. For in the passage where it is said, 'Those are the cattle-folds to which the cows have proceeded' (MN 34), the 'paṭṭhāna' by which those cattle-folds are called 'having cows that have proceeded' is, in meaning, 'going'. Thus, because in the Hāra methods that are not overly extensive, the teaching-knowledge proceeds without impediment, and because an extensive method is obtained in the divisions such as those partaking of defilement, the worldly, etc., and in the divisions mixed with both of these, and because there is an occurrence of proceeding by way of non-attachment, those divisions—those partaking of defilement, etc., and the worldly, etc.—both separately and mixed, are called 'paṭṭhāna' by way of the subject matter. Because it makes them clear, this section of the treatise should be known as 'paṭṭhāna'.

“Saṃkilesabhāgiya”ntiādīsu saṃkilissati etenāti saṃkileso. Saṃkilesabhāge saṃkilesakoṭṭhāse pavattaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ. Vāsanā puññabhāvanā, vāsanābhāge pavattaṃ vāsanābhāgiyaṃ, vāsanaṃ bhajāpetīti vā vāsanābhāgiyaṃ. Nibbijjhanaṃ lobhakkhandhādīnaṃ padālanaṃ nibbedho. Nibbedhabhāge pavattaṃ, nibbedhaṃ bhajāpetīti vā nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ. Pariniṭṭhitasikkhādhammā asekkhā, asekkhabhāve pavattaṃ, asekkhe bhajāpetīti vā asekkhabhāgiyaṃ. Tesu yattha taṇhādisaṃkileso vibhatto, idaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ. Yattha dānādipuññakiriyavatthu vibhattaṃ, idaṃ vāsanābhāgiyaṃ. Yattha sekkhā sīlakkhandhādayo vibhattā, idaṃ nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ. Yattha pana asekkhā sīlakkhandhādayo vibhattā, idaṃ asekkhabhāgiyaṃ. Itarāni tesaṃ vomissakanayavasena vuttāni.

In 'partaking of defilement', etc.: 'one is defiled by this', thus it is 'defilement' (saṃkilesa). Occurring in the part of defilement, in the division of defilement, is 'partaking of defilement' (saṃkilesabhāgiya). 'Cultivation' (vāsanā) is the development of merit. Occurring in the part of cultivation is 'partaking of cultivation' (vāsanābhāgiya); or, 'it causes one to resort to cultivation', thus it is 'partaking of cultivation'. 'Penetration' (nibbedha) is the piercing, the destroying, of the aggregates of greed, etc. Occurring in the part of penetration is 'partaking of penetration' (nibbedhabhāgiya); or, 'it causes one to resort to penetration', thus it is 'partaking of penetration'. The dhammas of one whose training is completed are 'those beyond training' (asekkha). Occurring in the state of one beyond training is 'partaking of the state beyond training' (asekkhabhāgiya); or, 'it causes one to resort to those beyond training', thus it is 'partaking of the state beyond training'. Among these, a sutta wherein craving and other defilements are analyzed is one 'partaking of defilement'. A sutta wherein the grounds for meritorious deeds such as giving are analyzed is one 'partaking of cultivation'. A sutta wherein the aggregates of virtue, etc., of a trainee are analyzed is one 'partaking of penetration'. A sutta wherein the aggregates of virtue, etc., of one beyond training are analyzed is one 'partaking of the state beyond training'. The others are spoken of by way of a method of mixing these.

Tāni pana cha dukā cattāro tikā ekaṃ catukkaṃ aparampi ekaṃ catukkanti dvādasa honti. Tesu cattāro dukā dve ca tikā uddhaṭā, itare [M 0.0220] na uddhaṭā, anuddharaṇe kāraṇaṃ natthi. Iminā nayena tepi gahetuṃ sakkāti pāḷiyaṃ saṃkhittāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tathā hi vakkhati – “imāni cattāri suttāni, sādhāraṇāni katāni aṭṭha bhavantī”tiādi. Tattha yasmā katthaci sutte taṇhāsaṃkilesova niddisīyati, katthaci diṭṭhisaṃkilesova, katthaci duccaritasaṃkilesova [V 0.0339] niddisīyati, tasmā saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ tidhā vibhajitvā uddiṭṭhaṃ “taṇhāsaṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ sutta”ntiādinā. Tathā vodānaṃ nāma saṃkilese sati hotīti vodānabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ saṃkilesavibhāgena tidhāva uddiṭṭhaṃ “taṇhāvodānabhāgiyaṃ sutta”ntiādinā. Taṃ pana atthato vāsanābhāgiyādi eva hoti. Ayañca nayo kesuci potthakesu natthi.

Now, these are six dyads, four triads, one tetrad, and another tetrad, thus there are twelve. Among them, four dyads and two triads are extracted; the others are not extracted, and there is no reason for their non-extraction. It should be understood that by this method they too can be taken, thus they are abbreviated in the Pāḷi. For so it will be said: 'These four suttas, when made common, become eight,' and so on. Therein, because in some suttas only the defilement of craving is indicated, in others only the defilement of views, and in others only the defilement of misconduct, therefore the sutta partaking of defilement is divided into three and pointed out as 'the sutta partaking of the defilement of craving,' etc. Similarly, because purification occurs when there is defilement, the sutta partaking of purification is also pointed out in three ways according to the division of defilements as 'the sutta partaking of purification from craving,' etc. But that, in meaning, is just the sutta partaking of habitual tendencies, etc. And this method is not found in some manuscripts.

“Tattha saṃkileso tividho”tiādi saṃkilesapaṭipakkhato samathādiniddhāraṇavasena vāsanābhāgiyādisuttānaṃ visayadassanatthaṃ āraddhaṃ. Tattha yadi āsatti uppajjati bhavesūti bhavesu chandarāgaṃ pajahituṃ asakkontassa yadi bhavapatthanā uppajjati. Evaṃ sāyanti evamassa puggalassa ayaṃ samathavipassanābhāvanāmayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu bhavati pujjabhavaphalanibbattanato. Tatrūpapattiyā saṃvattatīti tatra tatra bhave upapattiyā saṃvattati. Imāni cattāri suttānīti imāni saṃkilesabhāgiyādīni cattāri suttāni. Sādhāraṇāni katānīti saṃkilesabhāgiyañca vāsanābhāgiyañca, saṃkilesabhāgiyañca nibbedhabhāgiyañca, saṃkilesabhāgiyañca asekkhabhāgiyañca, vāsanābhāgiyañca nibbedhabhāgiyañcāti evaṃ padantarasaṃyojanavasena missitāni katāni. Aṭṭha bhavantīti purimāni cattāri imāni cattārīti evaṃ aṭṭha bhavanti.

'Therein, defilement is threefold,' etc., is begun for the purpose of showing the domain of the suttas partaking of habitual tendencies, etc., by way of determining calm, etc., as the opposite of defilement. Therein, 'if attachment arises in existences' means: if for a person unable to abandon desire and lust for existences, the aspiration for existence should arise. This being so, for such a person this ground for meritorious action consisting of the development of calm and insight occurs, because it brings about the result of a worthy existence. 'It conduces to rebirth there' means: it conduces to arising in this or that existence. 'These four suttas' means these four suttas partaking of defilement, etc. 'They are made common' means: they are made mixed by way of combining with another term, thus: (1) partaking of defilement and partaking of habitual tendencies; (2) partaking of defilement and partaking of penetration; (3) partaking of defilement and partaking of the state beyond training; and (4) partaking of habitual tendencies and partaking of penetration. 'They become eight' means: the former four and these four, thus they become eight.

Tāniyeva aṭṭha suttāni sādhāraṇāni katāni soḷasa bhavantīti tāniyeva yathāvuttāni aṭṭha suttāni vāsanābhāgiyañca asekkhabhāgiyañca nibbedhabhāgiyañca, asekkhabhāgiyañca saṃkilesabhāgiyañca vāsanābhāgiyañca, nibbedhabhāgiyañca saṃkilesabhāgiyañca vāsanābhāgiyañca, asekkhabhāgiyañca saṃkilesabhāgiyañca nibbedhabhāgiyañca, asekkhabhāgiyañca vāsanābhāgiyañca nibbedhabhāgiyañca, asekkhabhāgiyañca saṃkilesabhāgiyañca vāsanābhāgiyañca, nibbedhabhāgiyañca asekkhabhāgiyañca nevasaṃkilesabhāgiyañca, navāsanābhāgiyañca nanibbedhabhāgiyañca na [M 0.0221] asekkhabhāgiyañcāti evaṃ sādhāraṇāni katāni purimāni aṭṭha imāni aṭṭhāti soḷasa bhavanti. Tesu cattāro ekakā, cha dukā, cattāro tikā, eko catukko, aparopi eko catukkoti ayampi vibhāgo veditabbo. Tatthāpi dve dukā, dve tikā, dve catukkā ca pāḷiyaṃ anāgatāti veditabbā.

Those same eight suttas, when made common, become sixteen. Those same eight suttas as mentioned are: that pertaining to habitual tendencies, that pertaining to the state beyond training, and that pertaining to penetration; that pertaining to the state beyond training, that pertaining to defilement, and that pertaining to habitual tendencies; that pertaining to penetration, that pertaining to defilement, and that pertaining to habitual tendencies; that pertaining to the state beyond training, that pertaining to defilement, and that pertaining to penetration; that pertaining to the state beyond training, that pertaining to habitual tendencies, and that pertaining to penetration; that pertaining to the state beyond training, that pertaining to defilement, and that pertaining to habitual tendencies; that pertaining to penetration, that pertaining to the state beyond training, and that not pertaining to defilement; and that not pertaining to habitual tendencies, not pertaining to penetration, and not pertaining to the state beyond training. Thus, when made common, the former eight and these eight become sixteen. Among these, there are four singles, six pairs, four triplets, one quartet, and another one quartet—this division should also be understood. Therein, it should be known that two pairs, two triplets, and two quartets are not found in the Pāḷi text.

Idāni imassa paṭṭhānassa sakalasāsanasaṅgahitabhāvaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “imehi soḷasahi suttehi bhinnehi navavidhaṃ suttaṃ bhinnaṃ bhavatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tassattho – imehi saṃkilesabhāgiyādīhi soḷasahi suttehi paṭṭhānanayena vibhattehi suttageyyādinavavidhaṃ pariyattisāsanasaṅkhātaṃ suttaṃ bhinnaṃ soḷasadhā [V 0.0340] vibhattaṃ hoti. Iminā soḷasavidhena paṭṭhānena asaṅgahito pariyattisāsanassa padeso natthīti adhippāyo. Kathaṃ pana saṃkilesabhāgiyādibhāvo gahetabboti? Āha “gāthāya gāthā anuminitabbā”tiādi. Tattha gāthāya gāthā anuminitabbāti ayaṃ gāthā viya gāthā saṃkilesabhāgiyāti vā vāsanābhāgiyāti vā nibbedhabhāgiyāti vā asekkhabhāgiyāti vā anuminitabbā, anu anu minitvā takketvā jānitabbāti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Ettha ca gāthāveyyākaraṇavinimuttā sabbā pariyatti “suttenā”tipadena saṅgahitāti daṭṭhabbā.

Now, to clarify the state of this Paṭṭhāna as encompassing the entire teaching, it is said: “Through these sixteen divided suttas, the ninefold sutta becomes divided.” Its meaning is this: through these sixteen suttas, such as those pertaining to defilement, classified by the method of the Paṭṭhāna, the sutta known as the scriptural teaching, which is ninefold beginning with sutta, geyya, and so on, becomes divided in sixteen ways. By this sixteenfold Paṭṭhāna, there is no portion of the scriptural teaching that is not encompassed—this is the intention. But how is the state of being related to defilement and so on to be understood? It is said: “A verse should be inferred by a verse,” and so on. Therein, “a verse should be inferred by a verse” means that a verse, like this verse, should be inferred as pertaining to defilement, or pertaining to habitual tendencies, or pertaining to penetration, or pertaining to the state beyond training; it should be known by repeatedly comparing, reflecting, and understanding—this is the meaning. This same method applies to the remaining terms. And here, it should be understood that all scriptural teaching apart from verses and expositions is included by the term “sutta.”

90. Idāni saṃkilesabhāgiyādīni suttāni yathāniddiṭṭhāni udāharaṇavasena vibhāvetuṃ “tattha katamaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ sutta”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha “kāmandhā jālasañchannā”ti gāthāya attho heṭṭhā vuttoyeva. Yathā imassa, evaṃ ito parānampi heṭṭhā vuttatthānaṃ uttānapadānañca atthaṃ na vaṇṇayissāma.

90. Now, to clarify the suttas beginning with that pertaining to defilement, as they have been pointed out, by way of example, the passage beginning, “Therein, which is the sutta pertaining to defilement?” is undertaken. Therein, the meaning of the verse, “Blinded by sensual desire, enshrouded by a net,” has already been stated below. Just as we will not explain the meaning of this, so too for what follows, we will not explain the meaning of terms whose meaning has already been stated below and of terms that are self-evident.

Agatigamanānīti kāyādīhi ayuttagamanāni, akattabbakaraṇānīti attho. Chandāti chandahetu icchāpaccayā. Agatiṃ gacchatīti agantabbaṃ gatiṃ gacchati, akattabbaṃ karotīti attho. Dhammanti sādhūnaṃ ariyānaṃ dhammaṃ. Ativattatīti atimadditvā vītikkamati. Nihīyatīti hāyati. Yasoti kitti ca parivāro ca.

‘Improper goings’ means improper goings by way of body and so forth; the meaning is the doing of what should not be done. ‘Due to desire’ means due to the cause of desire, conditioned by wishing. ‘Goes to an improper destination’ means one goes to a destination one should not go to; the meaning is one does what should not be done. ‘The Dhamma’ means the Dhamma of the good, the noble ones. ‘Transgresses’ means one transgresses by trampling upon. ‘Declines’ means one falls away. ‘Fame’ means renown and following.

“Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā”ti gāthāyaṃ manoti yadipi kāmāvacarakusalādibhedaṃ sabbampi catubhūmakacittaṃ mano, imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne cakkhupālattherassa [M 0.0222] (dha. pa. 1-2; theragā. 95) purimajātiyaṃ vejjabhūtassa uppannavasena niyamiyamānaṃ paṭighasampayuttacittameva labbhati. So mano pubbaṅgamo etesanti manopubbaṅgamā, manasā paṭhamagāminā samannāgatāti attho. Dhammāti nissattanijjīvaṭṭhena dhammā, te pana vedanādayo tayo arūpino khandhā. Ete hi manopubbaṅgamā. Kathaṃ panetehi saddhiṃ ekasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ ekasmiñca ārammaṇe ekakkhaṇe uppajjamāno mano pubbaṅgamo nāma hotīti? Uppādapaccayaṭṭhena. Yathā hi bahūsu ekato gāmaghātādikammāni karontesu “ko etesaṃ pubbaṅgamo”ti vutte yo tesaṃ paccayo hoti, yaṃ yaṃ nissāya te taṃ kammaṃ karonti, so datto vā mitto vā tesaṃ pubbaṅgamoti vuccati, evaṃsampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Iti uppādapaccayaṭṭhena mano pubbaṅgamo etesanti manopubbaṅgamā. Na hi [V 0.0341] te mane anuppajjante uppajjituṃ sakkuṇanti, mano pana ekaccesu cetasikesu anuppajjantesupi uppajjati eva.

In the verse, “Phenomena are preceded by mind,” regarding the term ‘mind,’ although ‘mind’ is all four-plane consciousness, which has divisions such as sense-sphere wholesome consciousness and so on, in this context, however, only consciousness associated with aversion is obtained, which is specified by way of its arising in the Elder Cakkhupāla, who was a physician in a former life. That mind is the forerunner of these phenomena, hence they are ‘preceded by mind’; the meaning is that they are endowed with a mind that goes first. ‘Phenomena’ means they are dhammā in the sense of being without a being and without a life-principle; those phenomena, however, are the three immaterial aggregates beginning with feeling. For these are preceded by mind. But how can the mind, arising in a single moment in the same base and on the same object together with these, be called the forerunner? In the sense of being the condition for arising. For just as when many people are committing acts such as raiding a village together, and it is asked, “Who is their forerunner?”, the one who is their condition, the one upon whom they rely to perform that act—whether named Datta or Mitta—is called their forerunner; so should this matter be understood. Thus, in the sense of being the condition for arising, the mind is the forerunner of these phenomena, hence they are ‘preceded by mind.’ For they cannot arise if the mind does not arise, but the mind can indeed arise even when certain mental factors do not arise.

Adhipativasena mano seṭṭho etesanti manoseṭṭhā. Yathā hi corādīnaṃ corajeṭṭhakādayo adhipatino seṭṭhā, tathā tesampi mano seṭṭho. Yathā pana dāruādīhi nipphannāni bhaṇḍāni dārumayādīni nāma honti, tathā etepi manato nipphannattā manomayā nāma. Paduṭṭhenāti abhijjhādīhi dosehi paduṭṭhena dūsitena bhāsati vā karoti vā. So hi bhāsanto catubbidhaṃ vacīduccaritameva bhāsati, karontopi tividhaṃ kāyaduccaritameva karoti, abhāsanto akaronto tehi abhijjhādīhi paduṭṭhamanatāya tividhaṃ manoduccaritaṃ pūreti. Evamassa dasa akusalakammapathā pāripūriṃ gacchanti. Tato naṃ dukkhamanvetīti tato tividhaduccaritato taṃ puggalaṃ dukkhaṃ anveti duccaritānubhāvena catūsu apāyesu dukkhaṃ anugacchati. Yathā kiṃ? Cakkaṃva vahato padanti, yathā nāma sakaṭaṃ vahato balībaddassa padaṃ paharantaṃ cakkaṃ anugacchati, evaṃ naṃ puggalaṃ dukkhamanugacchatīti.

By way of dominance, the mind is chief for these phenomena; therefore, they are called 'mind-chief'. For just as among thieves and the like, the chief thief and others are the leaders, the foremost ones, so too for those phenomena, the mind is chief. Furthermore, just as goods made from wood and the like are called 'wooden' and so on, so too these phenomena, because they are produced from the mind, are called 'mind-made'. By 'corrupted' is meant: by a mind corrupted, defiled by faults such as covetousness, one speaks or acts. For that person, when speaking, speaks only the fourfold verbal misconduct, and when acting, performs only the threefold bodily misconduct. When not speaking and not acting, due to having a mind corrupted by that covetousness and the like, one fulfills the threefold mental misconduct. Thus, for that person, the ten unwholesome courses of action reach fulfillment. By 'Then suffering follows him' is meant: because of that threefold misconduct, suffering follows that person; or, through the power of misconduct, suffering follows one into the four woeful states. How so? 'Like the wheel follows the foot of the one who pulls': just as the wheel, striking, follows the foot of the draught ox pulling the cart, so suffering follows that person.

“Middhī yadā hotī”ti gāthāyaṃ middhīti thinamiddhābhibhūto. Mahagghasoti mahābhojano āharahatthakaalaṃsāṭakatatravaṭṭakakākamāsakabhuttavamitakānaṃ aññataro viya. Niddāyitāti supanasīlo. Samparivattasāyīti seyyasukhapassasukhānaṃ anuyuñjanavasena samparivattakasayanasīlo[M 0.0223]. Nivāpapuṭṭhoti kuṇḍakādinā sūkarabhattena puṭṭho. Gharasūkaro hi bālakālato paṭṭhāya posiyamāno thūlasarīrakāle gehato bahi nikkhamituṃ alabhanto heṭṭhāmañcādīsu samparivattitvā samparivattitvā assasanto passasanto sayateva. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yadā puriso middhī ca hoti mahagghaso ca, nivāpapuṭṭho mahāvarāho viya aññena iriyāpathena yāpetuṃ asakkonto niddāsīlo saṃparivattasāyī, tadā so “aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā”ti tīṇi lakkhaṇāni manasi kātuṃ na sakkoti. Tesaṃ amanasikārā mandapañño punappunaṃ gabbhaṃ upeti, gabbhavāsato na parimuccatīti.

In the verse 'When one is drowsy,' by 'drowsy' is meant overcome by sloth and torpor. By 'a great glutton' is meant a great eater, like one of the Brahmins Āharahatthaka, Alaṃsāṭaka, Tatravaṭṭaka, Kākamāsaka, or Bhuttavamitaka. By 'a sleeper' is meant one who is habitually sleepy. By 'a roller-over in sleep' is meant one who, by way of indulging in the pleasure of lying down and the pleasure of rolling over, is habitually a roller-over in sleep. By 'fattened on fodder' is meant fattened with pig's food such as broken rice. For a household pig, being raised from a young age, when it has a large body and is unable to exit the house, it just rolls about under beds and the like, breathing in and out as it lies there. This is what is meant: when a person is drowsy and a great glutton, unable to maintain themselves in any other posture, like a great boar fattened on fodder, they are habitually sleepy and a roller-over in sleep. Then, they are unable to apply the mind to the three characteristics: 'impermanent, suffering, not-self.' Due to not applying the mind to these, the person of dull wisdom repeatedly enters the womb; they are not freed from dwelling in the womb.

“Ayasāva mala”nti gāthāyaṃ ayasāti ayato. Samuṭṭhitanti jātaṃ. Tatuṭṭhāyāti tato uṭṭhahitvā. Atidhonacārinanti dhonā vuccati cattāro paccaye idamatthitāya alametenāti paccavekkhitvā paribhuñjanapaññā, taṃ atikkamitvā caranto atidhonacārī nāma. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yathā ayato malaṃ samuṭṭhāya yato taṃ samuṭṭhitaṃ, tameva khādati vināseti, evamevaṃ cattāro [V 0.0342] paccaye appaccavekkhitvā paribhuñjantaṃ atidhonacārinaṃ sāni kammāni attano santāne uṭṭhitattā attano santakāneva tāni kammāni duggatiṃ nayantīti.

In the verse 'As rust from iron,' by 'ayasā' is meant: from iron. By 'samuṭṭhitaṃ' is meant: arisen. By 'tatuṭṭhāya' is meant: having arisen from that. Regarding 'atidhonacārinaṃ': the wisdom of using the four requisites after reflecting, 'This is sufficient for this purpose,' is called 'dhonā'. One who acts exceeding that is called an 'atidhonacārī' (one who transgresses in reflective use). This is what is meant: just as rust, having arisen from iron, eats and destroys that very iron from which it arose, so too, one's own actions—which, having arisen in one's own continuum, are indeed one's own—lead the 'atidhonacārī', who uses the four requisites without reflection, to a woeful state.

“Coro yathā”ti gāthāyaṃ coro yathā sandhimukhe gahītoti yathā coro gharasandhiṃ chinditvā gehaṃ pavisanto gharasandhimukhe eva rājapurisehi gahito. Sakammunā haññati bajjhate cāti tena attanā katakammena kasābhitāḷanādinā haññati ceva addubandhanādinā bajjhati ca. Evaṃ ayaṃ pecca pajā paratthāti evampi ayaṃ pāpakārinī pajā ito cavitvā paraloke. Sakammunā haññati bajjhate cāti attanāva katena pāpakammena nirayādīsu nānappakārehi kammakāraṇādīhi haññati ceva paribajjhati cāti.

In the verse 'As a thief,' by 'as a thief caught at the breach' is meant: just as a thief, having broken through the joint of a house and entering the house, is caught by the king's men right at the opening of the house-joint. By 'by his own deed he is afflicted and bound' is meant: by that deed done by oneself, one is afflicted by beating with whips and the like, and is bound with fetters and the like. By 'So this populace, having passed away, in the next world' is meant: so too, this evil-doing populace, having passed away from here, in the next world... By 'by his own deed he is afflicted and bound' is meant: by the evil deed done by oneself, in hell and other such states, one is afflicted and bound by various kinds of karmic tortures and the like.

“Sukhakāmānī”ti gāthāyaṃ yo daṇḍena vihiṃsatīti yo puggalo daṇḍena vā leḍḍuādīhi vā vibādhati. Pecca so na labhe sukhanti so puggalo paraloke manussasukhaṃ vā dibbasukhaṃ vā na labhati, nibbānasukhe pana vattabbameva natthi.

In the verse, 'Those who seek happiness,' by 'who harms with a rod' is meant: the person who afflicts with a rod or with clods of earth and the like. By 'having passed away, he does not obtain happiness' is meant: that person does not obtain human happiness or divine happiness in the next world; as for the happiness of Nibbāna, there is nothing to be said.

Gunnaṃ [M 0.0224] ce taramānānanti gāvīsu mahoghaṃ tarantīsu. Jimhaṃ gacchati puṅgavoti yadi yūthapati usabho kuṭilaṃ gacchati. Sabbā tā jimhaṃ gacchantīti sabbāpi tā gāviyo kuṭilameva gacchanti. Kasmā? Nette jimhaṃ gate satīti nettari kuṭilaṃ gate sati, nettassa kuṭilaṃ gatattāti attho. So hi tāsaṃ paccayiko upaddavaharo ca.

Regarding 'Gunnaṃ ce taramānānaṃ': when the cows are crossing a great flood. By 'the bull goes crookedly' is meant: if the bull, the leader of the herd, goes crookedly. By 'all of them go crookedly' is meant: all those cows go only crookedly. Why? By 'when the leader goes crookedly' is meant: when the leader has gone crookedly; the meaning is, because of the leader's going crookedly. For he is their trusted one and the remover of their dangers.

“Evameva”nti gāthāyaṃ yathā cetaṃ, evamevaṃ yo manussesu padhānasammato, yadi so adhammacārī siyā. Ye tassa anujīvino, sabbepi adhammikāva honti. Sāmisampadā hi pakatisampadaṃ sampādeti. Yasmā ca etadeva, tasmā sabbaṃ raṭṭhaṃ dukkhaṃ seti, rājā ce hoti adhammiko. Sukiccharūpā vatāti suṭṭhu kicchāpannarūpā vata. Upadhīsūti kāmaguṇūpadhīsu. Rattāti rāgābhibhūtā. Kaṭukanti dukkhaṃ.

In the verse beginning 'Evameva': just as this is, so too, if one who is considered a leader among humans should be one who practices unrighteously, those who are his followers all become unrighteous. For the perfection of the master brings about the perfection of the subordinates. And because this is so, therefore the entire kingdom dwells in misery if the king is unrighteous. By 'how difficult indeed' is meant: indeed, in a state of great difficulty. By 'in the substrates' is meant: in the substrates which are sensual pleasures. By 'attached' is meant: being overcome by lust. By 'bitter' is meant: suffering.

Kukkuccajanakeneva pattavaṭṭippabhavassa upacchinnattā phaluppatti kadaliyā parābhavāya hotīti āha – “phalaṃ ve kadaliṃ hantī”ti. Tathā phalapariyosānattā osadhīnaṃ “phalaṃ veḷuṃ phalaṃ naḷa”nti vuttaṃ. Vaḷavāya kucchismiṃ gadrabhassa jātā assatarī nāma, sā gabbhaṃ gaṇhitvā kāle sampatte vijāyituṃ na sakkoti. Pādehi bhūmiṃ paharantī tiṭṭhati, athassa cattāro [V 0.0343] pāde catūsu khāṇukesu bandhitvā kucchiṃ phāletvā potakaṃ nīharanti, sā tattheva marati. Tena vuttaṃ – “gabbho assatariṃ yathā”ti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yathā attano phalaṃ kadaliveḷunaḷepi vināseti, gabbho ca assatariṃ, evaṃ attano kammaphalabhūto sakkāro asappurisaṃ vināsetīti.

Because the arising of fruit is for the destruction of the banana tree, as the origin of its leaf-bud is cut off, he said, “Indeed, the fruit kills the banana tree.” Similarly, because the life of medicinal plants ends with their fruit, it is said, “The fruit kills the bamboo, the fruit kills the reed.” A she-mule, so named because she is born in the womb of a mare from a donkey, cannot give birth when the time arrives, having conceived. She stands striking the ground with her feet. Then, having bound her four feet to four stakes, they split open her belly and take out the young one. She dies right there. Therefore, it is said: “Just as the fetus kills the she-mule.” This is what is said: just as its own fruit destroys the banana tree, bamboo, and reed, and the fetus destroys the she-mule, so too does honor, which is the fruit of one’s own kamma, destroy an unvirtuous person.

Kodhamakkhagarūti kujjhanalakkhaṇaṃ kodhaṃ, paraguṇamakkhanalakkhaṇaṃ makkhañca garuṃ katvā uddhaṃ katvā ukkhipitvā caranto. Sukhetteti sukhettepi. Pūtibījaṃvāti pūtibhāvaṃ gataṃ bījaṃ viya. Chakaṇarasādiparibhāvanasukkhāpanasukhasayādīni akaraṇena bījadosaduṭṭhanti attho.

By 'one who holds anger and scorn in high esteem' is meant one who acts having made anger—which has the characteristic of rage—and scorn—which has the characteristic of disparaging others’ virtues—important, having held them high, having exalted them. By 'in a fertile field' is meant: even in a good field. By 'like a rotten seed' is meant: like a seed that has become rotten. The meaning is: corrupted by the fault of the seed due to not performing such things as soaking in cow-dung liquid, sun-drying, and proper storing.

91. Cetasāti attano cittena. Cetoti tassa puggalassa cittaṃ. Pariccāti paricchinditvā. Iriyatīti pavattati. Yathābhatanti yathā kiñci āharitvā ṭhapitaṃ.

91. By 'cetasā' is meant: with one’s own mind. By 'ceto' is meant: that person’s mind. By 'pariccā' is meant: having delimited. By 'iriyati' is meant: it proceeds. By 'yathābhataṃ' is meant: as something brought and placed.

Mākatthāti mā akattha. Na pamutyatthīti pamokkho natthi. Upeccāpīti sañciccāpi, buddhipubbenāpīti attho.

By 'mākattha' is meant: do not do. By 'na pamutyatthi' is meant: there is no release. By 'upeccāpi' is meant: even intentionally, with prior thought; this is the meaning.

“Adhammenā”ti [M 0.0225] vatvāpi “musāvādenā”ti vacanaṃ musāvādassa mahāsāvajjabhāvadassanatthaṃ. Tenevāha – “ekaṃ dhammaṃ atītassā”tiādi (dha. pa. 176), tathā “evaṃ parittaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ, yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjā”tiādi (ma. ni. 2.108). Taṃ kathaṃ nu bhavissatīti taṃ dhanaṃ kena nu pakārena tesaṃ bhavissati. Adhammena tesaṃ sambhatattā tesu naciraṭṭhitikaṃ hotīti attho. Antarāyā su bhavissantīti adhammiyavohārādito rājantarāyādayo bhavissanti. Sūti nipātamattaṃ. Sambhatassa vinassatīti imassa sambhataṃ sajjitaṃ vinassati. Sagganti sugatiṃ. Sā hi rūpādīhi sobhanehi aggoti saggoti adhippetā. Ettāvatāti diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikānaṃ atthānaṃ hāniyā. Hatāti vinaṭṭhā.

Even after saying 'by unrighteous means,' the statement 'by false speech' is for the purpose of showing the great blameworthiness of false speech. For that reason he said: “For one who transgresses the one dhamma…” (Dhp. 176), and similarly: “So limited, Rāhula, is the recluseship of those who have no shame in deliberate false speech…” (MN 61). By 'how then will it be?' is meant: by what means will that wealth come to them? The meaning is: because it was accumulated by them through unrighteousness, it is not long-lasting for them. By 'obstacles will arise' is meant: from unrighteous trade and so forth, royal dangers and the like will arise. 'Sū' is merely a particle. By 'his accumulated wealth perishes' is meant: this person's gathered, amassed wealth is destroyed. By 'heaven' is meant: a good destination. For it is intended as 'heaven' (sagga) because it is supreme (agga) with its beautiful forms and so forth. By 'to this extent' is meant: by the loss of benefits pertaining to the present life and the future life. By 'destroyed' is meant: ruined.

Vivaṭṭateti nivaṭṭati. Lobhā khaṇati attānanti lobhahetu apuññāni karonto kāyavisamādiyogena attānaṃ khaṇati nāma. Mittehi jīratīti mittabhāvehi hāyati.

By 'vivaṭṭate' is meant: is lost. By 'through greed, one undermines oneself' is meant: by doing demeritorious deeds because of greed, one is said to undermine oneself through bodily misconduct and the like. By 'one is estranged from friends' is meant: one declines in friendship.

Carantīti catūhi iriyāpathehi akusalameva karontā vicaranti. Bālāti idhalokatthaṃ paralokatthañca [V 0.0344] ajānantā idha bālā nāma. Dummedhāti nippaññā. Na hi paññāya duṭṭhattaṃ nāma atthi. Amittenevāti amittabhūtena viya verinā viya hutvā. Kaṭukapphalanti tikhiṇaphalaṃ, dukkhaphalanti attho. Na taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ sādhu, yaṃ katvā anutappatīti yaṃ kammaṃ nirayādīsu nibbattanasamatthaṃ dukkhudayaṃ katvā anussaritānussaritakkhaṇe anutappati anusocati, taṃ kataṃ na sādhu na sundaraṃ na bhaddakaṃ. Yassa assumukhoti yassa assūhi tintamukho rodanto vipākaṃ paṭisevati anubhoti.

By 'wandering' is meant: they wander, engaging only in unwholesome actions with the four postures. Regarding 'fools': those who do not know the benefit of this world or the next are called fools here. By 'unwise' is meant: lacking wisdom. For there is no such thing as the corruption of wisdom. By 'like an enemy' is meant: as if one has become an enemy, like a foe. By 'bitter fruit' is meant: having a pungent fruit, meaning a painful result. Regarding 'that deed is not well done, which, having done, one regrets': that deed which is capable of causing rebirth in hells and so forth, is productive of suffering, and which, having done, one regrets and grieves over at every moment of repeated recollection—that deed, when done, is not good, not beautiful, not auspicious. By 'he whose face is with tears' is meant: he who, with a face wet with tears, weeping, experiences and undergoes its result.

Dukkaranti vattapaṭivattapūraṇādivasena ābhisamācārikasīlassa kātuṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya dukkaraṃ. Samādānato paṭṭhāya khaṇḍaṃ akatvā visesato ādibrahmacariyakassa carimakacittaṃ pāpetabbatāya duttitikkhaṃ, sīlasaṃvarādayo vā aparikkhate katvā sampādetuṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya dukkaraṃ. Adhivāsetabbānaṃ pana dussahanato khantisaṃvaraṃvasena duttitikkhaṃ. Abyattenāti mandapaññena. Sāmaññanti samaṇabhāvo. Tatthāti tassa sāmaññassa. Sambādhāti dunnivatthaduppārutamātugāmādisammaddā. Yatthāti sīlasaṃvarādīnaṃ paribandhabhūtesu sambādhasaṅkhātesu visabhāgārammaṇādīsu[M 0.0226]. Atha vā dukkarantipadassa atthaṃ dassetuṃ duttitikkhanti vuttaṃ. Duttitikkhanti dukkhamaṃ duradhivāsiyaṃ. Abyattenāti bālena. Sāmaññanti samaṇadhammo. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yaṃ paṇḍitā kulaputtā dasapi vassāni vīsatipi…pe… saṭṭhipi vassāni dantebhi dantamādhāya jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhitvā ekāsanaṃ ekabhattaṃ paṭisevamānā āpāṇakoṭikaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carantā sāmaññaṃ karonti, taṃ bālā abyattā kātuṃ na sakkontīti. Bahūhi tattha sambādhāti tasmiṃ sāmaññasaṅkhāte ariyamagge bahū sambādhā, maggādhigamāya paṭipannassa bahū parissayāti attho.

‘Difficult to do’ means it is difficult to do because of the inability to perform the morality of proper conduct by way of fulfilling major and minor duties. ‘Difficult to endure’ means that, starting from the undertaking, it is hard to endure because the initial holy life must be maintained without a break up to the final consciousness. Alternatively, it is difficult to do because of the inability to accomplish moral restraint and so forth by keeping them unimpaired. Furthermore, it is difficult to endure because of the difficulty in bearing what must be endured by way of the restraint of patience. ‘By an unskilled person’ means by one of weak wisdom. ‘Recluseship’ means the state of a recluse. ‘Therein’ refers to that recluseship. ‘Constrictions’ means the crowding of improperly dressed and improperly covered women, and so forth. ‘Wherein’ refers to unsuitable sense-objects and so forth, which are called ‘constrictions’ and are obstacles to moral restraint and the like. Alternatively, to show the meaning of the term ‘difficult to do,’ the word ‘difficult to endure’ is stated. ‘Difficult to endure’ means hard to bear, difficult to tolerate. ‘By an unskilled person’ means by a fool. ‘Recluseship’ means the practice of a recluse. This is what is said: That recluseship which wise sons of good family accomplish, practicing the holy life to the very end of their lives for ten, twenty… even sixty years, setting tooth to tooth, pressing the tongue against the palate, restraining the mind with the mind, observing a single session and a single meal—that, fools and those with little wisdom are unable to do. ‘There are many constrictions there’ means that in that noble path called ‘recluseship,’ there are many constrictions; or, for one who has entered upon the practice for the attainment of the path, there are many dangers. This is the meaning.

Appameyyaṃ paminantoti appameyyaṃ khīṇāsavapuggalaṃ “ettakasīlo ayaṃ ettakasamādhi ettakapañño”ti evaṃ minanto. Kodha vidvā vikappayeti ko idha vidvā medhāvī vikappeyya, khīṇāsavova khīṇāsavaṃ minanto vikappeyyāti dīpeti. Nivutaṃ maññeti yo pana puthujjano minetuṃ ārabhati, taṃ nivutaṃ avakujjapaññaṃ maññāmi. Akissavanti kissavā vuccati paññā, nippaññanti attho.

‘Measuring the immeasurable’ means thus measuring the immeasurable person whose taints are destroyed, saying: ‘This one has this much morality, this much concentration, this much wisdom.’ ‘Who here, knowing, would discriminate?’ means: who in this world, being a wise and intelligent person, could discriminate? It is shown that only one whose taints are destroyed, when measuring another whose taints are destroyed, could discriminate. ‘I deem him covered’ means: whoever, being an ordinary person, undertakes to measure, him I deem covered, one with overturned wisdom. ‘Without wisdom’ (`akissavaṃ`): here `kissavā` is a term for wisdom; the meaning is ‘one without wisdom.’

Kuṭhārīti attacchedakaṭṭhena kuṭhārisadisī pharusavācā. Chindatīti kusalamūlasaṅkhāte mūleyeva nikantati. Visaṃ halāhalaṃ ivāti halāhalasaṅkhātaṃ visaṃ iva. Evaṃ viraddhaṃ pātetīti viraddhaṃ [V 0.0345] aparaddhaṃ khalitapuggalaṃ evaṃ apāyesu vinipāteti. Vācā dubbhāsitā yathāti yathā vācā ariyūpavādanavasena dubbhāsitā.

‘An axe’ means harsh speech, which is like an axe due to its nature of cutting oneself. ‘It cuts’ means it severs right at the root, that which is called the wholesome root. ‘Like poison, like deadly venom’ means like the poison known as halāhala. ‘Thus it casts down the offender’ means thus it throws the offender, the one who has erred, into the lower realms. ‘As speech is ill-spoken’ means: as speech that is ill-spoken by way of reviling the Noble Ones.

92. Nindiyanti nindanīyaṃ. Taṃ vā nindati yo pasaṃsiyoti yo guṇavisiṭṭhatāya pasaṃsāraho puggalo, taṃ vā so pāpicchatādīni āropetvā garahati. Vicinātīti upacināti. Kalinti aparādhaṃ. Ayaṃ kalīti ayaṃ aparādho. Akkhesūti jūtakīḷanakkhesu. Sabbassāpi sahāpi attanāti sabbena attano dhanenāpi attanāpi saddhiṃ. Sugatesūti sobhanagamanattā, sundaraṃ ṭhānaṃ gatattā, sammā gatattā, sammā ca gadattā sugatasaṅkhātesu buddhādīsu. Manaṃ padosayeti yo manaṃ padoseyya, tassa ayaṃ manopadoso eva mahattaro kalīti vuttaṃ hoti. Kasmā? Yasmā sataṃ sahassānaṃ…pe… pāpakanti. Tattha sataṃ sahassānanti nirabbudagaṇanāya satasahassaṃ. Chattiṃsatīti aparāni chattiṃsati [M 0.0227] nirabbudāni. Pañca cāti abbudagaṇanāya pañca ca abbudāni. Tasmā vassagaṇanāya ettako so kālo, yaṃ kālaṃ ariyagarahivācaṃ manañca paṇidhāya pāpakaṃ nirayaṃ upeti, tattha paccatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Idañca saṅkhepena padumaniraye āyuppamāṇaṃ, vitthārena pana parato āgamissati.

92. ‘One who is blameworthy’ (`nindiyaṃ`) means one who is censurable. ‘Or one blames him who is praiseworthy’ means: a person who is worthy of praise on account of distinguished qualities, even him one criticizes by falsely ascribing to him wicked desires and other faults. ‘He accumulates’ means he increases. ‘A fault’ (`kaliṃ`) means an offense. ‘This is a fault’ means this is an offense. ‘In dice’ means in games of dice. ‘With all, and with oneself’ means with all of one's own wealth and also with oneself. ‘Regarding the Well-Gone Ones’ means regarding the Buddhas and others, who are called ‘Well-Gone’ because of their excellent going, because of having gone to a beautiful place, because of having gone rightly, and because of speaking rightly. ‘Should corrupt the mind’ means: for whoever should corrupt the mind, this very corruption of mind is a greater fault; thus it is said. Why? Because it is said, “for a hundred thousand… evil.” Therein, ‘a hundred thousand’ means one hundred thousand by the nirabbuda reckoning. ‘Thirty-six’ means another thirty-six nirabbudas. ‘And five’ means five abbudas by the abbuda reckoning. Therefore, by the reckoning of years, such is the length of time for which one who, having directed speech that reviles the noble ones and a malicious mind, goes to a wretched hell and is tormented there; thus it is said. And this, in brief, is the measure of the lifespan in the Paduma hell; in detail, however, it will come later.

Lobhaguṇeti “guṇo”ti bālehi diṭṭhattā, anekakkhattuṃ pavattitattā ca lobhoyeva lobhaguṇo, tasmiṃ lobhaguṇe, taṇhāyāti attho. Anuyuttoti anu anu yutto. Avadaññūti avacanaññū, buddhānampi ovādassa aggahaṇato. Maccharīti pañcavidhamacchariyena maccharī. Pesuṇiyaṃ anuyuttoti pesuṇiyasmiṃ anuyutto aggasāvakānaṃ bhedanena. Kokālikañhi mīyamānaṃ ovadantena āyasmatā mahāmoggallānena bhāsitā imā gāthāti. Mukhaduggāti mukhavisama. Vibhūtāti vigatabhūta alikavādi. Anariyāti asappurisa. Bhūnahūti bhūtihanaka attano buddhivināsaka. Purisantāti purisādhama. Kalīti alakkhipurisa. Avajātakaputtāti buddhassa bhagavato avajātaputta. Mā bahubhāṇidha nerayikosīti idāni bahubhāṇī mā hohi, nerayiko asi jāto. Rajamākirasīti kilesarajaṃ attani pakkhipasi. Santeti samitakilese khīṇāsave. Kibbisakārīti pāpakāri. Papatanti narakaṃ.

Regarding ‘the quality of greed’: ‘quality’ (`guṇa`) is so called because it is seen by fools and because it arises many times—thus greed itself is the ‘quality of greed’; in that quality of greed, that is, in craving, is the meaning. ‘Devoted’ means repeatedly attached. ‘Unreceptive to advice’ means not knowing the spoken advice, due to not grasping the counsel even of the Buddhas. ‘Miserly’ means miserly with the five kinds of miserliness. ‘Devoted to slander’ means devoted to slander by causing division among the chief disciples. For these verses were spoken by the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna while admonishing Kokālika as he was dying. ‘Foul-mouthed’ means with a distorted mouth. ‘Untruthful’ means devoid of truth, a speaker of falsehood. ‘Ignoble’ means not a good person. ‘A destroyer of welfare’ means a destroyer of welfare, a destroyer of one's own growth. ‘A base man’ means the lowest of men. ‘A wretch’ means an inauspicious person. ‘A degenerate son’ means a degenerate son of the Buddha, the Blessed One. ‘Do not be talkative here, you are hell-bound’ means: now do not be talkative; you have become one destined for hell. ‘You are scattering dust’ means you are casting the dust of defilements upon yourself. ‘Regarding the peaceful ones’ means regarding those with stilled defilements, the Arahants. ‘An evildoer’ means one who does evil. ‘They fall’ means into hell.

Idaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyanti idaṃ taṇhādīnaṃ sabhāvabhedato avatthābhedato ca anekabhedakaṃ dassetuṃ anekehi suttapadehi udāharaṇavasena dassitaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ suttanti veditabbaṃ.

‘This pertains to defilement’ means: it should be understood that this sutta—which is presented by way of example through many sutta passages in order to show the manifold nature of craving and other defilements according to the distinctions of their intrinsic nature and the distinctions of their states—is the Sutta Pertaining to Defilement.

Pasannenāti [V 0.0346] kammakammaphalādīni saddahantena.

‘With a clear mind’ means by one who has faith in kamma, the fruit of kamma, and so forth.

93. Iddhanti hatthūpagasīsūpagādialaṅkārehi maṇikanakādīhi ca samiddhaṃ. Phītanti telamadhuphāṇitādīhi ca dhanadhaññādīhi ca vipulaṃ. Ākiṇṇamanussanti nirantaramanussaṃ. Sambādhabyūhanti byūhā vuccanti anibbiddharacchāyo. Yesu paviṭṭhamaggeneva niggacchanti, te sambādhā byūhakā etthāti sambādhabyūhaṃ. Imināpi tassa nagarassa ghanavāsameva dīpeti. Bhantenāti damathaṃ anupagatena, ito cito ca paribbhamantena vā. Apāpakanti alāmakaṃ. Aveccappasādenāti acalappasādena, saccappaṭivedhato āgatena pasādena.

93. ‘Prosperous’ means endowed with ornaments such as hand ornaments and head ornaments, and with gems, gold, and so on. ‘Flourishing’ means abundant with oil, honey, molasses, and so on, and with wealth, grain, and so on. ‘Thronged with people’ means with an uninterrupted stream of people. Regarding ‘with narrow approaches’: approaches are said to be roads that are not thoroughfares. Because in this city there are narrow approaches where one must exit by the same path one entered, it is called ‘with narrow approaches.’ By this, it shows that the city is densely inhabited. ‘By one who is agitated’ means by one who has not attained self-control, or by one who is wandering here and there. ‘Not base’ means not inferior. ‘With unwavering faith’ means with unshakable faith, with the faith that comes from the penetration of the truths.

Pecca [M 0.0228] so labhateti yo bhūte daṇḍena na hiṃsati, so puggalo paraloke manussabhūto manussasukhaṃ devabhūto dibbasukhaṃ ubhayaṃ atikkanto nibbānasukhaṃ labhatīti attho.

‘Departed, one obtains’ means that a person who does not harm beings with a weapon, that person, in the next world, on becoming a human, obtains human happiness; on becoming a deva, obtains divine happiness; having transcended both, obtains the happiness of Nibbāna. This is the meaning.
