A layperson who has been engaging in the ten unwholesome courses of action since birth, or a monastic who commits a grave offense from the day of ordination, is called “utterly immoral.” Here, however, this is said with reference to the state of immorality that has come about through the karmic destination of one who is immoral in two or three existences. And here, by “the state of immorality,” the craving that arises dependent on the six doors of an immoral person should be understood. “As a māluvā creeper does to a sāl tree”: this refers to the immorality, identified as craving, in a person. Just as a māluvā creeper, when it rains, catches the water with its leaves and completely envelops a sāl tree that is bent down, breaking it apart, so this craving envelops one’s own being which is bent down towards the lower realms. Like a tree broken by the māluvā creeper and felled to the ground, so that person, being broken by that craving identified as immorality, is cast down into the planes of misery. The meaning is that one does to oneself just what an enemy wishing one harm would desire.

“Attanā hi kata”nti gāthāya ayaṃ saṅkhepattho – yathā pāsāṇamayaṃ pāsāṇasambhavaṃ vajiraṃ tameva asmamayaṃ maṇiṃ attano uṭṭhānaṭṭhānasaṅkhātaṃ pāsāṇamaṇiṃ khāyitvā chiddāchiddaṃ khaṇḍākhaṇḍaṃ katvā aparibhogaṃ karoti, evamevaṃ attanā kataṃ attani jātaṃ attasambhavaṃ pāpaṃ dummedhaṃ nippaññaṃ puggalaṃ catūsu apāyesu abhimatthati kantati viddhaṃsetīti.

“By oneself is evil done”: this is the summarized meaning of the verse. Just as a diamond, made of stone and originating from stone, consumes that very gem made of rock—the stone-gem which is its own place of origin—making it full of holes and fragments and rendering it unusable, so too, evil done by oneself, born of oneself, originating from oneself, crushes, cuts, and destroys the foolish, unwise person in the four planes of misery.

Niseviyāti katvā. Garahāti gārayhā. Bālamatīti mandabuddhino. Khayā ca kammassāti kammakkhayakarañāṇena kammassa khepanato. Vimuttacetasoti samucchedavimuttiyā paṭippassaddhivimuttiyā ca vimuttacitto. Nibbanti te jotirivindhanakkhayāti yathā nāma anupādāno jātavedo nibbāyati, evamevaṃ abhisaṅkhārassa viññāṇassa anavasesakkhayā nibbāyati.

“Having frequented”: having done. “Blame”: what is blameworthy. “Of foolish mind”: of dull intellect. “And by the destruction of kamma”: due to the elimination of kamma by means of the knowledge that destroys kamma. “With liberated mind”: with a mind liberated by the liberation through cutting off and the liberation through tranquillization. “They are extinguished like a flame when its fuel is consumed”: just as a fire without fuel is extinguished, so too one is extinguished through the destruction without remainder of consciousness conditioned by volitional formations.

123. “Yathāpi bhamaro”ti gāthāyaṃ bhamaroti yā kāci madhukarajāti. Pupphanti pupphārāme caranto pupphañca tassa vaṇṇañca gandhañca aheṭhayaṃ aheṭhayanto avināsento caratīti attho. Evaṃ caritvā ca paleti rasamādāyāti yāvadatthaṃ rasaṃ pivitvā aparampi madhukaraṇatthāya rasaṃ gahetvā ḍeti. So ekaṃ vanagahanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā rukkhasusirādīsu taṃ rajamissakaṃ rasaṃ ṭhapetvā anupubbena madhurarasaṃ madhuṃ karoti, na tassa pupphārāme caritapaccayā pupphaṃ vā tassa vaṇṇo vā gandho vā vinassati, atha kho pupphaṃ pākatikameva hoti. Evaṃ gāme munī careti evaṃ [V 0.0378] sekkho asekkho vā anagāriyamuni kulapaṭipāṭiyā gāme bhikkhaṃ gaṇhanto careyyāti attho. Na hi tassa gāme caraṇapaccayā saddhāhāni vā bhogahāni vā hoti, saddhāpi bhogāpi pākatikāva honti. Evaṃ caritvā ca pana gāmato nikkhamitvā bahigāme udakaphāsukaṭṭhāne saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā nisinno akkhabhañjana- (mi. pa. 6.1.2) vaṇalepanaputtamaṃsūpamavasena (mi. pa. 6.1.2; saṃ. ni. 2.63) paccavekkhanto [M 0.0263] piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathārūpaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ anupavisitvā ajjhattikakammaṭṭhānaṃ sammasanto maggaphalāni hatthagatāneva karoti. Asekkhamuni pana diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāramanuyuñjati. Ayamassa bhamarena madhukarena sarikkhatā. Khīṇāsavo panettha adhippetoti.

123. In the verse beginning, “Just as a bee”: “bee” refers to any kind of honey-making creature. Wandering in a flower garden, it forages without harming the flower, its color, or its fragrance; this is the meaning. And having foraged thus, “it departs taking the nectar”: having drunk its fill of nectar and taken more nectar for making honey, it flies away. Having entered a forest thicket, it deposits that pollen-mixed nectar in a tree hollow or the like and gradually makes it into sweet honey. Because of its wandering in the flower garden, the flower, its color, and its fragrance are not destroyed; on the contrary, the flower remains just as it was. “So should a sage wander in the village”: the meaning is that a homeless sage, whether a trainee or one beyond training, should wander for alms in the village, going from family to family in sequence. For because of his wandering in the village, there is no loss of faith or loss of wealth; both faith and wealth remain as they were. And having wandered thus, after leaving the village, he sits down in a secluded place with access to water, spreads out his outer robe, and consumes his almsfood, reflecting on it by way of the similes of greasing an axle, plastering a wound, and his son’s flesh. Then, having entered a suitable forest grove and contemplating his internal meditation subject, he brings the path and its fruit to his fingertips. A sage beyond training, for his part, devotes himself to the blissful dwelling in this very life. This is his similarity to the honey-making bee. Here, one whose taints are destroyed is intended.

Pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharatīti yo naṃ pāti rakkhati, taṃ mokkheti moceti āpāyikādīhi dukkhehīti pātimokkho. So eva kāyikavācasikassa vītikkamassa saṃvaraṇato pidahanato saṃvaro. Tena pātimokkhasaṃvarena saṃvuto samannāgato hutvā sabbiriyāpathesu carati. Ācāragocarasampannoti ācārena ca gocarena ca sampanno. Aṇumattesūti appamattakesu. Vajjesūti akusaladhammesu. Bhayadassāvīti bhayaṃ dassī. Samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesūti sikkhāpadesu yaṃ kiñci sikkhitabbaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ sammā ādiyitvā sikkhati.

“He dwells restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha”: The Pātimokkha is so called because it protects (pāti) one who guards it and frees (mokkheti), releases, one from the sufferings of the planes of misery and so on. That itself is “restraint” (saṃvara) because it restrains (saṃvaraṇato) and prevents (pidahanato) bodily and verbal transgression. Being endowed with that restraint of the Pātimokkha, he comports himself in all the postures. “Perfect in conduct and resort”: endowed with right conduct and a proper resort. “In the slightest”: in small ones. “Faults”: in unwholesome states. “Seeing danger”: one who sees danger. “He trains by undertaking the training rules”: whatever should be trained in among the training rules, he undertakes it all properly and trains in it.

Kāyakammavacīkammena samannāgato, kusalena parisuddhājīvoti ettha ācāragocaraggahaṇeneva kusale kāyakamme vacīkamme ca gahitepi yasmā idaṃ ājīvapārisuddhisīlaṃ na ākāsādīsu uppajjati, kāyavacīdvāresu eva pana uppajjati, tasmā tassa uppattidvāradassanatthaṃ “kāyavacīkammena samannāgato, kusalenā”ti vuttaṃ. Yasmā pana tena samannāgato, tasmā parisuddhājīvo, ājīvapārisuddhipi sīlamevāti dassanatthaṃ etaṃ vuttaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ – “katame ca thapati kusalā sīlā? Kusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ kusalaṃ vacīkammaṃ, parisuddhaṃ ājīvampi kho ahaṃ thapati sīlasmiṃ vadāmī”ti (ma. ni. 2.265). Āraddhavīriyoti yassa kāyikaṃ cetasikañca vīriyaṃ āraddhaṃ hoti, so “āraddhavīriyo”ti vuccati. Tattha yo gaṇasaṅgaṇikaṃ vinodetvā catūsu iriyāpathesu aṭṭhaārambhavatthuvasena ekako hoti, tassa kāyikaṃ vīriyaṃ āraddhaṃ nāma hoti. Yo cittasaṅgaṇikaṃ vinodetvā aṭṭhasamāpattivasena ekako hoti, gamanādīsu uppannakilesaṃ uppannaṭṭhāneyeva niggaṇhitvā jhānaṃ nibbatteti, tassa cetasikaṃ vīriyaṃ āraddhaṃ nāma hoti. Evaṃ āraddhavīriyo. Thāmavāti ṭhitimā. Daḷhaparakkamoti [V 0.0379] thiraparakkamo. Anikkhittadhuro…pe… sacchikiriyāyāti saṃkilesadhammānaṃ pahānatthaṃ vodānadhammānaṃ sampādanatthaṃ[M 0.0264], paccakkhakaraṇatthañca dhuraṃ anikkhipitvā vīriyaṃ ussukkāpento viharati. Paññavāti pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ udayabbayapariggāhikāya paññāya samannāgato. Tenāha “udayatthagāminiyā”ti.

“Endowed with wholesome bodily and verbal action, with a purified livelihood”: Here, although wholesome bodily action and verbal action are included by the taking of the words ‘conduct’ and ‘resort,’ because this virtue of purity of livelihood does not arise in space and so on, but indeed arises only at the doors of body and speech, therefore, to show its doors of arising, it is said, “endowed with wholesome bodily and verbal action.” And to show that because one is endowed with this, one therefore has a purified livelihood, and that purity of livelihood is itself virtue, this was said. For it has been said: ‘And what, householder, are wholesome virtues? Wholesome bodily action, wholesome verbal action; I say, householder, that purified livelihood is also included in virtue.’ “Of aroused energy”: one whose bodily and mental energy is aroused is called ‘one of aroused energy.’ Herein, one who has dispelled delight in company and is solitary in the four postures by way of the eight grounds for arousing energy—his bodily energy is said to be aroused. One who has dispelled delight in mental association (i.e., craving) and is solitary by way of the eight attainments, and who, having suppressed a defilement that has arisen during walking, etc., right where it arose, generates jhāna—his mental energy is said to be aroused. Thus, one is of aroused energy. “Stalwart”: steadfast. “Of firm exertion”: of firm striving. “Not laying down the burden … for the sake of realization”: he dwells striving with energy, not having laid down the burden for the sake of abandoning defiling states, for the sake of accomplishing cleansing states, and for the sake of direct realization. “Wise”: endowed with the wisdom that comprehends the rise and fall of the five aggregates. Hence it is said: “leading to rise and fall.”

Natthi puttasamaṃ pemanti mātāpitaro virūpepi attano puttake suvaṇṇabimbakaṃ viya maññanti mālāguḷe viya sīsādīsu katvā pariharamānā. Tehi uhaditāpi omuttitāpi gandhavilepanaṃ paṭicchantā viya somanassaṃ āpajjanti. Tenāha – “natthi puttasamaṃ pema”nti. Puttapemena samaṃ pemaṃ nāma natthīti vuttaṃ hoti. Gosamitanti gohi samaṃ godhanasadisaṃ aññaṃ dhanaṃ nāma natthi. Sūriyasamā ābhāti sūriyābhāya samā aññā ābhā nāma natthi. Samuddaparamāti ye keci aññe sarā nāma, sabbe te samuddaparamā. Samuddo tesaṃ uttamo, samuddasadisaṃ aññaṃ udakaṃ nidānaṃ nāma natthi bhagavāti vadati.

“There is no love equal to that for a child”: even if their own child is ugly, parents regard them as a golden image, carrying them on their heads and so on as if they were a garland-ball. Even when defecated and urinated upon by them, they experience gladness as if they were receiving fragrant ointment. Hence it is said: “There is no love equal to that for a child.” This means that there is no love equal to the love for a child. “Wealth equal to cattle”: there is no other wealth equal to cattle, similar to the wealth of cattle. “Radiance equal to the sun”: there is no other radiance equal to the sun’s radiance. “The ocean is supreme”: whatever other rivers there are, they all have the ocean as supreme. The ocean is their highest; there is no other source of water similar to the ocean, he says to the Blessed One.

Yasmā pana attapemena samaṃ pemaṃ natthi. Mātāpitaro hi chaḍḍetvāpi puttadhītaro aposetvā attānameva posenti. Dhaññena ca samaṃ dhanaṃ nāma natthi. Tathārūpe hi kāle hiraññasuvaṇṇādīnipi gomahiṃsādīnipi dhaññaggahaṇatthaṃ dhaññasāmikānameva santikaṃ gahetvā gacchanti. Paññāya ca samā ābhā nāma natthi. Sūriyādayo hi ekadesaṃyeva obhāsenti, paccuppannameva ca tamaṃ vinodenti, paññā pana dasasahassimpi lokadhātuṃ ekapajjotaṃ kātuṃ sakkoti, atītaṃsādipaṭicchādakañca tamaṃ vidhamati. Meghavuṭṭhiyā ca samo saro nāma natthi. Nadī vā hi hotu taḷākādīni vā, vuṭṭhisamo saro nāma natthi. Meghavuṭṭhiyā hi pacchinnāya mahāsamudde aṅgulipabbatemanamattampi udakaṃ na hoti, vuṭṭhiyā pana pavattamānāya yāva ābhassarabhavanāpi ekodakaṃ hoti. Tasmā bhagavā devatāvacanaṃ paṭikkhipanavasena paṭigāthaṃ vadanto “natthi attasamaṃ pema”ntiādimāha.

For there is no love equal to love of self. For parents, not nourishing their sons and daughters, or even abandoning them, nourish only themselves. And there is no wealth equal to grain. For at such a time, people take even gold and silver, cattle and buffalo, to the owners of grain in order to obtain grain. And there is no radiance equal to wisdom. For the sun and other luminaries illuminate only one region and dispel only the present darkness, but wisdom is able to make even a ten-thousandfold world-system into a single blaze, and it shatters the darkness of ignorance that conceals the past and so on. And there is no river equal to rain from a cloud. For whether it be rivers or lakes and so on, there is no river equal to rainfall. For when the rain from the clouds has ceased, in the great ocean the water does not rise even by a finger-joint's measure, but when the rain is falling, it becomes a single mass of water up to the Ābhassara Brahma-world. Therefore, the Blessed One, rejecting the devatā’s statement, uttered a verse in reply, saying: “There is no love equal to love of self,” and so on.

124. Kiṃsūdha bhītāti kiṃ nu bhītā. Maggo canekāyatano pavuttoti aṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇavasena anekehi kāraṇehi maggo kathito, evaṃ sante kissa bhītā hutvā ayaṃ janatā dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhiyo aggahesīti vadati. Bhūripaññāti bahupañña ussannapañña. Paralokaṃ na bhāyeti imasmā lokā paralokaṃ gacchanto na bhāyeyya.

124. “Why is one afraid here?” means: Why, indeed, are they afraid? “The path has been spoken of as having many grounds” means: the path is taught for many reasons, by way of the thirty-eight meditation objects; this being so, why has this generation, having become afraid, grasped the sixty-two views? he says. “Of extensive wisdom” means: of great wisdom, of abundant wisdom. “One does not fear the next world” means: one who goes from this world to the next world would not fear.

Paṇidhāyāti [V 0.0380][M 0.0265] ṭhapetvā. Gharamāvasantoti anāthapiṇḍikādayo viya bahvannapāne ghare vasanto. Saṃvibhāgīti accharāya gahitampi nakhena phāletvā parassa datvāva bhuñjanasīlo. Vadaññūti yācakānaṃ yācanavasena vuttavacanaññū, vacanīyo vā. Ettha ca vācanti cattāri vacīsucaritāni gahitāni. Mananti tīṇi manosucaritāni. Kāyenāti tīṇi kāyasucaritāni. Ime dasa kusalakammapathā pubbasuddhiaṅgaṃ nāma. “Bahvannapānaṃ gharamāvasanto”ti iminā yaññaupakkharo gahito. Saddhoti ekaṃ aṅgaṃ, mudūti ekaṃ, saṃvibhāgīti ekaṃ, vadaññūti ekanti imāni cattāri aṅgāni sandhāya “etesu dhammesu ṭhito catūsū”ti āha.

“Having directed” means: having established. “Dwelling in a house” means: dwelling in a house with abundant food and drink like Anāthapiṇḍika and others. “A sharer” means: one who has the habit of eating only after having given to another, splitting even a morsel taken with a finger-snap with his fingernail. “Generous” means: one who understands the words spoken by supplicants in accordance with their request, or one who is approachable. And here, by the word “speech,” the four kinds of good verbal conduct are taken. By the word “mind,” the three kinds of good mental conduct are taken. By the word “body,” the three kinds of good bodily conduct are taken. These ten wholesome courses of action are called the factor of preliminary purity. By “dwelling in a house with abundant food and drink,” the requisites for an offering are taken. “Faithful” is one factor, “gentle” is one, “a sharer” is one, and “generous” is one—thus, referring to these four factors, he said, “established in these four qualities.”

Aparo nayo – “vāca”ntiādīni tīṇi aṅgāni, “bahvannapāna”nti iminā yaññaupakkharova gahito, “saddho mudu saṃvibhāgī vadaññū”ti ekaṃ aṅgaṃ.

Another method: The three beginning with “speech” are three factors; by “abundant food and drink,” only the requisites for an offering are taken; “faithful, gentle, a sharer, generous” is one factor.

Aparo dukanayo nāma hoti – “vācaṃ manañcā”ti ekaṃ aṅgaṃ, “kāyena pāpāni akubbamāno bahvannapānaṃ gharamāvasanto”ti ekaṃ, “saddho mudū”ti ekaṃ, “saṃvibhāgī vadaññū”ti ekanti etesu catūsu dhammesu ṭhito dhamme ṭhito nāma hoti. So ito paralokaṃ gacchantona bhāyati.

There is another method by pairs: “speech and mind” is one factor; “not doing evil with the body and dwelling in a house with abundant food and drink” is one; “faithful and gentle” is one; and “a sharer and generous” is one. One established in these four qualities is called one established in the Dhamma. Such a one does not fear when going from here to the next world.

Kāyasamācārampītiādi pātimokkhasaṃvaradassanaṃ. Tattha duvidhenāti dvividhena, dvīhi koṭṭhāsehīti attho. Jaññāti jāneyya. Sīlakathā ca nāmesā kammapathavasena vā paṇṇattivasena vā kathetabbā. Tattha kammapathavasena tāva kathentena asevitabbakāyasamācāro pāṇātipātādinnādānamicchācārehi kathetabbo. Paṇṇattivasena kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadavītikkamavasena. Sevitabbakāyasamācāro pāṇātipātādiveramaṇīhi ceva kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadaavītikkamena ca kathetabbo.

“Bodily conduct,” etc.: this indicates the Pātimokkha restraint. Herein, “of two kinds” means: in two ways, that is, in two parts. “One should know” means: one should understand. This talk on virtue should be given either by way of the courses of action or by way of the prescribed rules. Therein, when explaining by way of the courses of action, bodily conduct that should not be practiced should be explained by way of the taking of life, the taking of what is not given, and sexual misconduct. By way of the prescribed rules, it is through the transgression of the training rules prescribed at the bodily door. Bodily conduct that should be practiced should be explained as both abstention from taking life, etc., and as not transgressing the training rules prescribed at the bodily door.

Asevitabbavacīsamācāro musāvādādivacīduccaritena ceva vacīdvāre paññattasikkhāpadavītikkamena ca kathetabbo. Sevitabbavacīsamācāro musāvādādiveramaṇīhi ceva vacīdvāre paññattasikkhāpadaavītikkamena ca kathetabbo.

Verbal conduct that should not be practiced should be explained as both verbal misconduct such as false speech, etc., and as transgressing the training rules prescribed at the verbal door. Verbal conduct that should be practiced should be explained as both abstention from false speech, etc., and as not transgressing the training rules prescribed at the verbal door.

Pariyesanā [M 0.0266] pana kāyavācāhi pariyesanā eva, sā kāyavacīsamācāraggahaṇena gahitāpi yasmā ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ nāma etasmiṃyeva dvāradvaye uppajjati, na ākāse, tasmā [V 0.0381] ājīvaṭṭhamakasīladassanatthaṃ visuṃ vuttā. Tattha nasevitabbapariyesanā anariyapariyesanāya kathetabbā, sevitabbapariyesanā ariyapariyesanāya. Vuttañhetaṃ – “katamā ca, bhikkhave, anariyapariyesanā? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesatī”tiādi (ma. ni. 1.274). Tathā “katamā ca, bhikkhave, ariyapariyesanā? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajātaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesatī”tiādi (ma. ni. 1.275).

The search, however, is a search by means of body and speech. Though it is included by taking up bodily and verbal conduct, because the virtue with right livelihood as the eighth factor arises only in this pair of doors, not in the sky, it is stated separately to show the virtue with right livelihood as the eighth factor. Herein, the search that should not be practiced should be explained as the ignoble search, and the search that should be practiced as the noble search. For it is said: “And what, bhikkhus, is the ignoble search? Here, bhikkhus, someone who is himself subject to birth seeks what is also subject to birth,” and so on. Likewise: “And what, bhikkhus, is the noble search? Here, bhikkhus, someone who is himself subject to birth, having understood the danger in what is subject to birth, seeks the unborn, unsurpassed security from bondage, Nibbāna,” and so on.

170. Maggānaṭṭhaṅgikoti jaṅghamaggādayo vā hontu dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhigatamaggā vā, sabbesampi maggānaṃ sammādiṭṭhiādīhi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi micchādiṭṭhiādīnaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ pāpadhammānaṃ pahānakaro nirodhaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā catūsupi saccesu dukkhaparijānanādikiccaṃ sādhayamāno aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo seṭṭho uttamo. Saccānaṃ caturo padāti “saccaṃ bhaṇe na kujjheyyā”ti (dha. pa. 224) āgataṃ vacīsaccaṃ vā hotu, “sacco brāhmaṇo, sacco khattiyo”tiādibhedaṃ sammutisaccaṃ vā, “idameva saccaṃ moghamañña”nti (ma. ni. 3.331; udā. 54; mahāni. 20) diṭṭhisaccaṃ vā, “ekañhi saccaṃ na dutiyamatthī”ti (su. ni. 890; mahāni. 119) vuttaṃ paramatthasaccaṃ vā hotu. Sabbesampi imesaṃ saccānaṃ parijānitabbaṭṭhena pahātabbaṭṭhena sacchikātabbaṭṭhena bhāvetabbaṭṭhena ekapaṭivedhaṭṭhena tathapaṭivedhaṭṭhena ca “dukkhaṃ ariyasacca”ntiādayo (mahāva. 14; dī. ni. 2.387; ma. ni. 1.120) caturo padā seṭṭhā nāma. Virāgo seṭṭho dhammānanti “yāvatā, bhikkhave, dhammā saṅkhatā vā asaṅkhatā vā, virāgo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyatī”ti (a. ni. 4.34; 5.32; itivu. 90) vacanato nibbānasaṅkhāto virāgo sabbadhammānaṃ seṭṭho. Dvipadānañca cakkhumāti sabbesampi devamanussādibhedānaṃ dvipadānaṃ pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumā bhagavāva seṭṭhoti.

170. “The eightfold is the best of paths”: whether they be paths such as footpaths, or the paths comprised in the sixty-two views, of all paths the eightfold path is the best, the highest. It is the eightfold path which, with its eight factors beginning with right view, destroys the eight evil states beginning with wrong view; which, by taking cessation as its object, accomplishes the functions of fully understanding suffering and so on in regard to the four truths. “The four statements are the best of truths”: whether it be the verbal truth that comes in the passage, “One should speak the truth, not get angry”; or conventional truth, with its divisions such as “a true brahmin, a true khattiya”; or truth as a view, as in “This alone is true, anything else is false”; or the ultimate truth spoken of thus, “Truth is one, there is no second.” Of all these truths, the four statements beginning, “This is the noble truth of suffering” are the best, in the sense of having to be fully understood, abandoned, realized, and developed, and in the sense of being penetrated simultaneously and being penetrated as they are. “Dispassion is the best of states”: in accordance with the text, “Bhikkhus, whatever states there are, conditioned or unconditioned, dispassion is declared the chief among them,” dispassion, which is a designation for Nibbāna, is the best of all states. “And the one with vision is the best of two-footed beings”: of all two-footed beings, with their divisions into devas, humans, and so on, the Blessed One, who is endowed with the five kinds of vision, is the very best.

Aggānīti uttamāni. Yāvatāti yattakā. Apadāti nippadā ahimacchādayo. Dvipadāti manussapakkhijātādayo. Catuppadāti hatthiassādayo[M 0.0267]. Bahuppadāti satapadiādayo. Rūpinoti kāmāvacararūpāvacarasattā. Asaññinoti asaññībhave nibbattasattā. Nevasaññīnāsaññinoti bhavagge nibbattasattā. Aggamakkhāyatīti guṇehi aggo uttamo seṭṭho akkhāyati.

“Chief” means: supreme. “Whatever” means: as many as. “Footless” means: without feet, such as snakes and fish. “Two-footed” means: humans, birds, and so on. “Four-footed” means: elephants, horses, and so on. “Many-footed” means: centipedes and so on. “Having form” means: beings of the sense-sphere and form-sphere realms. “Non-percipient” means: beings reborn in the non-percipient state of existence. “Neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient” means: beings reborn at the peak of existence. “Is declared the chief” means: is declared chief, supreme, and best on account of its qualities.

Asaṅkhatānanti nibbānameva vuttaṃ. Virāgotiādīni ca nibbānasseva nāmāni. Tañhi āgamma sabbe kilesā virajjanti, sabbe rāgamadādayo madā nimmadā honti abhāvaṃ gacchanti[V 0.0382], sabbā pipāsā vinayaṃ upenti, sabbe ālayā samugghātaṃ gacchanti, vaṭṭāni upacchijjanti, taṇhā khīyati, sabbapariḷāhā vūpasammanti, vaṭṭadukkhaṃ nirujjhati nibbāyati. Tasmā taṃ etāni nāmāni labhatīti.

“Of the unconditioned” means: Nibbāna itself is spoken of. “Dispassion” and so on are names for Nibbāna itself. For by resorting to it, all defilements fade away; all intoxications such as lust are quelled and disappear; all thirst is subdued; all attachments are eradicated; the rounds of existence are cut off; craving is destroyed; all fevers are allayed; and the suffering of the round ceases and is extinguished. Therefore it receives these names.

Dhammo ca kusalakkhatoti tassa satthuno dhammo ca kusalo anavajjo, anavajjattā eva paṭipakkhehi rāgādīhi kilesehi sabbatitthiyavādehi ca aparikkhato. Tāni tīṇi visissareti etāni tīṇi ratanāni loke sabbaratanehi visissanti guṇavasena sabbalokaṃ atisentīti attho.

“And the Dhamma is well-expounded”: the Dhamma of that Teacher is wholesome and blameless, and because it is blameless, it is unassailed by opposing defilements such as lust and by all sectarian doctrines. “These three are distinguished”: this means these three jewels, by virtue of their qualities, excel all other jewels in the world, surpassing the entire world. This is the meaning.

Samaṇapadumasañcayo gaṇoti padumasadisānaṃ ariyasamaṇānaṃ samūhasaṅkhāto gaṇo. Padumanti hi paripuṇṇasatapattassa saroruhassa nāmaṃ. Ariyapuggalā ca sabbathāpi paripuṇṇaguṇāti padumasadisā vuttā. Vidūnaṃ sakkatoti vidūhi paṇḍitehi sakkato. Naravaradamakoti naravaro ca purisānaṃ damako nāyako cāti attho. Lokassa uttarīti lokassa upari ṭhitāni, sabbaloke uttamānīti attho.

“The assembly of lotus-like ascetics” is the group designated as an assembly of noble ascetics resembling lotuses. For ‘paduma’ is the name of a lotus fully endowed with a hundred petals. And noble individuals are said to resemble lotuses because they are in every way fully endowed with virtues. “Honored by the wise” means honored by the wise, the learned. “The tamer of the best of men” means the best of men and the tamer, the leader of men. This is the meaning. “Superior to the world” means standing above the world, that is, supreme in all the world. This is the meaning.

Nirupadāhoti rāgapariḷāhādīhi anupadāho. Saccanāmoti avitathanāmo yathābhuccaguṇehi āgatanāmo. Sabbābhibhūti sabbalokaṃ attano guṇehi abhibhavitvā ṭhito. Saccadhammoti vaṭṭato ekantanissaraṇabhāvena avitatho saha pariyattiyā navavidhopi lokuttaradhammo, tato eva natthañño tassa uttarīti tassa uttari adhikaguṇo añño ca dhammo natthīti attho. Ariyasaṅghova niccaṃ sabbakālaṃ vidūhi sabbapaṇḍitehi pūjito.

“Without affliction”: free from the burning of afflictions such as passion. “Of true name”: a name that is not false, a name derived from his actual qualities. “All-conquering”: one who stands having overcome the entire world with his virtues. “The true Dhamma”: the ninefold supramundane Dhamma together with the scriptural teachings, which is unfailing as it is the sole escape from the round of existence. Therefore “there is nothing higher than it,” which means there is no other Dhamma with superior qualities. This is the meaning. The Noble Sangha indeed is constantly, at all times, honored by all the wise.

“Ekāyana”nti [M 0.0268] gāthāya ekāyananti ekaṃ maggaṃ. Maggassa hi –

In the verse “One way,” ‘ekāyana’ means the one path. For of the path—

“Maggo pantho patho pajjo, añjasaṃ vaṭumāyanaṃ;

Nāvā uttarasetu ca, kullo ca bhisi saṅgamo”ti. (cūḷani. pārāyanatthutigāthāniddesa 101) –

“Path, road, way, track, straight path, roadway; ship, causeway for crossing, raft, pontoon, and confluence.”

Bahūni nāmāni, svāyaṃ idha ayananāmena vutto. Tasmā ekāyananti ekamaggaṃ, na dvedhāpathabhūtanti attho. Atha vā ekena ayitabbanti ekāyanaṃ. Gaṇasaṅgaṇikaṃ pahāya vivekaṭṭhena [V 0.0383] pavivittena paṭipajjitabbanti attho. Ayanti vā etenāti ayano, saṃsārato nibbānaṃ gacchantīti attho. Ekassa vā sabbasattaseṭṭhassa bhagavato ayanoti ekāyano. Kiñcāpi hi tena aññepi ayanti, tathāpi bhagavatova so ayano, tena uppāditattā. Yathāha – “so hi, brāhmaṇa, bhagavā anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā”tiādi (ma. ni. 3.79). Ayatīti vā ayano, gacchati pavattatīti attho. Ekasmiṃ imasmiṃyeva dhammavinaye ayano, na aññatthāti ekāyano. Yathāha – “imasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhatī”ti (dī. ni. 2.214). Api ca pubbabhāge nānāmukhabhāvanāya pavattopi aparabhāge ekaṃ nibbānameva ayati gacchatīti ekāyano, taṃ ekāyanaṃ.

There are many names, but here it is referred to by the name ‘ayana’. Therefore, ‘ekāyana’ means the one path, not a forked road; this is the meaning. Or else, it is ‘ekāyana’ because it is to be traveled by one alone. This means that, having abandoned socializing in company, one should practice in seclusion, in solitude. This is the meaning. Or, it is an ‘ayana’ because one goes by means of it; this means they go from saṃsāra to Nibbāna. This is the meaning. Or, it is the ‘ayana’ of the One, the Blessed One, who is supreme among all beings; thus it is ‘ekāyano’. For although others also travel by it, it is still the Blessed One’s path because he is the one who produced it. As it is said: “For, brahmin, the Blessed One is the producer of the unarisen path…” and so on. Or, it is an ‘ayana’ because ‘it goes’; this means ‘it proceeds, it continues.’ This is the meaning. The ‘ayana’ is in this one Dhamma and Discipline alone, not elsewhere; thus it is ‘ekāyano’. As it is said: “In this Dhamma and Discipline, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is found.” Moreover, although in the preliminary stage it proceeds by way of various approaches to development, in the final stage it goes to the one Nibbāna alone; thus it is ‘ekāyano’. That one way.

Jātikhayantadassīti jātiyā khayasaṅkhāto anto jātikhayanto. Jātiyā accantakhayanto nibbānaṃ, taṃ passīti jātikhayantadassī. “Maggaṃ pajānāti hitānukampī”tipi pāṭho. Tassattho – vuttappakāraṃ ekāyanasaṅkhātaṃ maggaṃ sayambhuñāṇena bhagavā pajānāti, jānanto ca tena tena hitena satte anukampatīti. Idāni tassa maggassa ekāyanabhāvaṃ, tīsupi kālesu ekantaniyyānatañca vibhāvetuṃ “etena maggena tariṃsu pubbe, tarissanti ye ca taranti ogha”nti āha. Tassattho – ye atītamaddhānaṃ kāmoghādicatubbidhaṃ oghaṃ tariṃsu, ye taṃ anāgatamaddhānaṃ tarissanti, etarahi ca taranti, te sabbe eteneva maggena, na aññenāti. Visuddhipekkhāti caturoghanittharaṇena accantavisuddhiṃ nibbānaṃ apekkhantā, parinibbāyitukāmāti attho.

'Seer of the end of birth': the end of birth is the end designated as the destruction of birth. The utter destruction of birth is Nibbāna; one who sees that is a 'seer of the end of birth.' There is also the reading: 'He understands the path, compassionate for their welfare.' Its meaning is: the Blessed One, with his self-originated knowledge, understands the path designated as the one way, and knowing it, he has compassion for beings for their welfare in various ways. Now, to show that the path is a one way and that it is the sole means of deliverance in the three times, it is said: 'By this path they crossed in the past, and will cross, and are crossing the flood.' Its meaning is: those who in the past crossed the fourfold flood beginning with the flood of sensual pleasures, those who will cross it in the future, and those who are crossing it now—all crossed, will cross, and are crossing by this very path, not by another. 'Aspiring for purity' means aspiring for the ultimate purity, Nibbāna, by crossing over the four floods; that is, they are desirous of attaining final Nibbāna.

Evaṃ [M 0.0269] duvidhampi sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ nānāsuttapadāni udāharantena vibhajitvā idāni saṃkilesabhāgiyādīhi saṃsanditvā dassetuṃ puna “lokiyaṃ sutta”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha dassanabhāgiyena ca bhāvanābhāgiyena cāti nibbedhabhāgiyena. Nibbedhabhāgiyameva hi dassanabhāgiyaṃ bhāvanābhāgiyanti dvidhā bhinditvā dassitaṃ. Lokiyañca lokuttarañcāti lokiyaṃ lokuttarañca suttaṃ, saṃkilesabhāgiyādīhi dassanabhāgiyādīhi cāti ubhayehi niddisitabbanti adhippāyo. Yasmiṃ suttetiādi niddisanākāradassanaṃ. Tattha saṃkilesabhāgiyanti saṃkilesakoṭṭhāsasahitaṃ, saṃkilesatthadīpananti attho. Esa nayo sesesupi.

Having thus analyzed the twofold foundation of the teaching by citing various sutta passages, now, in order to show it by correlating it with the part pertaining to defilement and so on, the section beginning 'the worldly sutta' is taken up again. Therein, 'by the part pertaining to vision and by the part pertaining to development' means by the part pertaining to penetration. For it is the part pertaining to penetration itself that is shown divided in two as the part pertaining to vision and the part pertaining to development. 'The worldly and the supramundane': the intention is that both the worldly sutta and the supramundane sutta are to be indicated by both sets of terms, i.e., 'the part pertaining to defilement, etc.' and 'the part pertaining to vision, etc.' The phrase 'in which sutta, etc.' shows the manner of indication. Therein, 'pertaining to defilement' means connected with the portion of defilement; that is, illuminating the meaning of defilement. This method applies to the rest as well.

Evaṃ lokiyattikassa saṃkilesabhāgiyādīhi catūhi padehi saṃsandanaṃ dassetvā iminā nayena sesatikānaṃ sesapadānañca saṃsandanaṃ suviññeyyanti taṃ anuddharitvā saṃkilesabhāgiyādīnaṃ [V 0.0384] samatikkamanaṃ dassetuṃ “vāsanābhāgiyaṃ sutta”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yadipi saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ, vāsanābhāgiyañca suttaṃ lokiyameva. Tathāpi lokuttarasuttāni viya lokiyasuttānaṃ vāsanābhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyassa samatikkamāya hotīti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “vāsanābhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyassa suttassa nigghātāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha nigghātāyāti pahānāya. Suttasīsena cettha suttattho gahitoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yasmā ca vodānadhammā viya saṃkilesadhammānaṃ dassanabhūmisamatikkamaneneva bhāvanābhūmi adhigantabbā, tasmā “bhāvanābhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ dassanabhāgiyassa suttassa paṭinissaggāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Yasmā pana asekkhadhammesu uppannesu maggabhāvanākiccaṃ nāma natthi. Jhānabhāvanāpi diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāratthā eva hoti, tasmā “asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ bhāvanābhāgiyassa suttassa paṭinissaggāya, asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārattha”nti ca vuttaṃ.

Having thus shown the correlation of the worldly triad with the four terms beginning with 'pertaining to defilement,' and since the correlation of the remaining triads and terms can be easily understood by this method, without citing that, in order to show the transcending of what pertains to defilement and so on, the passage beginning 'the sutta pertaining to latent dispositions' was stated. Therein, although the sutta pertaining to defilement and the sutta pertaining to latent dispositions are indeed worldly, nevertheless, just as the supramundane suttas serve to transcend the worldly suttas, so the sutta pertaining to latent dispositions serves to transcend the sutta pertaining to defilement. To show this meaning, it is said: 'The sutta pertaining to latent dispositions is for the destruction of the sutta pertaining to defilement.' Therein, 'for the destruction' means for the abandonment. It should be understood that here the meaning of the sutta is taken by its heading. And because, just as states of purification are attained by transcending states of defilement, the stage of development is to be attained only by transcending the stage of vision, therefore it is said: 'The sutta pertaining to development is for the relinquishment of the sutta pertaining to vision.' Moreover, since, when the states of the non-trainee have arisen, there is no such thing as the task of path development, and the development of jhāna is only for the sake of a pleasant abiding in this very life, therefore it is said: 'The sutta pertaining to the non-trainee is for the relinquishment of the sutta pertaining to development,' and 'the sutta pertaining to the non-trainee is for the sake of a pleasant abiding in this very life.'

Idāni tikapadeheva saṃsanditvā dassetuṃ “lokuttara”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Ekabījinātiādīsu yo sotāpanno hutvā ekameva attabhāvaṃ janetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayaṃ ekabījī nāma. Yathāha –

Now, in order to show by correlating with the very terms of the triads, the passage beginning 'supramundane' was stated. Regarding 'one-seeder' and so on: a person who, having become a stream-enterer, generates just one existence and attains arahantship, this person is called a 'one-seeder.' As it is said:

“Katamo ca puggalo ekabījī? Idhekacco puggalo tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo [M 0.0270] niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo. So ekaṃyeva mānusakaṃ bhavaṃ nibbattetvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo ekabījī”ti (pu. pa. 33).

'And what kind of person is a one-seeder? Here, a certain person, with the utter destruction of the three fetters, becomes a stream-enterer, not subject to downfall, assured, bound for enlightenment. He, having brought into being only one human existence, makes an end of suffering. This person is called a one-seeder.'

Yo pana dve vā tīṇi vā kulāni sandhāvitvā saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti, ayaṃ kolaṃkolo nāma. Yathāha –

But a person who, after running on and wandering through two or three families, makes an end of suffering, is called a 'clan-to-clan returner.' As it is said:

“Katamo ca puggalo kolaṃkolo? Idhekacco puggalo tiṇṇaṃ…pe… parāyaṇo. So dve vā tīṇi vā kulāni sandhāvitvā saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo kolaṃkolo”ti (pu. pa. 32).

'And what kind of person is a clan-to-clan returner? Here, a certain person... bound for enlightenment. He, after running on and wandering through two or three families, makes an end of suffering. This person is called a clan-to-clan returner.'

Tattha kulānīti bhave. Dve vā tīṇi vāti idamettha desanāmattameva. Yāva chaṭṭhabhavā saṃsarantopi kolaṃkolo hoti eva.

Therein, 'families' means existences. 'Two or three' here is merely a manner of teaching. Even one who transmigrates for up to the sixth existence is indeed a clan-to-clan returner.

Yo [V 0.0385] pana satta bhave saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti, ayaṃ sattakkhattuparamo nāma. Yathāha –

But a person who, after transmigrating for seven existences, makes an end of suffering, is called a 'seven-times-at-most returner.' As it is said:

“Katamo ca puggalo sattakkhattuparamo? Idhekacco…pe… parāyaṇo. So sattakkhattuṃ deve ceva mānuse ca sandhāvitvā saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo sattakkhattuparamo”ti (pu. pa. 31).

'And what kind of person is a seven-times-at-most returner? Here, a certain person… bound for enlightenment. He, after running on and wandering for seven times among devas and humans, makes an end of suffering. This person is called a seven-times-at-most returner.'

Ko pana tesaṃ etaṃ pabhedaṃ niyametīti? Keci tāva “pubbahetu niyametī”ti vadanti. Keci “paṭhamamaggo”, keci “upari tayo maggā”. Keci “tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ vipassanā”ti. Tattha pubbahetu niyametīti vāde paṭhamamaggassa upanissayo kato nāma hoti. Upari tayo maggā nirupanissayā uppannāti āpajjati. Paṭhamamaggo niyametīti vāde upari tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ niratthakatā āpajjati. Upari tayo maggā niyamentīti vāde “paṭhamamagge anuppanne eva upari tayo maggā uppannā”ti āpajjati. Vipassanā niyametīti vādo pana yujjati. Sace hi upari tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ vipassanā balavatī hoti, ekabījī nāma hoti. Tato mandatarā kolaṃkolo. Tato mandatarā sattakkhattuparamoti. Ettha ca yo manussesu eva sattakkhattuṃ saṃsaritvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, yo ca [M 0.0271] devesuyeva sattakkhattuṃ saṃsaritvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, ime na idhādhippetā. Yo pana kālena devesu, kālena manussesūti vomissakanayena saṃsaritvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, so idhādhippeto. Tasmā “sattakkhattuparamo”ti idaṃ idhaṭṭhakavokiṇṇavaṭṭajjhāsayassa vasena veditabbaṃ. Vaṭṭajjhāsayo hi ādito paṭṭhāya cha devaloke sodhetvā akaniṭṭhe ṭhatvā parinibbāyissati.

Who, then, determines this distinction among them? Some, for their part, say: 'A prior cause determines it.' Some say: 'The first path.' Some say: 'The three higher paths.' Some say: 'Insight pertaining to the three paths.' In the view that a prior cause determines it, a support for the first path is indeed made, but it follows that the three higher paths arise without support. In the view that the first path determines it, the meaninglessness of the three higher paths follows. In the view that the three higher paths determine it, it follows that 'the three higher paths arise even before the first path has arisen.' But the view that insight determines it is sound. For if the insight pertaining to the three higher paths is powerful, one becomes a one-seeder; if it is weaker than that, a clan-to-clan returner; and if it is weaker still, a seven-times-at-most returner. And here, one who transmigrates for seven times only among humans and attains arahantship, and one who transmigrates for seven times only among devas and attains arahantship—these are not intended here. Rather, the one intended here is he who attains arahantship after transmigrating in a mixed way, sometimes among devas, sometimes among humans. Therefore, this term 'seven-times-at-most returner' should be understood here with reference to one whose disposition is for a mixed round of existence established in this sensual realm. For one with a disposition for the round, having from the beginning purified the six deva worlds, will be established in Akaniṭṭha and attain final Nibbāna.

Tattha yo saddhaṃ dhuraṃ katvā sotāpattimaggaṃ nibbatteti, so maggakkhaṇe saddhānusārī nāma hoti. Phalakkhaṇe pana saddhāvimutto nāma hutvā vuttanayena ekabījiādibhedo hoti. Yo pana paññaṃ dhuraṃ katvā sotāpattimaggaṃ nibbatteti, so maggakkhaṇe dhammānusārī nāma. Phalakkhaṇe pana diṭṭhippatto nāma hutvā ekabījiādibhedo hoti. Idañca aṭṭhannaṃ vimokkhānaṃ alābhino vasena vuttaṃ. Lābhī pana phalakkhaṇe kāyasakkhī nāma hoti. Tattha ye saddhāvimuttadiṭṭhippattakāyasakkhināmakā tayo sotāpannā, te ekabījiādīhi tīheva saṅgahetvā vuttaṃ – “pañcahi puggalehi niddisitabbaṃ ekabījinā…pe… dhammānusārinā”ti, evaṃ pañcahi.

Therein, one who makes faith his forerunner and generates the path of stream-entry is called a faith-follower at the moment of the path. At the moment of fruition, however, having become one liberated by faith, he is distinguished as a one-seeder and so on, in the way described. But one who makes wisdom his forerunner and generates the path of stream-entry is called a Dhamma-follower at the moment of the path. At the moment of fruition, however, having become one attained to view, he is distinguished as a one-seeder and so on. And this is stated with reference to one who has not obtained the eight liberations. But one who has obtained them is called a body-witness at the moment of fruition. Therein, the three types of stream-enterers named the one liberated by faith, the one attained to view, and the body-witness, having been included under just the three types beginning with the one-seeder, it is said: 'It should be indicated by five persons: by the one-seeder… by the Dhamma-follower'—thus by five.

Dvādasahi [V 0.0386] puggalehīti sakadāgāmimaggaṭṭho, sakadāgāmī, anāgāmimaggaṭṭho, abhedena anāgāmī, antarāparinibbāyiādayo pañca, saddhāvimuttadiṭṭhippattakāyasakkhino tayoti bhedena aṭṭhāti, evaṃ dvādasahi. Tattha hi yo avihādīsu tattha tattha āyuvemajjhaṃ appatvā parinibbāyati, ayaṃ antarāparinibbāyī. Yo pana āyuvemajjhaṃ atikkamitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayaṃ upahaccaparinibbāyī. Tathā yo avihādīsu upapanno asaṅkhārena appayogena arahattaṃ adhigacchati, ayaṃ asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. Yo pana sasaṅkhārena sappayogena arahattaṃ adhigacchati, ayaṃ sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. Uddhaṃ uparūpari brahmaloke upapattisoto etassāti uddhaṃsoto. Paṭisandhivasena akaniṭṭhe gacchatīti akaniṭṭhagāmī.

By twelve persons: the one on the path to once-returning; the once-returner; the one on the path to non-returning; the non-returner, undifferentiated; and the eight non-returners, differentiated—namely, the five beginning with the one who attains final Nibbāna in the interval, and the three: the one liberated by faith, the one attained to view, and the body-witness. Thus, twelve. Among them, one who attains final Nibbāna in the Aviha realm and others without reaching the midpoint of the lifespan is one who attains final Nibbāna in the interval. One who attains arahantship after surpassing the midpoint of the lifespan is one who attains final Nibbāna upon landing. Similarly, one who is reborn in the Aviha realm and others and attains arahantship without prompting and without exertion is one who attains final Nibbāna without prompting. One who attains arahantship with prompting and with exertion is one who attains final Nibbāna with prompting. One whose stream of rebirth proceeds upward to ever higher brahma worlds is an upward-streamer. One who goes to the Akaniṭṭha realm by way of rebirth-linking is one who goes to Akaniṭṭha.

Tattha atthi uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī atthi uddhaṃsoto na akaniṭṭhagāmī, atthi na uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī atthi na uddhaṃsoto na akaniṭṭhagāmīti. Tattha yo idha anāgāmiphalaṃ patvā avihādīsu nibbatto [M 0.0272] tattha yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā uparūpari nibbattitvā akaniṭṭhaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayaṃ uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī nāma. Yo pana avihādīsu nibbatto tattheva aparinibbāyitvā akaniṭṭhampi appatvā uparūpari brahmaloke parinibbāyati, ayaṃ uddhaṃsoto na akaniṭṭhagāmī nāma. Yo ito cavitvā akaniṭṭheyeva nibbattati, ayaṃ na uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī nāma. Yo pana avihādīsu catūsu aññatarasmiṃ nibbattitvā tattheva parinibbāyati, ayaṃ na uddhaṃsoto na akaniṭṭhagāmī nāma. Saddhāvimuttādayo vuttavibhāgāyeva.

Herein, there is one who is an upward-streamer and one who goes to Akaniṭṭha; there is one who is an upward-streamer but not one who goes to Akaniṭṭha; there is one who is not an upward-streamer but is one who goes to Akaniṭṭha; and there is one who is neither an upward-streamer nor one who goes to Akaniṭṭha. Herein, one who attains the fruit of non-returning here, is reborn in the Aviha realm or another Pure Abode, abides there for the full lifespan, and then is reborn successively higher until reaching Akaniṭṭha—this one is called an 'upward-streamer who goes to Akaniṭṭha.' But one who is reborn in the Aviha realm or another, and without attaining final Nibbāna there and without reaching Akaniṭṭha, attains final Nibbāna in a still higher brahma world—this one is called an 'upward-streamer but not one who goes to Akaniṭṭha.' One who passes away from here and is reborn directly in the Akaniṭṭha realm—this one is called 'not an upward-streamer but one who goes to Akaniṭṭha.' But one who is reborn in one of the four realms beginning with Aviha and attains final Nibbāna right there—this one is called 'neither an upward-streamer nor one who goes to Akaniṭṭha.' The one liberated by faith and the others are to be understood according to the classification already stated.

Navahi puggalehīti ettha aṭṭhannaṃ vimokkhānaṃ alābhī arahā paññāvimutto nāma. Tesaṃ pana lābhī vikkhambhanasamucchedavimokkhavasena ubhohi bhāgehi rūpakāyanāmakāyasaṅkhātato ubhato bhāgato vimuttattā ubhatobhāgavimutto nāma. Samasīsināti ettha tividho samasīsī – iriyāpathasamasīsī, rogasamasīsī, jīvitasamasīsīti.

By nine persons: Here, an arahant who has not obtained the eight liberations is called one liberated by wisdom. But one who has obtained them is called one liberated in both ways, because he is liberated from both parts—that is, from what are designated the material body and the mental body—by means of both kinds of liberation, namely, liberation by suppression and liberation by eradication. As to 'one with a level tip,' there are three kinds: one with a level tip in regard to posture, one with a level tip in regard to illness, and one with a level tip in regard to life.

Tatra yo ṭhānādīsu iriyāpathesu yeneva iriyāpathena samannāgato hutvā vipassanaṃ ārabhati, teneva iriyāpathena arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyati, ayaṃ iriyāpathasamasīsī nāma. Yo pana ekaṃ rogaṃ patvā antoroge eva vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā arahattaṃ patvā teneva rogena parinibbāyati, ayaṃ rogasamasīsī nāma. Palibodhasīsaṃ taṇhā, bandhanasīsaṃ māno, parāmāsasīsaṃ diṭṭhi, vikkhepasīsaṃ uddhaccaṃ, kilesasīsaṃ avijjā, adhimokkhasīsaṃ saddhā, paggahasīsaṃ vīriyaṃ, upaṭṭhānasīsaṃ sati, avikkhepasīsaṃ samādhi, dassanasīsaṃ paññā, pavattasīsaṃ [V 0.0387] jīvitindriyaṃ, gocarasīsaṃ vimokkho, saṅkhārasīsaṃ nirodhoti terasasu sīsesu kilesasīsaṃ avijjaṃ arahattamaggo pariyādiyati, pavattasīsaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ cuticittaṃ pariyādiyati. Tattha avijjāpariyādāyakaṃ cittaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ pariyādātuṃ na sakkoti. Jīvitindriyapariyādāyakaṃ avijjaṃ pariyādātuṃ na sakkoti. Aññaṃ avijjāpariyādāyakaṃ cittaṃ, aññaṃ jīvitindriyapariyādāyakaṃ. Yassa cetaṃ sīsadvayaṃ samaṃ pariyādānaṃ gacchati, so jīvitasamasīsī nāma.

Herein, a person who begins insight meditation while in a particular posture—standing or another—and in that very posture attains arahantship and passes away into final Nibbāna, is called 'one with an equal end in regard to posture.' A person who, having contracted a disease, establishes insight while ill, attains arahantship, and passes away into final Nibbāna from that very disease, is called 'one with an equal end in regard to illness.' The end of obstacles is craving; the end of bondage is conceit; the end of misapprehension is wrong view; the end of distraction is restlessness; the end of defilements is ignorance; the end of resolve is faith; the end of exertion is energy; the end of establishment is mindfulness; the end of non-distraction is concentration; the end of vision is wisdom; the end of occurrence is the life faculty; the end of resort is liberation; the end of formations is cessation. Among these thirteen ends, the path of arahantship brings to an end ignorance, the end of defilements; the decease-consciousness brings to an end the life faculty, the end of occurrence. Herein, the consciousness that brings ignorance to an end cannot bring the life faculty to an end. The consciousness that brings the life faculty to an end cannot bring ignorance to an end. The consciousness that brings ignorance to an end is one; the consciousness that brings the life faculty to an end is another. A person for whom this pair of ends comes to an equal end is called 'one with an equal end in regard to life.'

Kathaṃ [M 0.0273] panidaṃ samaṃ hotīti? Vārasamatāya. Yasmiñhi vāre maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, sotāpattimagge pañca paccavekkhaṇāni, sakadāgāmimagge pañca, anāgāmimagge pañca, arahattamagge cattārīti ekūnavīsatime paccavekkhaṇañāṇe patiṭṭhāya bhavaṅgaṃ otaritvā parinibbāyato imāya vārasamatāya idaṃ ubhayasīsapariyādānampi samaṃ hoti nāma. Tenāyaṃ puggalo “jīvitasamasīsī”ti vuccati, ayameva idhādhippeto. Evaṃ suññatavimuttādayo tayo saddhāvimutto paññāvimutto ubhatobhāgavimutto samasīsīti satta sāvakā arahanto, paccekabuddho, sammāsambuddhoti imehi navahi puggalehi asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ niddisitabbaṃ.

But how is this equal? By equality of the turn. For in the turn when there is emergence from the path, for one who attains final Nibbāna after descending into the life-continuum, being established in these nineteen reviewing knowledges—that is, five for the path of stream-entry, five for the path of the once-returner, five for the path of the non-returner, and four for the path of arahantship—by this equality of the turn, the ending of both ends is indeed equal. Therefore this person is called 'one with an equal end in regard to life,' and this is the one intended here. Thus, the discourse pertaining to the adept's state is to be indicated by these nine persons: the seven Arahant disciples—that is, the three liberated through emptiness, the signless, and the desireless, plus the one liberated by faith, the one liberated by wisdom, the one liberated in both ways, and the one with an equal end—and the Paccekabuddha and the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Rāgacaritoti rāgasahitaṃ caritaṃ etassāti rāgacarito. Rāgena vā carito pavattito rāgacarito, rāgajjhāsayo rāgādhikoti attho. Esa nayo sesesupi. Rāgamukhe ṭhitoti rāgapariyuṭṭhāne ṭhito, pariyuṭṭhitarāgoti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.

'One of lustful temperament' means one whose temperament is accompanied by lust. Or, it means one whose temperament is driven or impelled by lust; the meaning is one with a lustful disposition, one in whom lust is predominant. This same method applies to the other cases. 'Standing at the face of lust' means standing in the grip of the obsession of lust; the meaning is that one's lust has become obsessive. This same method applies to the other terms as well.

Vāsanābhāgiyaṃ suttanti lokiyaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānaṃ vāsanābhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ. Lokiyaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyañhi suttaṃ rāgacaritehi puggalehi niddiṭṭhaṃ. Tattha “lokiyaṃ, sattādhiṭṭhāna”nti padadvayaṃ anuvattamānaṃ katvā vuttaṃ “vāsanābhāgiya”nti. Sīlavantehīti sīlavantādīhi puggalehi. Pakatisīlantiādi yehi samannāgatā, te puggalā. Tesaṃ dassanena puggalānaṃ upalakkhaṇaṃ. Atha vā dhammādhiṭṭhānaṃ pakatisīlādivasena, sattādhiṭṭhānaṃ pakatisīlavantādivasena veditabbanti imassa nayassa dassanatthaṃ “sīlavantehi niddisitabba”nti vatvā “pakatisīla”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Taṃ pakatisīlādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ eva gahaṇaṃ nidassanamattaṃ, pattidānaabbhanumodanadhammassavanadesanādiṭṭhijukammādīnampi cettha sambhavato. Tesampi vā ettheva saṅgahetvā dassanatthaṃ “pañcā”ti vuttaṃ.

'A discourse pertaining to dispositions' means a worldly discourse founded on beings is a discourse pertaining to dispositions. For a worldly discourse founded on beings is a discourse pertaining to defilement, indicated by persons of lustful temperament. Here, having let the two terms 'worldly' and 'founded on beings' carry over, 'pertaining to dispositions' is stated. 'By the virtuous' means by persons who are virtuous and so on. 'Natural virtue,' etc., are the qualities with which those persons are endowed; by showing these, the persons are indicated. Alternatively, to show the following method—that a discourse founded on phenomena should be understood by way of natural virtue, etc., while a discourse founded on beings should be understood by way of those endowed with natural virtue, etc.—having said 'to be indicated by the virtuous,' 'natural virtue,' etc., was stated. The taking up of just the five beginning with natural virtue is merely an illustration, since dedication of merit, rejoicing in merit, hearing the Dhamma, teaching the Dhamma, the straightening of one's views, etc., are also possible here. Or, to show that these too are included right here, it is said 'five.'

Tattha [V 0.0388] pakatisīlanti sampattaviratisīlaṃ. Cittappasādoti kammaphalasaddhā ratanattayasaddhā ca. Ñāṇaṃ paññāya niddisitabbanti yasmiṃ sutte paññā āgatā, taṃ suttaṃ ñāṇanti niddisitabbaṃ. Na kevalaṃ paññāpariyāyeneva, atha kho paññindriyādipariyāyenapi yattha paññā āgatā, taṃ suttaṃ ñāṇanti niddisitabbanti dassetuṃ “paññindriyenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassattho – heṭṭhā vutto eva. Yaṃ vā panātiādīsu yaṃ vā aññaṃ kiñci paññāya adhivacanaṃ. Sabbaṃ taṃ yattha katthaci sutte āgataṃ, taṃ suttaṃ ñāṇanti niddisitabbanti attho.

Here, 'natural virtue' means virtue consisting of restraint when the occasion arises. 'Clarity of mind' means faith in kamma and its fruit and faith in the Triple Gem. '"Knowledge" should be indicated by wisdom' means that in whatever discourse wisdom is found, that discourse should be indicated as 'knowledge.' To show that not only by the expression 'wisdom' alone, but also by expressions such as the faculty of wisdom, etc., wherever wisdom is found, that discourse should be indicated as 'knowledge,' it is said 'by the faculty of wisdom,' etc. Its meaning has already been stated below. In the phrases beginning 'Or whatever else...,' whatever other designation for wisdom there is—all of that, wherever it occurs in any discourse, that discourse should be indicated as 'knowledge.' This is the meaning.

Ajjhattikabāhirehīti [M 0.0274] yasmiṃ sutte ajjhattikāni āyatanāni, bāhirāni ca āyatanāni āgatāni, taṃ suttaṃ tehi āyatanehi ñāṇaṃ ñeyyanti niddisitabbaṃ. Paññāpi ārammaṇabhūtā ñeyyanti ñeyyato visuṃ katvā paññā vuttā. Tathā hi paññā ñāṇantarassa ārammaṇanti katthaci sutte ñeyyabhāvenapi vuccati. Yaṃ kiñci ārammaṇabhūtanti yaṃ kiñci ñāṇassa visayabhūtaṃ rūpādi. Ajjhattikaṃ vā bāhiraṃ vāti vā-saddena oḷārikādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Sabbaṃ taṃ saṅkhatena asaṅkhatena cāti sabbaṃ taṃ yathāsambhavaṃ saṅkhatabhāvena asaṅkhatabhāvena ca ñeyyanti niddisitabbaṃ. Ñeyyadhammavasena hi ñeyyasuttaṃ ñeyyanti vuccatīti.

By 'internal and external': In any sutta where the internal and external sense bases are mentioned, that sutta should be indicated as 'knowable' by means of those sense bases. Wisdom, too, being an object, is knowable; thus, wisdom is mentioned separately from other knowable things. For indeed, in some suttas, wisdom is called something to be known because it is an object of another kind of knowledge. 'Whatever is an object' means whatever is the domain of knowledge, such as form and so forth. In 'internal or external,' the word 'or' includes the coarse and so on. 'All that, by the conditioned and the unconditioned' means all that, as is appropriate, should be indicated as something to be known by way of its conditioned state and its unconditioned state. For a sutta about the knowable is called 'knowable' by way of knowable phenomena.

Yaṃ vā pana kiñci bhagavā aññataravacanaṃ bhāsatīti lokiyalokuttarādisuttesu ekasmiṃ sutte dve. Tesu yaṃ vā pana kiñci aññataravacanaṃ ekasseva kathanaṃ bhāsati niddisati. Sabbaṃ taṃ yathāniddiṭṭhaṃ dhārayitabbanti taṃ yathā sabbaṃ suttaṃ lokiyādīsu yadi aññataravasena, atha ubhayavasena yathā yathā niddiṭṭhaṃ, tathā tathā gahetabbaṃ, taṃ taṃ padhānabhāvena niddisitabbanti attho.

Regarding 'Or whatever particular expression the Blessed One speaks': In suttas that are worldly, supramundane, etc., in one sutta there may be two kinds. Among these, 'whatever particular expression' he speaks or indicates is the statement of just one of them. 'All of that should be retained as it has been indicated' means this: however the entire sutta—among the worldly, etc.—is indicated, whether by way of one kind or by way of both kinds, it should be grasped in just that way. This means it should be indicated according to what is predominant.

Kilesasahitaññeva kammaṃ vipākassa hetu, na itaranti vuttaṃ “duvidho hetu yañca kammaṃ ye ca kilesā”ti. Samudayo kilesāti ettha “samudayo”ti etena samudayapakkhiyā vuttā. “Kilesā”ti ca kilesavanto, saṃkiliṭṭhāti attho. Yaṃ dissatīti yaṃ yaṃ dissati. Tāsu tāsu bhūmīsūti puthujjanabhūmiādīsu. Kappiyānulomenāti kappiyena ca kappiyānulomena ca. Tattha kappiyaṃ pāḷiyaṃ sarūpato vuttaṃ, kappiyānulomaṃ mahāpadesavasena nayato dassitaṃ. Paṭikkhittakāraṇenāti yena kāraṇena bhagavatā yaṃ paṭikkhittaṃ, tena kāraṇena taṃ niddisitabbaṃ. Ekantena sarāgādisaṃvattanameva hi bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ, taṃ sarāgāya saṃvattanādikāraṇena niddisitabbaṃ[V 0.0389]. Dhammassāti asaṅkhatadhammassa. Ariyadhammānanti maggaphaladhammānaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

Only kamma accompanied by defilements is the cause of result, not the other; therefore it is said: 'There are two kinds of causes: kamma and defilements.' Here, in 'origin is defilements,' by the word 'origin' are meant things belonging to the side of origin. And 'defilements' means things possessing defilements, that is, defiled things. 'Whatever is seen' means whatever is seen. 'In those various states' refers to the state of ordinary people and so on. 'In accordance with what is allowable' means both by what is allowable and by what conforms to what is allowable. Therein, what is allowable is stated in the Pāli in its own form, while what conforms to what is allowable is shown by way of method based on the great authorities. 'By the reason for rejection' means: by whatever reason the Blessed One has rejected something, by that reason it should be indicated. For the Blessed One has rejected only what entirely leads to passion and so forth; that should be indicated by the reason that it leads to passion and the like. 'Of the Dhamma' refers to the unconditioned Dhamma. 'Of noble Dhammas' means the Dhammas of the paths and fruits. The rest is easily understood.

Ettha ca yathā saṃkilesabhāgiyādīnaṃ aññamaññaṃ saṃsaggato anekavidho paṭṭhānabhedo icchito, evaṃ lokiyasattādhiṭṭhānādisaṃsaggatopi anekavidho paṭṭhānabhedo sambhavati. Pāḷiyaṃ pana ubhayatthāpi ekadesadassanavasena āgatattā nayadassananti veditabbaṃ. Sakkā hi iminā [M 0.0275] nayena viññunā te niddhāretunti. Yathā ca saṃkilesabhāgiyādīnaṃ lokiyādīnañca visuṃ visuṃ saṃsaggabhedavasena ayaṃ paṭṭhānabhedo anekavidho labbhati, evaṃ ubhayesampi saṃsaggavasena ayaṃ nayo yathārahaṃ labbhateva. Labbhati hi lokiyaṃ suttaṃ kiñci saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ, kiñci vāsanābhāgiyaṃ. Tathā lokuttaraṃ suttaṃ kiñci nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ, kiñci asekkhabhāgiyanti. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

And here, just as a manifold division of conditional relations is intended through the mutual intermingling of discourses pertaining to defilement, etc., so too, a manifold division of conditional relations is possible through the intermingling of worldly discourses, discourses founded on beings, etc. In the Pāli, however, since it is presented in both cases by way of showing only a portion, it should be understood as an exposition of a method. For by this method, a wise person is able to determine them. And just as this manifold division of conditional relations is obtained by way of the various interminglings of discourses pertaining to defilement, etc., and worldly discourses, etc., separately, so too, this method is appropriately obtained by way of the intermingling of both. For a worldly sutta is found that is partly pertaining to defilement and partly pertaining to dispositions. Similarly, a supramundane sutta is found that is partly pertaining to penetration and partly pertaining to the non-learner. This same method applies to the remaining cases as well.

Evaṃ soḷasavidhe paṭṭhāne aṭṭhavīsatividhaṃ paṭṭhānaṃ pakkhipitvā, aṭṭhavīsatividhe ca paṭṭhāne soḷasavidhaṃ pakkhipitvā yathārahaṃ dukatikādibhedena sambhavato paṭṭhānavibhāgo veditabbo, so ca kho tīsu piṭakesu labbhamānassa suttapadassa vasena. Yasmā pana tāni tāni suttapadāni udāharaṇavasena niddhāretvā imasmiṃ atthe vitthāriyamāne atipapañco hoti, atibhāriyā ca nettisaṃvaṇṇanā, sakkā ca iminā nayena viññunā ayamattho viññātuṃ, tasmā na taṃ vitthārayimha. Teneva hi pāḷiyaṃ aññamaññasaṃsaggavasena paṭṭhānavibhāgo ekadeseneva dassito, na nippadesatoti.

Thus, having included the twenty-eightfold paṭṭhāna in the sixteenfold paṭṭhāna, and having included the sixteenfold paṭṭhāna in the twenty-eightfold paṭṭhāna, the division of the paṭṭhāna of the teaching should be understood as it occurs appropriately by way of the divisions beginning with dyads and triads. And this should be understood by way of the sutta terms found in the three Piṭakas. However, since, when this meaning is elaborated upon by citing those various sutta terms by way of example, it becomes an excessive proliferation, and the Netti commentary becomes too burdensome, and since it is possible for a wise person to understand this meaning by this method, therefore we have not elaborated on that meaning. For that very reason, in the Pāḷi, the division of the paṭṭhāna is shown only in part by way of mutual intermingling; it is not shown exhaustively.

Sāsanapaṭṭhānavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Section on the Paṭṭhāna of the Teaching is finished.

Nigamanakathā

Conclusion

Ettāvatā [V 0.0390] ca –

By this much—

Hāre naye ca paṭṭhāne, suvisuddhavinicchayaṃ;

Vibhajanto navaṅgassa, sāsanassatthavaṇṇanaṃ.

Wishing to analyze the Hāras, the Nayas, and the Paṭṭhānas, which have an extremely pure analysis, and which are an explanation of the meaning of the nine-factored Dispensation,

Nettippakaraṇaṃ dhīro, gambhīraṃ nipuṇañca yaṃ;

Adesayi mahāthero, mahākaccāyano vasī.

the wise one, the master, the great elder named Mahākaccāyana, taught that Nettipakaraṇa, which is profound and subtle.

Saddhammāvataraṭṭhāne, paṭṭane nāgasavhaye;

Dhammāsokamahārāja-vihāre vasatā mayā.

By me, residing in the monastery of the great king Dhammāsoka, in the port city named Nāgasa, a place for the descent of the good Dhamma,

Ciraṭṭhitatthaṃ yā tassa, āraddhā atthavaṇṇanā;

Udāharaṇasuttānaṃ, lakkhaṇānañca sabbaso.

that commentary on the meaning of that Nettipakaraṇa, which explains the meaning of all the example suttas and the characteristic suttas, was undertaken for the sake of its long endurance.

Atthaṃ [M 0.0276] pakāsayantī sā, anākulavinicchayā;

Samattā sattavīsāya, pāḷiyā bhāṇavārato.

That commentary, explaining the meaning with unconfused analysis, is completed in twenty-seven recitation sections by way of the Pāḷi.

Iti taṃ saṅkharontena, yaṃ taṃ adhigataṃ mayā;

Puññaṃ tassānubhāvena, lokanāthassa sāsanaṃ.

Thus, by the power of whatever merit has been acquired by me in composing that commentary,

Ogāhetvā visuddhāya, sīlādipaṭipattiyā;

Sabbepi dehino hontu, vimuttirasabhāgino.

may all embodied beings, having plunged into the Dispensation of the Lord of the World with the pure practice beginning with virtue, become partakers of the taste of liberation.

Ciraṃ [V 0.0391] tiṭṭhatu lokasmiṃ, sammāsambuddhasāsanaṃ;

Tasmiṃ sagāravā niccaṃ, hontu sabbepi pāṇino.

May the Dispensation of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One long endure in the world; may all living beings always be reverential towards it.

Sammā vassatu kālena, devopi jagatīpati;

Saddhammanirato lokaṃ, dhammeneva pasāsatūti.

May the deva rain rightly in due season; may the lord of the earth also, delighting in the good Dhamma, rule the world only in accordance with the Dhamma.

Iti badaratitthavihāravāsinā ācariyadhammapālena katā

Thus, composed by the teacher, the elder Dhammapāla, a resident of the Badaratittha Monastery,

Nettippakaraṇassa atthasaṃvaṇṇanā samattāti.

the Explanation of the Meaning of the Nettipakaraṇa is completed.

Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Nettipakaraṇa is finished.
